Some days the dream and your ordinary life look far apart, and people tell you to be realistic. Keep it anyway, because it is there to lift you.

Believe in the dream, and let go of what it should look like. It never arrives the way it first appeared in your head. Give it some structure to work through, and it starts to take form. What you have to give is your heart more than any picture. Leave it open, and it sets the people around you alight.
fields.iching:
Things are going well, and they are going well because the parts of your life are meeting. What you hope for and what is in front of you line up. The people above you and the people below you want the same thing. This time came after a stretch of careful steps, and it is a season you are passing through.

It asks you to use what you have to keep things moving. Spend your means to hold the meeting open, and make room for the people on either side of you. Every level road has a slope ahead, so the season will turn. Some good times are won with strength, and some are kept with gentleness. This one is kept with gentleness, and sharing what comes is how it lasts.

In the body this is the belly placed over the head. Let what you feel toward people lead, and let your thinking follow. Earth over Heaven is the hexagram of a good season in your life. Heaven is the drive in you that keeps going and does not tire. Earth is the part of you that is easy to meet and lets things grow. The drive sits inside and the ease outside, because you can be strong within and still gentle with people. This hexagram has long been read as heaven and earth coming together. When the people above and the people below want the same thing, the work moves without a fight. It is also the first month of spring, so what you start now has half a year to grow. Your life goes well when your strength meets the world softly. Peace
fields.gene_keys:
Obscurity Idealism Light Idealism is a mind that plays with the pictures that come to it. Once you start to trust them, they arrive in a flood, and some of them are huge. For an afternoon you may feel you are someone great from history. None of it is you. Each picture is moving through you, and you can enjoy it without becoming it. Only the present is safe, because the present is the one thing you cannot turn into a character.

Held that way, the pictures keep moving. A castle you were shown can turn out to stand for a way of living in fellowship. These pictures are old memories, far older than you, on their way into the world. First you have to find out which dreams are truly yours. Obscurity is a haze between you and what is in front of you. You look at your beliefs about a thing and call it seeing. Most of what people take for the world is a dim version of it, seen through a narrow band of light. Inside the haze, belief feels like knowing. It loves a system, a teacher or a method that promises to lift the haze for you. A system can carry you across, the way a raft carries you over a river, and then you have to step off.

The haze is made of pictures you pushed away. They rise from the side of you that thinks in images rather than words. They come faster than you can sort, and they do not seem to make sense. So you put them out of sight, where they turn into secret daydreams and hidden wishes. The ones you avoid hardest keep finding you, often in the face of the person you love. Light begins as one point in a dark sky: a single moment when your thoughts stop and you are simply aware. Then another comes, and another, while you wash the dishes or wait at a red light. In time there is more light than dark, and the dark patches open from inside. At the end the pictures fuse into one image of everything you fear and love. You sit face to face with it until nothing of you stands apart. Then a clear light shows through every form, and no one can hide or pretend. It is found only by going down into the dark. The world looks the way it did to you as a child, before good and evil divided it.
fields.human_design: Ideas Gate 11 is the gate of ideas, and it fills you with more of them than you know what to do with. It presses you to sort them, as if each one is a job to do. Most are not yours to act on. You come up with ideas for other people, and your part is to hold each one until the right person or moment appears. The few that are yours, you guard, because others will take them and sell them. When the pressure wins, you try to force every idea into being and wear yourself out. The question this gate keeps asking is what if, and it is happy to let the answer wait.
fields.tarot: This energy sees how things could be, and it belongs to a family of four, the Ring of Light. UL 5, The Space Between Time, is the answer you wait for. UL 9, Ease in This, is the small step you keep taking. UL 26, Lighter Than a Feather, is your knack for getting a thing done unseen. This one is the picture that shows you where to walk. Five of the tarot's major cards, its Arcana, come through the ring and the two trigrams.
fields.body:
The pituitary is given this energy because a picture in you has to reach the rest of you. The gland sits deep behind the bridge of your nose, about the size of a pea. It does almost none of the body's work itself. Nearly everything it releases is a message to another gland, and the whole body answers. That is what a picture does in you: it is seen behind your eyes, and it moves you from there.

The nerves from your two eyes cross just above it, so everything you look at passes over it on the way to becoming sight. Close your eyes and put a finger on the bridge of your nose. The crossing lies straight back from there, and the gland hangs just under it. How tall you grew was set by this small gland while you slept. The pictures in you have a chemistry, and one substance in it is threonine. Your body cannot make it, so it comes from food such as milk and cheese. Light reaches your eyes, and further back in your head it becomes the images you imagine. This substance belongs to that passage, from light to picture. When a haze sits between you and what you see, it sits there, between the light and how your mind reads it.

You share this chemistry with three other energies, each a different way you take in light. Much of what you eat of it goes to renew the slippery lining of your gut, where no light ever reaches.

fields.essence: Someone is talking to you, and under their words you can hear whether they mean them. That is your heart at work, telling the real from the fake before you can say why. What you can fall in love with, you trust. When you speak from your heart, people hear what you feel, and it stirs them.
fields.glance:
Someone is talking to you, and under their words you can hear whether they mean them. That is your heart at work, telling the real from the fake before you can say why. What you can fall in love with, you trust. When you speak from your heart, people hear what you feel, and it stirs them.

There are stretches when you let people in a little at a time and keep the rest back. Turn the same honesty on yourself and you will find a fear under it, that someone could take something from you. Nobody can take it, because what is pure in your heart is out of anyone's reach. The feelings you kept out rise and fall again without drowning you.

So let people in, and the world with them. Your heart opens a petal at a time, and each one that opens leaves you freer. The aloneness you have been looking for turns out to be your own heart. From there you can love without holding anything back.
fields.iching:
Nothing is getting through. What you say is not heard, you reach out and no help comes, and the people who should meet you have turned away. The ones who flatter get ahead, and the ones with something real to give step back. This is a season, the end of summer, when the growing has stopped. No one can change it, and none of it is your fault.

Do not push against it. Draw in, and spend little, of your money and of yourself. Turn down the pay and the praise this time offers, because taking them ties you to it. Keep to the few who are like you. Keep what you are worth inside, where no one can make a show of it. Whatever others do, do not let it wear away your own honesty. Learn what you can while you wait, so the hard time is not wasted.

You may feel it as a tightness in the throat and an unease in the chest. Sit with it and keep your word. This time turns, as every season does. Heaven over Earth is the hexagram of a time when nothing passes between you and the people around you. Heaven is the strength in you that stands firm. Earth is the softness in you that takes things in. Here the strength is on the outside and the softness is hidden within, so you look steady while nothing reaches you. This hexagram has long been read as heaven and earth drawing apart. A face kept firm over a heart kept shut is that drawing apart in a person. Around you, the small come forward and the worthy step back. You keep what you are worth inside until the time turns. Standstill
fields.gene_keys:
Vanity Discrimination Purity Discrimination is the urge to be better, turned into art. A fake reaches you as a discomfort in the body, from a person with a hidden aim or a song with nothing behind it. Nobody selling a dream can take you in. You know which food and which people are good for you. It sets you apart, because it cannot sit near a compromise.

What it is for is falling in love, the human kind, with all its drama and its danger. You are moved by feeling all your life, and you are here to pass the feeling on. Enter the drama without fear and let it run through you. In time you stop watching love from the side and become it. Vanity is the quiet love of being separate, of being the one who is different. It needs no audience, which is what sets it apart from pride. It hides in what you leave unsaid as easily as in what you say. The finer you become, the finer it becomes, until you feel a little purer than the people around you. Your mind is sharp enough to find the reason each person falls short. On the surface you are calm and collected. Underneath, feeling runs hot, and being loved can frighten you more than being alone.

You cannot think your way out of it, because the thought that you are getting over it is more of the same. As long as you feel yourself to be separate, it keeps pace with you. It lets go late, and all at once. Purity is a heart with nothing on it, and it lies under everything else in everyone. Lower down, you love yourself as someone set apart. Here, what is highest in you falls in love with you, and the two are one love. Lock such a person up and their love goes on. Even the worst person has this at the centre, so there is no evil, only thicker and thinner layers over it.

To arrive here you give up everything you gained. You come out like a child, still human, with a voice past words. Most who live it live plain lives, unseen, and remind whoever meets them that this can exist in a person. The moment you see anything as bad, it is gone.
fields.human_design:
Caution Gate 12 is the drive to put what you feel into words, held by a fine sense of when. You speak when you are moved to, not because a silence needs filling. You take longer than most to answer, because the answer has to come up from what you feel. When the words come easily, the time is right. When they will not come, wait. Forced out early, they fall flat and leave you doubting yourself.

People who like speed may read your pauses as shyness, and your silence when you are overwhelmed as coldness. The shyness is only the timing. You are shy and bold by turns, and when you do speak, your words carry weight.
fields.tarot: This energy is the last thing in you to let go, and that is its test. It belongs to a family of three, the Ring of Trials, three tests on the way to knowing yourself. First comes forgetting who you are, in UL 33, Echos of Time. Then comes being pulled about by your senses, in UL 56, Infinite Journey. This one is the last test, the belief that you are separate. Inside the three it forms its own ring, the Ring of Secrets, and what you keep hidden there opens only when your heart does. Five major tarot cards arrive through the ring and the two trigrams, each one a way you guard or open your heart.
fields.body:
Swallowing is the reason this energy is given to the throat. Each time you swallow, your voice box lifts and a small flap folds down over it. Inside it, the two folds that make your voice close tight. For about a second your breath stops while what you swallowed passes behind. It happens several hundred times a day: everything in you goes still so that one thing can pass. When you laugh or cry, the rhythm of your breath changes, and your chemistry changes with it.

Put a finger on the ridge at the front of your throat and swallow. It rises under your finger, and for that second no breath comes. The old story calls it the apple caught in Adam's throat, the place where you get stuck on your own words. No substance in your body answers to this energy. Your body builds itself by reading a long written message, and three of the words in it name nothing. Where the reading reaches one, nothing more is added. The piece being made is let go whole. This energy carries that stop into your life. It is a passage from one way of being to another. Your hold on your own past ends, and you come out changed for good. At its far end the sense of being separate ends too, and you are taken into life itself.

Two other energies in you carry the same stop, and of the three this is the last.

fields.essence: When someone starts telling you what they have kept to themselves for years, you go quiet and listen with all of you. Your whole body takes in what they mean and cannot say. You need time for this, and often a little distance. People sense it, and trust you before they know why.
fields.glance:
When someone starts telling you what they have kept to themselves for years, you go quiet and listen with all of you. Your whole body takes in what they mean and cannot say. You need time for this, and often a little distance. People sense it, and trust you before they know why.

Some days everything you hear sounds heavy, your own life included. Watch the heavy feeling without arguing with it, and it loses its hold.

Let your heart speak before your thoughts do, and give it quiet to speak in. Listen to your own past like that, and it starts to teach you. What kept repeating becomes something you learned from. The more you listen, the more strangers feel like your own people.
fields.iching:
You are among people who are not your family or your usual crowd, out in the open, and something has to hold you together. Blood will not do it here, and neither will habit. What holds you is an aim you all share, bigger than any one of you. Keep your own gain out of it. A group gathered for one person's profit breaks at the first strain. A group gathered for everyone's good can take on something hard together.

Be the first to give. Help the others toward what they want, and in time you find your own aim reached along the way. Do not leave a friend to walk home alone at night.

Your eyes do the work here. Look at each face as it is, without hurry, and keep your hands open. A company holds when every person in it has been seen. Heaven over Fire is the hexagram of people joined by one aim. Fire is the clear sight in you that sees each person as they are. Heaven is the aim in you that keeps going, the same from every side. The aim sits above the sight because people who see each other clearly still need something to face together. This hexagram has long been read as fire climbing toward the sky. People who share an aim rise together, and each can still be seen. It also asks you to tell one kind of thing from another. You belong with the people you see clearly and walk the same way with. Fellowship
fields.gene_keys:
Discord Discernment Empathy Discernment starts when you listen to yourself. The wants still run through your body, and you cannot stop them. Now something in you watches them go by and is not carried off. You see how much of your view of other people was your own mood. Your agenda comes into the light, where you can set it down. From there you can hear other people properly for the first time.

Then your past changes. What looked like a run of accidents shows a pattern, the same few stories every culture tells, and you are living one of them. That brings a hope you feel in your belly. The deeper you listen, the more of what you hear is love. Discord is hearing only one band of what is going on. An old part of you listens for danger, and on its days the world comes in as bad news, one crisis after another. It does not feel like a mood. It feels like being realistic. Every generation says it the same way: things were simpler once, and people cared more. Good news comes too, and you hear it and cannot believe it. How could so many people be wrong, and only you and a few others be right?

Under it is distrust, of people and then of life itself, as if the story were bound to end badly. Nobody chooses to hear this way. There is too much noise in the head and too much armour round the heart. Under the noise, what you have forgotten is love. Empathy is being inside another person, not beside them. Sympathy needs two people. Empathy needs one, and the one is not you. It is a kind of death: the one who was listening goes. What is left is the listening itself, and it can take in any living thing from the inside. First there is a fear to cross, the cold of feeling cut off from everything alive.

To sit with someone who lives here is to be healed by being heard. Every fear you have comes up and is loved until it is gone. You stop being a point and become a place, with every creature in it.
fields.human_design:
Narrative Gate 13 is the drive to take in what has been lived, yours and other people's, and keep it until it means something. You give people direction just by listening to them with respect. What they confide is theirs, and keeping it private is part of this drive.

The cost is weight. Other people's stories stay with you, and so does your own past. You can end up living there, telling the old hurt until it is who you are. There can be so much room for others that none is left for you. The story you tell about yourself sets the direction of your life. You can tell it again, truer, on any day you choose.
fields.tarot: This energy listens to the past, and desire is loud enough to drown it out. It belongs to a family of two, the Ring of Purification. The other is UL 30, Sparking the Blaze, the desire that heats a life from inside. Your listening and that desire are weighed against each other, and the ring is named for what the weighing does to both. Open it when wanting keeps winning over what you already know. Five of the tarot's major cards show sides of this energy you may know in yourself.
fields.body:
The flinch is the reason this energy is given to the amygdala. The amygdala is two clusters of nerve cells the size of almonds, one deep in each side of your head. It hears first: a rough copy of every sound and sight reaches it a moment before the thinking part of you has the whole. It keeps each memory with the feeling that came with it. A voice that once meant hurt is stored with the hurt still on it. A likeness alone can set your heart going before you know why. Someone speaks, and something in you has already answered. Real listening begins when you watch that answer instead of obeying it.

The next time a sudden sound makes you jump, notice that the jump comes before you know what it was. Put a fingertip just in front of the opening of your ear. A few centimetres straight in is the part of you that heard first. The heaviness you hear on a bad day has a chemistry in you, and it holds only while you believe it. One substance in that chemistry is glutamine. Your body makes it, mostly in the muscle, and bread is full of it. More of it floats loose in your blood than any other piece your proteins are built from.

It goes first to your gut. The cells lining your gut burn it before anything else, taking it from the blood as it passes. Your gut sorts what you eat: what feeds you is drawn out, and the rest is let go. Listening does the same with a day or a person, down in the belly, below thought. The desire that pulls against your listening runs on the same substance.

fields.essence: On the days you have more in you than you know what to do with, an appetite for the work you love takes hold. Your body is at the work before your mind has decided to start. You do it in your own manner, one nobody else could copy. What you bring in is more than you need, and it feeds the people around you.
fields.glance:
On the days you have more in you than you know what to do with, an appetite for the work you love takes hold. Your body is at the work before your mind has decided to start. You do it in your own manner, one nobody else could copy. What you bring in is more than you need, and it feeds the people around you.

This appetite fades when you settle, one small time after another, for work you do not want. Each time, something low in you tightens, and you feel a little worse. When you notice it, one choice a day that stays true to yourself is enough to turn it round.

Get clear on what you want your work to serve, even if that takes months. Then start, and let it build speed at its own pace. Work among people, and the right help finds its way to you. This is how the gifts you were born with, handed down through everyone before you, come into bloom.
fields.iching:
The harvest is in, and it is large. You have more than you need, and it came from years of steady work as much as from good fortune. The season is right, and for now everything you start goes well.

The danger now is not loss but pride. Plenty tempts you to believe you made it alone. Those who have a great deal should not let themselves feel full. Stay modest, and stay easy for people to reach. Stop what does harm, in yourself first, and let the good in you show. Offer the best of what you have to something larger than your own house.

The belly does the work now. Fill it and keep your mind empty. Take in all that has come without holding on to it in your thoughts. Stand the way a generous host stands, with plenty on the table and the door open. Fire over Heaven is the hexagram of having a great deal and using it well. Heaven is the strength in you that keeps working, day after day, without being asked. Fire is the clear sight in you that tells what is worth keeping from what is not. The clear sight sits on top because so much strength needs a goal to give it shape. This hexagram has long been read as the sun high in the sky. Like that sun, what you have does the most good when it goes out to everyone around you. What you have stays good for as long as you can see what it is for. Great Possession
fields.gene_keys:
Compromise Competence Bounteousness Competence is what someone who loves their work looks like while they do it. Nobody can teach it. It finds the quickest and simplest way past whatever is in the way. It has a style no one else could copy. When it meets a task it has never done, it learns it.

The fire sits in the belly, and it works by drawing rather than pushing. Your work goes like a saw pulled toward the belly: a finer cut for less effort than one shoved away. The heat of it spreads. It turns a small group into a team, all keen on the same thing. If you would rather work alone, look underneath the wish. Usually there is a fear of how large you could be. Settling for second best starts so young that most of us no longer notice we do it. The dream of being great that you had as a child was a real urge to excel. School taught most of us that work means boredom and effort, and by forty the dream has usually gone.

Each small surrender damps the fire in you a little more. Your spine droops, and your energy sinks with it. Not every give costs you. Staying home because someone you love is unwell costs nothing, since love made that choice. Work you dislike can cost nothing too, when it is a step toward your dream. What costs is doing what you do not want because others pressed you to. That becomes a habit, and what you were born with starts to leak away. Bounteousness begins as gratitude for a spark. The ember is tiny and easily lost, and you breathe on it in your hands until it holds. Fed, it grows into a flame and then a fire, until there is a sun inside you. A sun gives itself away all day and is filled again by the giving.

Nothing is taken anymore. Receiving is still here, and receiving only deepens the thanks. The more you give, the more you are given. What was plenty turns out to be fertility, moving through one life into many others.
fields.human_design: Power Skills Gate 14 is a surge low in your body that wants to produce. It drives you to bring in resources, money and the things a life runs on, and much of what it brings is meant for others. It does not run at a steady level. It pulses, strong for a stretch and then gone, and on the strong days you can outwork anyone. Without a direction it turns into restlessness, and people may call you greedy or unable to stop. Pointed at something you want, it becomes stamina.
fields.tarot: This energy pours what it has into work, and the spark behind it was there first. Its one sibling is UL 1, Earth's Breath, which carries creation out of nothing. Your plenty grows out of that creative spark. The spark of genius needs fanning, and freshness is what keeps it alight. Open it when the work you love has gone stale. Five of the tarot's major cards, its Arcana, arrive through the ring and the two trigrams.
fields.body:
The meal is the reason this energy is given to the small intestine. Several metres of it lie folded under your navel. It receives whatever you have eaten and turns it into what the rest of you can use. Its inside is folded, and the folds are covered in tiny fingers. So a tube you could close a hand around has a surface as large as a room's floor. Nearly everything that feeds you crosses that wall into your blood. It keeps nothing for itself, and it passes on what it cannot use.

After a meal more blood goes to it, which is part of why you feel warm and slow for an hour. Its lining is shed and grown again every few days, faster than any other part of you. Between meals a slow wave sweeps it clean, every hour and a half or so. The growl you call hunger is mostly that wave. The spark in what you are good at has a chemistry in you, and lysine is part of it. Your body cannot make it, so it has to come in from meat, eggs or beans. Grain alone leaves you short of it. A spark like yours is there from birth, and it has to be fanned before it becomes a fire. In your body, what fans it is what you eat.

On a long walk, hours after your last meal, you are running on stored fat. Lysine goes into the carrier that brings that fat out to be burned. That is the fire in you with something to feed.

fields.essence: It takes a quiet kind of courage to meet an ordinary day in full, with the same street and the same people. That is where your magnetism lives. It grows as you slow down to the pace of growing things. Without any effort from you, it draws people and what you need. You do the plain work well and let the credit go, and people feel something near you that they cannot name.
fields.glance:
It takes a quiet kind of courage to meet an ordinary day in full, with the same street and the same people. That is where your magnetism lives. It grows as you slow down to the pace of growing things. Without any effort from you, it draws people and what you need. You do the plain work well and let the credit go, and people feel something near you that they cannot name.

Some days go grey and flat, with nothing wrong in them, and you fear that every day will be like this one. Running from it into something new does not help, and neither does sinking into it. Let the grey all the way in, and at some depth it fills with life again.

Trust your own rhythm, slow for a stretch and then fast. Welcome everyone who comes, the drab and the bright alike. Lived this way, an ordinary day turns out to be full.
fields.iching:
You can do more than the people around you know, and this is a time to carry it low. Do the work in full and let the credit go. Treat the people around you as your equals, and share the plain work with them. People resent whoever is full of themselves, and they help whoever keeps low. Carried this way, every step turns out well, from the first to the last.

Weigh what is in front of you. Take some away where there is too much. Add where there is too little, and count your own share too. Then see the thing through, because starting is easy and finishing is the hard part. Keeping low is not the same as being weak. When someone threatens what is fair, stand up for it without taking it personally.

Your body does this through your hands, which work without anyone watching them. Stand with your weight low and your hands open, with nothing to prove. Earth over Mountain is the hexagram of a real strength carried low. Mountain is what is solid in you, the weight of what you can do. Earth is the plain, yielding side you show to people. The yielding side sits on top because people resent a strength that is shown off, and they help one that is kept low. This hexagram has long been read as a mountain inside the earth. Someone who looks ordinary can have a mountain of strength under the surface. You go furthest when you carry your strength without showing it off. Modesty
fields.gene_keys:
Dullness Magnetism Florescence Magnetism is a pull that grows as you slow down to the pace of the earth. The earth is never in a hurry: leave a city alone for a thousand years and it turns back into forest. The closer you come to that pace, the more you draw people and what you need. This is not charisma, which spills over the surface of a person. It comes from far below, and it may never show in your manner. People feel something around you that they cannot put a name to.

What you feared was draining your life turns out to feed it, the way an empty jar turns out to be full. Your love reaches people at every level of life, the grey ones included. Loving everyone does not mean liking them. It means you can feel what a person is and find something in them worth loving. The grey of the low days becomes colour here. A grey day with nothing wrong in it is where this energy sinks lowest. The colour goes out of things. Underneath runs a fear that tomorrow will be the same, and every day after it. That is the fear of an ordinary life. Anger is not dull, and grief is not dull. Dullness is the dead middle, with no charge either way. On a cloudy morning your body changes a little, as everyone's does, and the dullness comes from how you take that change.

A dog can sit on a doorstep for a month and never be bored. Only a person can find a day dull, because only a person has an attitude toward it. Stuck in your head, you reach for anything to fill the day. Stuck in your feelings, you sink, and your energy sinks with you. No trick takes the feeling away. Let the grey in all the way, and at some depth it stops being dull. Florescence is a whole tree bursting into flower at once, in every direction. It comes when the seeking in you finally comes to rest. No effort brings it, and nothing can hurry it. People know it when they see it in someone.

Then the fruit falls back to the ground, and the flowering comes back into ordinary life. The ones it happens to come down off the mountain and become entirely ordinary, even a little strange. They may let you think they are weak or flawed, just to stay close to you. The holiest people are the gardeners, because they know that everything comes at its proper time. You learn the same, and everything in you flowers in the end.
fields.human_design: Extremes Gate 15 is the pressure to live by your own rhythm, and that rhythm swings. You may work hard for weeks and then rest. You may spend time with people and then need to be alone. This is not balance. It is a love of the whole range of life, with room for every kind of person in it. From outside, the swings can look like you cannot follow through. Forced into fixed daily habits, the rhythm jams. Then you blame yourself for keeping hours that are not yours. You may also swing between giving everything away and keeping everything for yourself. Set limits around a stretch of work, go in fully while it lasts, and rest in between. Share from the heart without giving your heart away.
fields.tarot: This energy is where seeking comes to rest. It belongs to a family of six, the Ring of Seeking, and each one presses you to look for something. UL 39, Nobel Spark, carries the push to break through. UL 52, Timeless Blossom, carries the wish for complete rest. UL 53, Creation Oscillation, carries the urge to start something new. UL 54, Everlasting Bounty, carries the drive to rise. UL 58, Rhythm of Life, carries joy. This one is where the looking ends. Four of the tarot's major cards reach this one, and the Hermit comes by two roads.
fields.body:
The liver holds this energy in your body, and the reason is direction. It keeps your blood and your energy moving freely, and it sends blood wherever you need it. It also gives a life its plan and the way it faces. When it moves freely, you go through a day at your own pace and in your own direction.

After a meal, the liver stores the sugar your blood does not need yet. Between meals it lets it out a little at a time. So your blood stays at one level, whether you ate an hour ago or ten. Go half a day without food and you keep going, because the liver is paying out what it put by. Whatever pace your day takes, fast or slow, it keeps you level underneath. The pressure in you to seek has a substance, and the substance is serine. It is one of the twenty small pieces every protein in you is built from. Your body makes it from what it is already burning, so you never have to eat it. The same substance runs through this energy's kin, and each of them presses you to seek something different.

Here is where that seeking finally comes to an end. All your struggles and your highest moments are written into this chemistry. The seeking in you runs on something you make yourself, and in time it burns itself out.

fields.essence: Some mornings you wake up wanting to get to the thing you love. That is enthusiasm, and it says yes before you have thought it through. You begin before you feel ready, and you learn as you go. When you talk about it your voice lifts, and the people around you catch it.
fields.glance:
Some mornings you wake up wanting to get to the thing you love. That is enthusiasm, and it says yes before you have thought it through. You begin before you feel ready, and you learn as you go. When you talk about it your voice lifts, and the people around you catch it.

There are days when nothing seems worth getting up for, and your plans stay on the table. It feels like tiredness, and under it is a fear that caring will swamp you. Your heart cannot be overwhelmed; it only opens wider. Go and do one real thing, and the caring comes back with it.

Begin on the thing you most enjoy, and a surge of energy comes up in you. You stop bending your path to suit other people. Nobody else can take this first step for you. Once you are in it, your days fill with purpose and you are glad to get up.
fields.iching:
You have made ready, and the time to move has come. What you prepared in quiet is ready to come out, and the people around you are ready to follow. It is a good time to bring helpers in and set out together.

It asks you to prepare, then go without hesitating. Study the target before you let the arrow go, and once you have seen it, do not wait out the day. Move with the time, the way the sun and the moon keep their course and the seasons come when they should. Enjoy what comes to you, and keep some of it back for what comes after. The danger is on the far side of the joy, when pleasure turns into laziness and you forget the people who came with you.

Your feet are where the body feels this. Notice whether your weight has already shifted forward. Stand as you do just before you step off, ready and at ease. Thunder over Earth is the hexagram of getting ready and then moving. Thunder is the excitement in you that gets you on your feet. Earth is the quiet part of you that rests and makes ready. The excitement sits on top because it comes up out of what was stored below. This hexagram has long been read as thunder rising out of the ground in spring, waking a whole field. Your excitement wakes a room the same way. Its name has been read both as delight and as getting ready, and your delight lasts when you have prepared. When you are ready, your joy carries others with it. Enthusiasm
fields.gene_keys:
Indifference Versatility Mastery Versatility begins with caring about one thing enough to lose yourself in it. You pick up the instrument and give it years. It takes about seven for a skill to be written into your body, so that your hands know it without you. By then the skill has become a talent, and you no longer have to think about it.

Once you know one thing through and through, you find you can pick up almost anything. The same pattern runs under every art and every science, and that pattern is what you learned. The discipline that looked hard from outside is easy once your heart is warm. You move from painting to business with the same ease, and you waste nothing. You spot a child's talent early and put it where it can grow. Not caring feels like nothing much, and under it is fear. You live in the comfortable part of your life, the emails and the job, and your attention stays on what does not matter. You are full of plans, and they rarely get off the ground. The book or the business waits for a day with more time, though time is not the reason.

The instrument you were born to play sits in the corner. Picking it up would make you different from everyone who is not bothering either, and there is safety in numbers. You can build a clever life out of skills and methods while it stays there. Skill of that kind makes an expert. It never makes a master. Mastery is living well, and it has stopped being about skill. For years your heart opened, closed and opened again, and now it no longer needs to close. The person it happens to is ordinary. They are cheerful without pretending, they give because they want to, and they pass almost unnoticed. They may not be rich, and you can still see that they are prospering.

Here all learning ends, and there are no more levels to climb. The knowledge of how to play the hardest music is already in every person alive. At this height your enthusiasm is what the word first meant, to be filled with the breath of God. Nobody near you can stay indifferent to it.
fields.human_design:
Zest Gate 16 is the pull to leap at something you love and get good at it. It says yes before the details are in, dives to the bottom of a subject and wants to share what it can do. It masters by repetition, the way an instrument is learned, one pattern played until it is yours. Your passion for it tends to spread to whoever is listening.

When it is off, it presses in one of two ways. You may hold a skill back for years because it is not perfect yet. Or a leap that went wrong may have burned you, until your zest feels dangerous and you take no risks at all. Leaping with no map and no food makes you look unreliable. Your enthusiasm needs something to carry it, so pack what you need, then jump.
fields.tarot: This energy finds the one thing you do best, and it cannot prosper alone. It belongs to a family of two, the Ring of Prosperity. UL 45, Tribal Tapestry, gathers people around what there is and shares it out. This one brings the talent. Real wealth comes when people follow their own gift and work together. Five of the tarot's major cards come with this energy, and each is a stage of what it does in your life.
fields.body:
The parathyroid holds this energy in the body, and the reason is the store. These are four glands the size of grains of rice, tucked behind the thyroid, and together they weigh less than a paperclip. Every muscle that closes and every beat of your heart runs on calcium, and these four keep its level in your blood steady. When a meal falls short, they draw on a store you laid down over years, your bones. When the meal is enough, the bones are built back. A move that comes easily to you is drawing on years.

You cannot feel the glands, only find the place. Put a fingertip in the notch at the top of your breastbone, then move a thumb's width up, either side of the windpipe. Now close your hand into a fist. Every muscle in that fist closes on calcium those four grains keep level. Enthusiasm has a chemistry in you, and one substance in it is cysteine. Your body makes it for itself, but only from a piece it has to be fed. That piece comes from meat, eggs or beans. It is one of two pieces in you that carry sulphur, the smell of burning hair.

This chemistry belongs to finding the one thing you do better than anything else, and to the risk of being different that finding it takes. When you stop spending yourself on what does not matter, your body has more for that one thing. The further you go into it, the more the world comes to meet you halfway. You share this chemistry with the energy that gathers people, so your talent does best among others.

fields.essence: When something is only starting, you can often already see where it is heading. You watch one step lead to the next, and the pattern shows you what comes after. You feel it in your chest before your head can explain it. What you see can lift a conversation and help people imagine more than they thought possible.
fields.glance:
When something is only starting, you can often already see where it is heading. You watch one step lead to the next, and the pattern shows you what comes after. You feel it in your chest before your head can explain it. What you see can lift a conversation and help people imagine more than they thought possible.

The people around you may not be ready to hear it for years. Said too early, it only makes them push back, and you may start to doubt what you saw. Hold on to it, and the world catches up in its own time.

So hold what you see as a possibility and keep looking as things change. Share it when someone asks, and people will take it as help. Then you can see both sides of a question at once, and what you say points everyone in a better direction.
fields.iching:
This is a time of following. Someone goes ahead and others come after, and you may be on either side of it. People follow gladly or not at all. Push them and they pull away. Serve them and they come, and they stay. So whoever wants others behind them learns first to walk behind someone worth following. To get, you give first.

What it asks is care over what you follow. Following is only as good as what lies ahead of it. Behind what is right, it takes you a long way. Behind whatever is nearest or loudest, it turns on you. Follow the time as well: move while the day moves, and stop when it ends.

Your feet do this now, each step going where the last one led. Walk behind the one you trust, at their pace. When evening comes, go in and rest until morning. Lake over Thunder is the hexagram of following and being followed. Thunder is the drive in you to get up and move. Lake is the pleasure you take in the people around you. The movement sits below the pleasure because people come along gladly only when nobody is pushing them. This hexagram has long been read as thunder gone down into a lake at nightfall. The storm rests under the water until morning, the way you stop and go home when the day is done. It is also read as the strong one walking behind the weaker ones. You are followed once you have learned to follow. Following
fields.gene_keys:
Opinion Far-Sightedness Omniscience Far-sightedness is seeing both sides of a thing at once. With both eyes open the world has depth again. You take in the small workings of a thing along with the whole of it. This gift has work to do. It calls out an argument that shows one side and hides the other. You know a fixed view from the inside, so you do not fight it in anyone else or try to win them round. You doubt your own doubt as freely as anyone else's, so there is nothing to defend.

At first the view comes and goes. There is a moment when the whole is clear, then ordinary sight again. You need the plain days between, to bring what you saw into your life. Somewhere young you took a side, and you have been finding proof for it ever since. You have two eyes so that the world has depth, and a fixed view closes one of them. The seed goes in during your first seven years, before you have words for it. It comes up in your teens, when the mind looks for something solid to hold on to. It finds a flaw in people or in you, and builds a whole story around it. By the time you are grown, a small thing has become a mountain.

A view held that way has to be defended, and while you defend it you stop looking. Take something that bothers you and see whether a should is hidden in it, the feeling that things should not be like this. That feeling is the first refusal of how things are. Notice, too, that the view could change by tomorrow. That is how you know the view is not who you are. Omniscience is one eye that sees in every direction at once. There is no longer you on one side and the world on the other, so there is nothing to take sides about. It feels less like seeing and more like being seen through, with nobody in the way.

A falcon wears a hood on the falconer's glove and dozes. When the hood comes off it is awake at once, and its body moves the moment its eye finds a mark. At this height you are the same: you see, and you act in that moment without second-guessing. Nothing needs doing, and whatever you decide is already right.
fields.human_design:
Anticipation Gate 17 presses your mind to run ahead. It takes what has already happened, finds the pattern in it and follows the pattern forward to what could be. It often reaches further than other people think is possible. It wants order in a world that keeps surprising you.

The same pressure brings the urge to say it now. A view offered before anyone asked shuts a room that it could have opened. The other habit is doubt for its own sake, until a mind built to see what could go right sees only what could go wrong. So hold the view until someone asks, and keep it open to change. People change, and not everything in a life follows a pattern.
fields.tarot: This energy sees ahead, and that is one part of being human. It belongs to a family of six, the Ring of Humanity, which holds the story every life passes through. With UL 25, The Mysteries Play, you start out wounded. With UL 38, Inner Light Symphony, you fight your own shadows. Here you outgrow the limits of your mind. With UL 21, Beyond Binary, you give up control. With UL 10, Internal Treasure, you find yourself. With UL 51, Unshakable Arrival, you wake up. Five of the tarot's major cards, its Arcana, arrive through the ring and the two trigrams.
fields.body:
Your pituitary gland carries this energy, and the reason is your eyes. The nerves from your two eyes cross just above it, deep in the middle of your head. Everything you look at passes over it on its way to becoming sight. It does none of the seeing itself. Nearly everything it releases is word sent to another gland, to your thyroid or to the glands above your kidneys, and they do the work. A pea-sized gland sends word, and the whole of you answers.

How tall you grew was set by this gland, year by year, in what it released while you slept. Close your eyes and put a fingertip to the bridge of your nose. The crossing is straight back from there, deep in your head, and the gland hangs just beneath it. Your far sight has a chemistry, and one substance in it is arginine. It is one of the twenty pieces every protein in you is built from. Your body makes most of what it needs, and the rest comes from meat, eggs or a handful of nuts. It is written into you in six different ways, more than almost any other piece.

You share this chemistry with the other energies that make a person human. What people are still to become is folded into it, along with what you already are.

fields.essence: An instinct for what has gone wrong lives in you, and so does the wish to put it right. When something comes to you already spoiled, in a family or in a piece of work, you are the one who sees it. Once you start on it, you stay, and you keep making it a little better. Held well, this is integrity. You keep a high standard, and it shows in how you stand.
fields.glance:
An instinct for what has gone wrong lives in you, and so does the wish to put it right. When something comes to you already spoiled, in a family or in a piece of work, you are the one who sees it. Once you start on it, you stay, and you keep making it a little better. Held well, this is integrity. You keep a high standard, and it shows in how you stand.

At times the faults are all you can see, in the people nearest you and in yourself. Ask whether you would rather be right or happy. What bothers you most in someone else usually points to something in you that wants settling, so start there.

Treat the life around you as your own body, only greater. The more of it you care for as yours, the less personally you take it, and the lighter your days become. Mend what you can, one thing at a time. What was spoiled becomes sound again, steadier than it was before.
fields.iching:
Something has come to you already going bad. It went wrong in the hands of the people before you, and now it is in yours. The spoiling is not your fault. Setting it right is your work, and this is a good time for it, because what has gone bad can still be mended.

This time asks you to act, not to wait for things to sort themselves out. Before you start, look hard at how it went wrong. When you finish, look again at what your work has changed. Take up what the ones before you meant, and leave what they did. Stir up whatever has gone still, in yourself and in the people around you, and give them heart.

Bend your back to it. No one is ever fully ready to carry the work a family or a place leaves undone. Carrying it is how you grow into it. Mountain over Wind is the hexagram of setting right what was spoiled. Wind is the gentleness in you that finds its way in. Mountain is the part of you that holds still. The stillness sits above because that is how a family or a workplace spoils, when those in charge stop and everyone else goes along. This hexagram has long been read as wind blocked at a mountain's foot, where the air goes stale. A bowl left standing too long spoils, and the cure is to clean it and use it. The same spoiling, watched and stopped in time, makes rice wine. You can make good what went bad. Work on the Decayed
fields.gene_keys:
Judgement Integrity Perfection Integrity is a word builders use for how much load a structure can bear before it fails. In you it is physical, a steady core that shows in how you stand and move before you have said anything. Every animal has it without trying, which is why nothing in a forest judges. You were born with it too, and still you have to earn it. Once earned it stays, because it was your true nature all along.

The eye that found every flaw turns first on your own thinking, and clearing out old verdicts gives you back a clear head. From there you hold a high standard in all you do and ask it of others, from the heart, which is never cruel. You go against the grain calmly, leading by example. Part of you is in the game and part of you rests outside it, which is where the calm comes from. Having seen how a person is shaped young, you can help others finish growing up. The flaw is the first thing you see, and the mind that sees it was built that way. What goes wrong at this height is that you become your verdicts. Each one feels like who you are and makes you feel safe, so you defend it. Holding them that tightly makes you tense, and people feel the tension before they hear a single opinion. What you think about a thing hardly matters. How tightly you hold it does.

It usually sets in between fourteen and twenty-one. A young mind sees faults everywhere, in parents and teachers. It escapes them by freezing into one fixed view, usually borrowed from its friends. It feels like safety, and it stops the mind from growing. Much of a day's thinking stays there, in quiet complaints about the people nearest you and worry over money and health. Every complaint harms twice, the one it is about and the one who makes it. The world is perfect as it is, and now you can see it, the flaws included. The mind that judged goes quiet. The clearer it is that nothing needs mending, the more you mend until the day you die. The more good you do, the more you see could be done, and that restlessness is the work itself.

In anyone, even someone who seems wholly bad, you see only what is highest. Holding that sight lifts them. You could leave the world behind, and you stay. Your body belongs to the whole body of people, and no one is fully well until everyone is.
fields.human_design: Correction Gate 18 gives you an eye for what has gone out of line, the detail everyone else has stepped over. It arrives as an instinct, before any thought, and it is usually right. It is less about getting a thing perfect than about making it a little better, again and again. The hard part is timing. Offered before anyone asks, a correction is heard as criticism, and people push away the very thing that would help them. Then you are the one who feels judged. So wait until you are asked, and give it to bring more joy between people, never to prove you were right. It is worth knowing how it feels to be right and keep it to yourself.
fields.tarot: This energy shapes the mind between fourteen and twenty-one, when your views are formed. It belongs to a family of four called the Ring of Matter. Together they shape how soundly you grew in body, feeling and mind. UL 57, Flight of the Tao, carries the months before you were born. UL 46, Fountain of Light, carries your body in your first seven years. UL 48, Doorways of the Unknown, carries your feelings in the seven after. This one carries your mind. Five of the tarot's major cards, its Arcana, come to this energy through the ring and the two trigrams.
fields.body:
The lymph carries this energy in the body, and the reason is washing. All day your blood leaves water behind in the spaces between your cells, along with whatever the cells are done with. None of it is left there. A second set of vessels gathers it, two or three litres a day, and carries it through several hundred small filters. Anything wrong in it is met there, before the water goes back into your blood. Your body has no pump for it. It moves when you move, lifted by each step and each breath, and it pools while you sit.

The clear drop that beads on a graze before any blood comes is that same water. The word lymph means clear water, so you have already seen what it washes. The energy that puts things right has a substance in you, and the substance is alanine. It is one of the twenty small pieces every part of you is built from. Your body makes this one itself, from what the sugar in your blood becomes as it burns. There is more of it in you than of almost any other piece. The fears this energy carries lie deep in your body, in the defences that fight off what does not belong in you. Going through them, never around them, is what opens what is higher in you.

This substance is made from what already runs in your blood. You share it with three other energies, each carried by a different part of your growing up.

fields.essence: When you come close to someone, you can feel what they are missing before they say a word. That is sensitivity, and it lives in your skin as much as in your mind. You walk into a room and know where the warmth has gone out of it. It is a kind of touch, and it reaches animals as well as people.
fields.glance:
When you come close to someone, you can feel what they are missing before they say a word. That is sensitivity, and it lives in your skin as much as in your mind. You walk into a room and know where the warmth has gone out of it. It is a kind of touch, and it reaches animals as well as people.

Some days you give until nothing is left, and you start leaning on the people you look after. Wanting something back from them blurs the feeling. See to your own needs first, and ask for help when you are low. Then what others are missing is plain to you again.

Lean into the hard conversation, or the friend who is ill, instead of keeping away. Let old resentments go, and look after yourself the way you look after others. Being open and soft is your strength. Living this way, you feel more alive and more human.
fields.iching:
Something good is on its way to you, and it is still some way off. The worst of the cold is over, though you may not feel it yet. What is coming grows a little every day. Let it travel the whole distance at its own pace. It has to run its full course before you can call it yours.

If you have come through a long dark stretch, do not look down on the people still in it. Do not think less of work that seems smaller than yours. Keep teaching, and do not tire of it. Look after the people near you without fencing them in. There is a warning inside this good time. By autumn, what rises now will be falling. Do the work while things are growing, and let go of what is already on its way down.

Your mouth does the work now, to welcome and to teach. Keep your face open and your words few, and let what is coming arrive. Earth over Lake is the hexagram of drawing near. Lake is the warmth in you that people feel before you speak. Earth is the part of you that makes room for whatever comes close. The warmth sits underneath because people come near to what is glad to see them. This hexagram has long been read as the turn of the year, when the days begin to lengthen and the cold still holds the ground. You do nothing to bring the spring, and it comes all the same. You cannot hurry what is coming to you, and you do not have to. Approach
fields.gene_keys:
Co-Dependence Sensitivity Sacrifice Sensitivity opens once you are fed. When your own needs are met, you stop wanting anything from the people around you. Then you start to read everyone nearby the way a barometer reads the weather. Much of it reaches you through the hands, the skin and even the hair, which is why many who have it heal for a living. Being easily hurt is something else. This is a strength, and it looks after itself because it knows what it needs.

Its whole art is going slowly. You do not rush to greet a stranger, and you let them come to you at the speed they like. With an animal you wait until it trusts you, then let it touch you first. You learn this fast, mostly from the times you got it wrong. Once it is yours, you feel strong and soft at the same time, as if you have come home to the family of living things. Leaning on something outside yourself is where this energy starts, and the habit is very old. People once lived on what nature gave them, and they made gods of it. The same lean runs through a marriage, a family or a faith. You are all right only while someone above you stays kind, which is how it feels to be a victim. From inside, it feels like love. Both people give up part of themselves to keep the other close, and neither feels whole.

The old fear of not having enough is fading, and it is not going quietly. Some people are stepping out on their own while others hold tighter to the old ways, and it shows first at home. What ends the lean is not a better person to lean on. It is finding that life feeds you directly, with no one standing in between. Sacrifice is where this energy ends up, and it holds nothing back. The small kind gives your power away to please other people, and it harms you. The real kind happens inside you. You give up the harsh word about someone, the grievance, even the wish to be understood. Often the sacrifice is to say nothing, because what you see cannot yet be shown.

The greatest lives of this kind are never seen. Every living thing is fed by the life below it, and you belong to that chain. Past a certain point you work for everyone and no longer call it giving, because you know no other way to live.
fields.human_design: Wanting Gate 19 is a pressure to have your needs met, and the needs of the people around you. You long to be close, and you notice at once when a person close to you is left out. Tension between people presses on you until you want to settle it. The feeling behind it can be fine to the point of discomfort. Some who carry it cannot stand the seams in their socks, or being touched in certain ways. The same pressure makes it easy to give too much. It works best when you give from what is left over, never from what you have to keep for yourself.
fields.tarot: This energy reaches toward other creatures. It belongs to a family of three, the Ring of Gaia, which ties every living thing on earth into one body. This one carries sacrifice. UL 60, Woven Light, carries the justice that returns to you whatever you give up without thought for yourself. After that comes UL 61, Celestial Remembrance, which carries the sacred in every living thing. The ring and the two trigrams bring five of the tarot's major cards, its Arcana.
fields.body:
The body hair carries this energy, and the reason is goosebumps. Every hair has a nerve wrapped round its root, so you feel a thing when it bends the hair, before it reaches your skin. At each root is a muscle the size of a thread, pulled by the same adrenaline that quickens your heart. Cold, fear or a bar of music can raise them, and nothing you decide can. In an animal the raised hair lifts a coat to keep it warm, and in you it still rises for a coat that is gone. Something comes near, your skin knows first, and your arms answer before you have named it.

Blow across the back of your hand. You feel the air at once, through the hairs, before it could cool the skin. That is the part of you that feels what is coming before it arrives. What you feel in other creatures has a chemistry in you, and one of its substances is isoleucine. Your body cannot make it and has to take it in from meat, milk or beans. The same piece is in every animal you have ever touched, because every living body is built from the same twenty. You share this substance with two other energies.

As the old ways tighten their grip, a reaction is going on in that chemistry, in your body more than your mind. It opens a way of feeling what it is like to live inside another creature. It brings you back to being one with everything alive on this planet.

fields.essence: Just before you act, you can stop and see your life as it is. Calm lives in that pause. You see the kind moments and the careless ones alike, without judging either. From there a choice emerges on its own, clear, from the whole of you. People near you feel this calm before you have said a word.
fields.glance:
Just before you act, you can stop and see your life as it is. Calm lives in that pause. You see the kind moments and the careless ones alike, without judging either. From there a choice emerges on its own, clear, from the whole of you. People near you feel this calm before you have said a word.

For long stretches you are elsewhere, reacting and rushing, without noticing. Then something brings you up for air, and you remember what being here is like. Meet those stretches gently. Forcing the calm back only makes you tight.

Make room for it in small things. Keep your space simple, and know where things go in your house. Before you drink a cup of tea, stop and look at it. Calm grows from a love of small things like these. Then it stays with you through the day, and you know that everything is going to be all right.
fields.iching:
You have stopped just before you act. The hands are washed, and the offering is not yet made. Nothing has happened yet, and this pause matters most. A sincerity gathers in you here, and it shows without a word being said. The people who look to you see it and are changed by it.

So look before you go on. Look at yourself first, at what you want from this and whether you are sure you are right. Sometimes it is not the question that needs looking at, but the one asking it. Then look out across your whole life, the way wind moves over a field and reaches every part of it. The seasons keep their order without a word from the sky, and what you teach by being seen works the same way.

Keep your eyes open and your hands still. Sit the way someone waits before an offering, and let what you see settle before you move. Wind over Earth is the hexagram of looking at your life and being seen. Wind is the attention in you that moves gently into every part of a day. Earth is your life as it is, the ground under everything you do. The attention sits above the ground because you see your life only when you rise a little above it. This hexagram has long been read as a tower on high ground, where you see far and are seen from far. Stand at a window over a street, and the people below can see you too. You are known by where you stand when you look. Contemplation
fields.gene_keys:
Superficiality Self-Assurance Presence Being looked after is the first feeling of this gift, as if something larger than you were keeping watch. That something is your own greater nature coming through. Life has its own plans, and you stop getting in their way. No method brings this; only life can show you how to let go. It rests on giving way rather than pushing, which makes it far more than confidence. Its seat is low in the belly. It grows through trust and patience. You let things come to you instead of chasing them down. This is a kind of holy laziness, and it is what lets you rest inside.

Criticism still comes, and you can take it in without falling over. Old habits come back and are let go again, slowly, achingly slowly. Life feels lighter, with a quiet humour inside it. Living on the surface of your own life is older than you are. An insect on a summer day is busy from the first warmth until dark, alive the whole time and aware of none of it. Much of a human day runs the same way. Your mind can only think in a line, from before to after, so each time you think you seem to leave the present. You still live in the present whether you like it or not. You only stop feeling it. Keeping busy then feels like being alive, though it is really a way of not being there.

It is painful to look back at the hurt you caused without noticing, or the dreams you left lying about. That is where the looking begins. At the end of a day, ask how much of it you were there for. Nothing is being judged. You are only seeing what is. A leaf falls from a tree in autumn, and the leaf does not decide it. The tree lets it go. Presence is that letting go, and one day it happens to you. You do not decide it either. Life lets you go a little more each day, until nothing in you is holding on. You could sit in one place for three days and feel no time pass. A leaf or a stone in front of you holds more life than any idea you have. There is nothing to say about it, so you are silent.

Anyone can feel it near you. The air around you eases, breathing grows deeper, and soon the whole room breathes as one. Your gaze turns soft.
fields.human_design: The Now Gate 20 is the drive to act in the present, rather than planning ahead or going back over what is past. It carries a sense of timing, when to move and when to hold back, which is a different thing from haste. Waiting is part of it. While you wait, you sense what has to be set in motion behind the scenes, such as the right people or a skill to learn. When the moment is ripe, you move with all of your weight behind one act. In conversation your attention is undivided, and people feel it. The cost comes when you act too soon. You force what would have come on its own, then want to quit when it does not come.
fields.tarot: This energy watches, and a child learns by watching. It belongs to a family of six, the Ring of Life and Death. The other five are what a child needs to see you do. UL 27, Inner Majesty, carries the way you give. UL 42, Moving to Perfection, carries the way you let go. UL 24, Frequency Flutter, carries what you invent. UL 3, Messengers of the Infinite, carries the new things you try. UL 23, Beneath the Surface, carries how simply you live. This one carries your watching. Its family and its two trigrams bring four of the tarot's major cards, its Arcana, to this one.
fields.body:
Now is the reason this energy is given to the brain stem. The brain stem is the stalk your brain sits on, just inside the base of your skull. It sets the pace of your breathing and the beat of your heart. It has done this since before you were born, through every night's sleep and every hour your mind was elsewhere. It keeps no memory and makes no plan. Your mind can be in last year or next week, while this part of you is in this breath. When your mind comes back to your body, it comes back to where the brain stem already was.

Count the breaths you have taken since you began reading. You decided none of them. Put a finger in the hollow at the back of your neck, just under the skull. A finger's length inside, behind the bone, is the part of you that is always in the present. The calm in you has a chemistry, and one substance in it is leucine. Your body cannot make it, so it has to come in from meat, milk or beans. Your body never turns it into sugar. It only burns it or builds you with it.

A child near you takes in what you are, more than anything you say. When you give without holding on, try new things and keep life simple, the child grows up sure of itself. Calm shares its chemistry in you with silence and with giving. It shares it too with a child's innocence and with celebration.

fields.essence: When something is stuck and no one will decide, authority wakes in you. You feel it as a steadiness in your chest before you have said a word. You see what has to happen, you say it plainly, and you stand behind it. People settle when you speak, because they trust you to carry what follows.
fields.glance:
When something is stuck and no one will decide, authority wakes in you. You feel it as a steadiness in your chest before you have said a word. You see what has to happen, you say it plainly, and you stand behind it. People settle when you speak, because they trust you to carry what follows.

Some days you try to control everything around you, and by evening you are worn out. Under that grip is a fear that things will fall apart unless you hold them. Notice the fear and let one thing go its own way. Trust life to do some of the work, and your strength comes back.

Authority is given to you by people who trust you, and it cannot be taken. It grows as you stop needing to be in charge. Live in the balance between letting things go their own way and stepping in. Use it to serve the people who gave it to you. Then no one is above you or below you, and the people you lead work beside you.
fields.iching:
Something has come between you and the people you live or work with, and it will not go away by itself. Waiting will not move it, and talking around it will not either. It has to be dealt with, once and fairly. First look at it until you can see exactly what it is and how big it is. Then act, and make what you do fit the size of the wrong. Too little leaves it in place. Too much does harm of its own. Whatever you put right by force costs you something too, so try to settle it by talking first. When talking fails, be firm. Rules that everyone knows in advance save a great deal of trouble later.

Put your attention on your jaw for a moment. A jaw goes tight when something has to be dealt with and has not been. Once the matter is handled, the jaw closes and rests, and people can come together again. Fire over Thunder is the hexagram of dealing with what stands in the way. Thunder is the strength in you that moves and acts. Fire is the clarity in you that tells one thing from another. The clarity sits above the strength because a blow struck before you can see lands in the wrong place. This hexagram has long been read as a mouth held open by something caught between the teeth. When something sits unsettled between you and another person, you cannot take anything in or speak freely either. Dealing with it lets the two of you come together again. You act well when you see clearly first. Biting Through
fields.gene_keys:
Control Authority Valour Strength of this kind comes from giving up control, never from taking more of it. The sword you were handed is rusty, the horse is old and the odds are against you. That is the test, and it is the size you can meet. Meet each one with honesty and care, and the sword starts to shine where people can see it. Loyalty won through fear moves elsewhere the moment it can. Loyalty won through love stays, because there is more love in you than fear.

At its best the one in charge serves, and the one who serves is trusted with charge. Neither is under the other, and the two of you work with a power neither had alone. In time people come toward you, drawn by the same light they want in themselves. Everything you call yours is ground to be held, and the first ground is your own body. From there the line goes out around your family, your house, your money and your country. Under it is the oldest fear there is, that one day you will simply stop existing. So you take up the sword and hack at life to keep it in line, and life hits back. The grip works for a while. Rule people by force and you get your way for a time, and then it all comes apart. Too much discipline makes people rebel, and too little leaves everything loose. Here the one who controls and the one who is controlled both lose. What drives it all is a distrust of life itself. Hold on tight for long enough and you find you were only ever fighting yourself. Valour is courage with love in it, and it is what is left once no one in you needs to be in charge. You see something noble in the other person, even the one you cannot stand, and you bow to it. In an old story a young king wins a fight, then hands his sword to the man he beat. When you win and still bow to the one you beat, you gain their loyalty for life. The sword that once hacked is used to heal.

People who live this never feel like an authority, and they meet you as a friend. Threaten what they love, though, and they fight with everything they have.
fields.human_design:
Self-Regulation Gate 21 is the drive to manage what you have, from your money and your time to the people who rely on you. It wants a say in how each of these is run. It is known as the hunter and the treasurer, the one who brings in what is needed and then keeps count of it. At its best it starts with you. You give yourself the rest and the limits you need, and act from there.

When fear takes over, you feel you have to earn your place. You take on too much and work for support you could simply accept. The challenge here is to let go of outcomes and of managing other people. What is left is a calm in the middle of your own storm.
fields.tarot: This energy decides for others, where the oldest wound between people begins. It belongs to a family of six, the Ring of Humanity, which tells the story every person lives. UL 25, The Mysteries Play, carries the wound you are born with. UL 38, Inner Light Symphony, carries the fight with your shadow. UL 17, Pearl of Christos, carries getting past your own mind. UL 10, Internal Treasure, carries finding yourself. UL 51, Unshakable Arrival, carries waking up. This one carries letting go of the need to run life. The ring and the two trigrams give this card five of the tarot's major cards, its Arcana.
fields.body:
The breath out is the reason this energy is given to your lungs. You just let one go, and you will let the next one go without deciding to. Your lungs take the air of the room across a wall thinner than paper, and a moment later it is in your blood. Breathing is the one thing in your body your will can take over. You can hold a breath, slow it, or shape it into words. You cannot keep the hold. Within a minute or two your body takes the breath back, whatever you decide. That is where your say over your own body ends.

Your lungs have no muscle of their own, and your ribs move them. Breathe all the way out and wait, and the next breath comes without you. Even after the hardest breath out, about a litre of air stays inside. Your lungs have not been empty since your first breath. Leading and being led have a chemistry in you, and one substance in it is arginine. Your body makes it for itself, and more comes in with meat, beans or nuts. It is one of the twenty pieces every protein in you is built from. It is also the last step by which your body turns the nitrogen it cannot use into waste and lets it go.

Rank is one of the oldest wounds between people, one above and one below, and only love heals it. Your body carries the same substance whether you lead or follow. When the one in charge serves and the one who serves is trusted, the difference between them starts to fade.

fields.essence: A strong feeling comes up in you while someone else is in the room. Graciousness lives in what you do next. You feel it whole in your body, the joy or the grief or the anger. The people with you are treated kindly all the same, and near you they feel listened to.
fields.glance:
A strong feeling comes up in you while someone else is in the room. Graciousness lives in what you do next. You feel it whole in your body, the joy or the grief or the anger. The people with you are treated kindly all the same, and near you they feel listened to.

Some days a low mood arrives for no reason you can find, and you want someone to blame. Let it pass through you without putting it on anyone, and it is gone within minutes. Decide nothing big until it has passed.

Say what you feel when the mood is with you, and wait when it is not. Say a hard thing kindly, at a time it can be heard. What you have lived through becomes a treasure, and it shows in the way you treat people. You grow grateful for whatever each day brings, and people turn to you when their own feelings run high.
fields.iching:
Things are going well enough, and how they look matters now. A kind word or a tidy room helps, and each is a small thing. Take care over the outside of things, and let it show what is truly there. The beauty is real, and it changes nothing underneath.

Use it for the small matters of the day. Do not settle anything serious by how it looks, because a decision made on the surface will not hold. Let what is solid lead and the beauty follow. If you want more than small gains, learn and live more, a little each day. What you know becomes your beauty, and what you live through becomes your grace.

Your eyes do the work now, and your hands stay still. Take in every detail of what is in front of you, and hold off from reaching for it. Sit the way someone sits looking at a hillside at dusk.
