Mountain over Fire is the hexagram of how what is inside you shows on the outside. Fire is the clarity in you that sees each thing plainly. Mountain is the steadiness in you that stays as it is, whatever light falls on it. The clarity sits inside and the steadiness outside, because you see a great deal and show only a little of it. This hexagram has long been read as a fire at the foot of a mountain. Its light makes the hillside beautiful at dusk, and the rock underneath does not change. So the light is enough for the small matters of a day, never for settling a serious dispute. What you show is beautiful when it comes from what you are. Grace
fields.gene_keys:
Dishonour Graciousness Grace Graciousness grows once your feelings are your own. You live fully and hold nothing back, and you still consider how the people around you feel. You express what you feel safely and disrespect no one, yourself included. Nobody else's mood makes a victim of you either. When someone close to you is low and puts it on you, you feel for them and stay clear of it.

Now the strings are in tune, and people feel listened to around you. You know that an unkindness done to someone comes back, so you treat everyone with dignity, however they behave. This is tested all your life, and each test refines it. You learn to be careful without being fearful, warm without being overbearing, and candid without being cruel. In time you grow grateful for whatever comes. Discomfort comes, and the first thing you do is look for its cause outside you. You blame the weather, or more often another person. That is where dishonour starts, and it starts with you. Every time you refuse the way you feel, you dishonour yourself. Put your mood on someone else, and you dishonour both of you at once.

Think of your feelings as the strings of an instrument that hears everything. At this height the strings are out of tune, so whatever comes near sounds wrong. You try to fix your mood or change it, when it only needs to pass through. Every feeling is there to be trusted, and trusting it is not the same as acting on it. Nothing you do goes unheard, and what you send out comes back to you. Grace comes down on you, and you cannot make it happen. It can be a small moment. A tiny bird with a gold stripe on its head stops you on a morning walk, and you carry it all day. Moments like this lift you when you have fallen. You prepare for them by meeting each fall openly, because grace is hidden inside every low.

When it stays, your life is no longer yours to steer. You are the instrument, and something greater plays you. Fear ends for good, and every feeling turns into love. Whoever meets you feels it and never forgets it.
fields.human_design: Openness Gate 22 sits in the pit of your stomach and wants to be heard. What you feel presses to be taken in by another person. Its fear is speaking and not being heard, and when the fear wins you go silent. It follows your mood. When the mood is right, you say what you feel with depth, and people are moved. When it is not, you want no company, and nothing is wrong with that. It has a sense of timing, knowing when to speak and when to listen. Held back out of fear, it settles for less than it wants.
fields.tarot: This energy meets pain with kindness, and its family is built around suffering that opens you. It belongs to a family of four, the Ring of Divinity. UL 36, Crystal Creation, carries the dark stretch that tests you. UL 37, Journey Home, carries the warmth of the family you belong to. UL 63, Adornments of Time, carries the question that will not let you go. This one carries grace. Five of the tarot's major cards, its Arcana, arrive through the ring and the two trigrams.
fields.body:
A catch under the breastbone is the reason this energy is given to the solar plexus. Bad news comes, and in the first second something catches there, before you have a word for it. Your breath stops for a beat. Then the feeling either rises to your throat and is said, or it stays where it landed. Held there, fear settles in as tension through your whole body. Let through, it leaves your body at rest.

The solar plexus is a knot of nerves on the front of your spine, behind the stomach. It is two knots, each the size of a fingertip, with fibres going out like the rays of a sun. Lay a hand flat in the soft hollow below your breastbone and take a sharp breath in. The hollow pushes out against your hand. About a hand's depth behind it is where you feel things before you know them. The feeling that comes over you has a chemistry, and one substance in it is proline. Every protein in you is built from twenty pieces, and your body makes this one itself, from another of the twenty. You never need to eat it.

At its fullest this energy comes down into you and fills the whole of you. It floods you the way a woman early in pregnancy is flooded and made ready. Your body is readied, low in the belly, for something that has not yet arrived. What fills you then was made inside you and never taken in from outside. Three other energies in you share this chemistry.

fields.essence: Beneath all that a life piles up, there is one thing that matters, and clarity is how you find it. You feel it first as ease in your body. Worry drops away, and you breathe freely. A problem you have carried for days turns out to be simple. You cut through the rest and say the point in a few plain words.
fields.glance:
Beneath all that a life piles up, there is one thing that matters, and clarity is how you find it. You feel it first as ease in your body. Worry drops away, and you breathe freely. A problem you have carried for days turns out to be simple. You cut through the rest and say the point in a few plain words.

Some days your mind will not trust a plain answer, because a plain answer gives it nothing to think about. It wraps the answer in more, and the more it adds, the more anxious you feel. Then leave the problem alone and cook or dig, and your rhythm comes back.

Before each choice, ask whether it will make your life simpler. Look around your home for what is neither useful nor beautiful, and give it away. Eat when you are hungry, drink when you are thirsty, and stop when you have had enough. Your days open up, and people understand you the first time.
fields.iching:
Something you relied on is falling away, and it started low, where you were not looking. What was added for show goes first. Then whatever has the least beneath it begins to tip. It is the end of a season, and the change creeps up slowly from below.

Do not set out for anywhere now. Stay low and keep still, and do not argue with what is pulling at you. Give to the people who hold you up, since a height stands only on its base. What is against you is stronger than you for now, and it will pass. The turn back comes after it, so let it pass without bitterness.

Keep your feet where they are, and let the ground settle under them. Sit the way a mountain sits on the plain, low, wide and still. Mountain over Earth is the hexagram of what falls away. Earth is the part of you that gives way and carries whatever is put on it. Mountain is the part of you that stands firm and stops. The firm part sits on top because everything you have built rests on what holds it up. This hexagram has long been read as a tall mountain on too narrow a base, wearing away into the plain. What wears away first in your life is what you stand on. When the extra falls away, you see what was holding you up. Splitting Apart
fields.gene_keys:
Complexity Simplicity Quintessence Simplicity is a knack more than a skill, and it cannot really be taught. Above the cloud you see further, and you hear only what matters while the noise drops away. Your rooms have space in them. You are good with money because you know where not to waste it. People relax around you, and the problems they brought seem to dissolve. You watch in silence until the answer jumps out, then you say it. It is often funny and catches a whole moment in one line.

Inside, the clearing goes on for years. Your thoughts start to have gaps between them, and your feelings are let run their course. You stop needing to settle everything. When you say no, you say it with grace, and a yes sits inside it. A mind that wants to feel safe makes things complicated. The harder it tries to control the world, the more tangled and unsafe the world becomes. In cloud a pilot sees nothing and flies in circles looking for a way out. The mind circles the same way around a simple question. You cannot give a straight reply, even when someone asks for one word, and the listener backs away.

It is never the words. It is the tone under them. If even a trace of fear drives what you say, nobody can take it in, however fine the words are. Under it is a fear of being shut out, and the fear brings about the very thing it fears. Quintessence is what is left when you boil something down to its heart, then boil that heart down again. Beyond the cloud there is only silence. Each thought you do not need splits apart, and what remains speaks through you. A person living this touches the gold in other people with a word or a look, without knowing they do it.

You cannot get here by trying. You find it by mistake, once you have stopped seeking and let yourself wonder. When you speak from here, the pauses between your words say as much as the words. You come to see your life and its ending at the heart of each other.
fields.human_design:
Transmission Gate 23 is the drive to take something complicated, break it down and say it in a way nobody has said it before. You know things ahead of the proof and ahead of the room. So you can feel like an outsider until the others catch up. Everything turns on the hour. Said too early, to people who are not ready, the truest thing you know sounds like a need to be right. Then you feel bitter and unseen, and you wonder why nobody sees what is obvious to you.

Broken down too far, a thing loses what mattered in it, so the work is to make it small without making it less. Trust what you know before you can explain it. The people who are ready will ask.
fields.tarot: This energy keeps what matters and lets the rest fall away. It belongs to a family of six, the Ring of Life and Death, which holds the plainest truths about a life. Messengers of the Infinite shows you that everything changes, and Emerging as the Code that what is real is this moment. Frequency Flutter shows you that things begin again, Inner Majesty the good in your heart, and Moving to Perfection how to let go. This one gathers them into a simple life. The ring and the two trigrams bring five of the tarot's major cards, its Arcana, each a way you meet this energy.
fields.body:
The pause is the reason this energy is given to the throat. Every breath in parts the two small folds in your throat, and while they stay apart you cannot make a word. They close for sound and part again for the next breath. So you build every sentence between breaths, and you never choose the gaps. Lay a hand on your throat and breathe in, and it goes still under your fingers. Say a long sentence and it stops where your breath runs out.

Just below your voice sits the gland that sets the pace of your whole body. Its hormone goes into each cell and works there, out of sight, so what it did this morning shows only hours or days later. The timing that decides whether your words suit the listener works the same way, below anything you can watch. The simplicity in you has a chemistry, and leucine is part of it. Your body cannot make it. It has to come in with food such as meat, milk or beans. It is part of every protein in your body. Your muscles take it apart themselves instead of sending it to the liver.

You share this chemistry with five other energies, and what they share is the plainest fact there is. Everything alive in you is changing, and everything that changes comes to an end. Its essence is not in your head. It sits deep in your belly, at the centre of all your centres.

fields.essence: Invention comes alive in you when you go back to something you know well. You return to an old problem or a habit and turn it over once more. Then your thinking goes quiet for a moment. In that pause an idea is there that you could never have planned. It often comes while you rest or sleep, and it surprises you as much as anyone. It lifts you, and the old weight falls away.
fields.glance:
Invention comes alive in you when you go back to something you know well. You return to an old problem or a habit and turn it over once more. Then your thinking goes quiet for a moment. In that pause an idea is there that you could never have planned. It often comes while you rest or sleep, and it surprises you as much as anyone. It lifts you, and the old weight falls away.

Sometimes the quiet feels empty, even like falling. You reach for your phone or for something to do, and the same old round starts again. When that happens, stay a little longer. The empty feeling passes, and it is the room a new idea needs.

Be honest that you do not know, and let the question rest. Go back to an old hurt and look for what it gave you. When a new way appears, take one step with it, then take the same step next time until it is how you live. Each time you come round, you come round a note higher.
fields.iching:
A long decline has reached its end, and the turn has come. Nothing on the surface shows it yet. The light comes back on its own, the way the days lengthen after midwinter. No effort of yours brought it, and none can hurry it.

What has just come back is small, so keep it close. On the shortest day the rulers closed the gates, and even traders stayed at home. Rest, look after your own people, and spend no strength on the wider world for now. Come and go without strain. Friends will find you, and no one is at fault. The turn comes round in its own time, and once it has come it is good to have somewhere to go.

Part of this return happens by itself. The other part is your care in keeping it. Move your body a little each day, because the mind moves with it. Then stand still in your own centre and let the turn come to you. Earth over Thunder is the hexagram of coming back after the lowest point. Thunder is the part of you that starts to move again. Earth is the part of you that takes in what comes and lets it grow. The movement sits under the ground because a return starts out of sight, long before anything shows. This hexagram has long been read as thunder inside the earth at midwinter. On the shortest day the fields look dead, and the days are already getting longer. The same turn happens when you find your way back after a wrong turn. You come back to yourself before anyone can see it. Return
fields.gene_keys:
Addiction Invention Silence Invention is what arrives when you stay in the gap. The gaps open for everyone, and once you meet one it is not frightening at all. You catch yourself reaching to fill it, and you stay instead. Then anything can happen. A great tennis player does this under pressure, with a shot nobody could have trained against. What comes surprises you as much as anyone.

It comes most often at rest, while you sit quietly, dream or do nothing. You think a problem over along the usual routes, and then something shifts and you see it whole. The same tune comes round, a note higher each time. It asks one honesty of you, to say you do not know and may never know. A mind finds a few tunes it likes and plays them for the rest of its life. There are many keys in you, and most days you play the same handful. Your thoughts follow the same routes, and your life follows them too. Every so often the tune stops, for a second or for a week. In that gap you meet your own discomfort with nothing in the way. Most people fill it fast, with a drink, a screen or more work. Then the old tune starts again.

That is why a new town or a new partner changes so little. The same scene plays out with new faces. Your hope moves into the future, and nothing outside you can end what runs inside. What begins to change it is noticing that you are in it. The moment you see the pattern, a pause has opened. Silence is what is left when the thinking stops for good. It is the quiet of a night sky, full of light. It comes down on you, though it was inside you all along. Your centre drops from your head into your belly. You stop doing the thinking, and life does it through you.

The last habit goes with it, the belief that you are separate from life. Your body will come and go, as every body does. The silence between the notes is the one thing that keeps coming back.
fields.human_design:
Blessings Gate 24 is the need to know why. It sends your mind back over the same ground, an old hurt or an unsolved problem, to see what it missed. From outside this can look like being stuck. It is how this kind of mind works, by going back rather than going on. Each time round it can find something new.

Its trouble is that it can talk itself into anything. Faced with an old pain, it can build a story in which settling for less makes sense. The story feels like protection and does the damage. At its best it goes back to the pain on purpose and finds the blessing in it. Then it tells the story again with that inside it. The answers it cannot think of are waiting in the gaps between thoughts.
fields.tarot: This energy goes back to the gap where one cycle ends and the next begins. It belongs to a family of six, the Ring of Life and Death, and between them they hold one whole life of yours. Your first breath is in Messengers of the Infinite, and your watching in Emerging as the Code. Your clearing out is in Beneath the Surface, your feeding in Inner Majesty and your finishing in Moving to Perfection. This one holds your turn at the bottom, when you start again. Open the one whose season you are in. Five of the tarot's major cards, its Arcana, stand near this energy.
fields.body:
This energy is given to the neocortex, the outer sheet of the brain, and the reason is the path. Everything you learn is a route worn into that sheet. A route used once is faint. A route used a thousand times becomes a road you take without thinking, and routes you stop using fade. That is why your second try is easier than your first. The old thoughts you keep returning to are roads like this. Something you know well even uses less of the sheet than it did while you were learning it.

Sign your name, then sign it with the other hand. The first is a road worn over years. The second has no road at all, and you feel the difference at once. A new road in you is made the way the old one was, one step taken again. This energy has a chemistry in you, and the substance is leucine. Your body cannot make it, so it has to come from food such as meat, beans or corn. Corn is full of it and short of what beans have, so when you eat the two together you get what each lacks.

What this family shares is the gap. It is the family of coming into a body and leaving it, of a wheel that keeps turning. Whatever changes in you changes in the spaces between, between two lives or two notes. Your body takes its leucine in fresh with every meal.

fields.essence: Love runs through you most freely on a day that does not go to plan. The car ahead is slow and the rain comes at the wrong moment, and you let each be as it is. You slow down, and the day tastes different. You feel you belong wherever you are, and a grudge is hard for you to keep. What you do comes with nothing to gain from it, and people can feel that.
fields.glance:
Love runs through you most freely on a day that does not go to plan. The car ahead is slow and the rain comes at the wrong moment, and you let each be as it is. You slow down, and the day tastes different. You feel you belong wherever you are, and a grudge is hard for you to keep. What you do comes with nothing to gain from it, and people can feel that.

Some days a worry hums in you with no cause you can name. Thinking will not get you out of it. Feel it where it sits in your body, and it starts to loosen.

Nobody can force a heart open, and yours opens in its own time. The more you accept yourself and the people around you, the more love grows in your life. You are at your strongest when you are most natural. In the end the same warmth goes out from you to everyone alike.
fields.iching:
You are acting from the heart, with nothing to gain. That is when things go best, and it is also when the unexpected finds you. Something may go wrong that you did not cause. Being blameless does not keep trouble away, but it does not have to throw you off balance either.

What this time asks is to keep your aim plain. A wish to be seen or a hidden bargain turns the same move against you. Then no direction helps. This is not the time for a long journey or a big plan. Wisdom here is knowing when fixing a thing would bring more trouble than leaving it be. Do your part, and let the result take its own course.

Stop turning it over in your head, and let your breath settle low in your belly. Let what you do be as plain as what you mean. Heaven over Thunder is the hexagram of acting with nothing false in you. Thunder is the sudden move in you that comes before you have thought it through. Heaven is the strength in you that keeps going and asks nothing back. The move sits under the strength because it goes well only when it serves more than what you want for yourself. This hexagram has long been read as thunder rolling under the sky. Thunder is loud and means no harm. When nothing is hidden in what you do, people trust even your strongest words. You do best when you want nothing back. Innocence
fields.gene_keys:
Constriction Acceptance Universal Love Acceptance is a way of seeing, and it comes in three steps. The first step is to allow. Whatever is happening, you let your body feel what it feels, and after a while your breath slows. Then you accept. With the breath settled, you can feel your feelings without drowning in them. You may weep, go numb or be afraid, and your heart reminds you that underneath it all things are still all right. Last you embrace, and the mind lets go like a factory manager who has spent all day keeping machines from overheating and gives up.

Resignation is the dropped head of someone who has decided nothing can change. Acceptance is done with your head held high, almost in defiance. It says to the pain: I see you, and you are only the beginning. Each time you try to accept yourself, you find a further place where you do not. Life keeps testing it, and each time it goes deeper. Constriction starts in the breath. It sits as a tightness across the chest and a pressure pushed down into the belly. Most people learn it very young, from the way their parents breathed. Fear is what holds it in place, and fear is clever. It is afraid of itself, so it never looks at itself, and that is how it survives. The grip spreads into how you hold on to things, an opinion, an object or a person. Love grows where there is room and dies in a grip. Turn away from the pain and life shrinks to distraction, a half-life lived around the tightness. The harder you choke it down, the tighter it holds.

Something wound this tight is there to be unwound. Turn toward it, and the unwinding has already begun. There is nothing personal in universal love. It is what holds everything together, and here you can no longer say you love anyone more than anything else. It cannot be willed. You go on opening and softening, and it arrives on its own once the personal flavour has burned off. What remains is a knowing in your body that everything is one.

Blood has long stood for this love. What your family handed down to you in it carries both their old hurts and their healing. From here the tightness is nothing to be ashamed of. It was the grit inside the oyster, and the pearl formed around it.
fields.human_design: Spirit Gate 25 is the love of spirit, a love for life itself. It drives you to live as an offering instead of a performance put on to prove your worth. It carries a purity so bright it can overwhelm. You pick up what the people around you feel, sometimes before they have said it. Setbacks do not easily disillusion you, because you see them as part of a larger pattern. The same openness can make you idealise a partner and miss what is plainly wrong. When this pull is mistrusted, you try to make your life by willpower alone, and you end up feeling cut off and unworthy. Lived well, you take up no more room than is yours, and no less.
fields.tarot: This love is the core of being human, and it starts from a wound. Its family of six tells the one story every life tells. The Mysteries Play is the wound you start with. Inner Light Symphony is the fight with your own shadows. Pearl of Christos is the mind's limits outgrown, and Beyond Binary is the need to control given up. Internal Treasure is finding who you are. Unshakable Arrival is the waking after. Open any of them to see where you stand. The ring and the two trigrams bring five of the tarot's major cards, its Arcana.
fields.body:
The heart is given this energy because of the blood. It sends the same blood to every part of you and picks no favourites. Your brain and your little toe get it alike. The whole of it goes round your body in about a minute. It began beating about three weeks after you were conceived, before there was a brain to know it. That is what this love is like from inside, a warmth that goes to everything because that is the only way it goes.

Put your hand flat on the left of your chest and you will find the beat. When you are afraid, your chest tightens around it and your breath rises high. Let the fear be felt instead of braced against, and the chest gives, a little at a time. It does not have to be told. It only has to stop being held. This love has a chemistry in you, and one substance in it is arginine. It is part of every protein in your body. Your body makes it. A body healing from a wound cannot make enough, so it takes the rest from meat, eggs or beans.

What you carry is wound in layers deep in your body, one around another. As each layer relaxes, you can feel love moving in you again.

fields.essence: The drive to make things happen is alive in you, and it can get almost anything done. You feel it rise when you believe in something. You know how to show that thing so people want it, in words that fit whoever is in front of you. You love being seen carrying something that matters. Held back until you know what it is for, this drive grows stronger.
fields.glance:
The drive to make things happen is alive in you, and it can get almost anything done. You feel it rise when you believe in something. You know how to show that thing so people want it, in words that fit whoever is in front of you. You love being seen carrying something that matters. Held back until you know what it is for, this drive grows stronger.

Some days a voice in you says nothing comes unless you grab it. Then you cannot rest for a moment, and nothing you gather feels like enough. Stop there, and listen under your own plans for the aim that was there first.

When you hear it, put your whole heart behind it. Sell only what you know is true, and sell it with love. Rest when the work is done, because you are worth resting. Use what you gather to bring more to the people who have less. Then let the good you do go unseen, and you will feel lighter than a feather.
fields.iching:
You have more strength than this moment can use, and this is a time to store it. The power is real, and so is the danger of spending it all at once. When strength and plenty come together, it is easy to act without thinking. So when you feel the pull to rush in, keep still instead. Energy stored now is ready to be released later. What you learn now is ready to be taught.

Fill yourself each day with what the people before you said and did, and let it shape who you are. Renew yourself daily with rest, good food and a fresh look at what you are working for. Then go out and cross the great river, and take on the large thing. Take nothing for yourself from the people you serve.

Stand with the presence of a mountain, with the whole strength of the sky moving through you. Keep your hands still until it is time to use them. Mountain over Heaven is the hexagram of a great strength stored until its time. Heaven is the drive in you that never tires. Mountain is the part of you that can keep still. The stillness sits above the drive because strength spent the moment it arrives never builds into anything. This hexagram has long been read as the sky held inside a mountain. Your strength gathers the way rain gathers between the peaks, before it falls. It also asks you to take what you gather out into the world and never to live off the people you serve. What you store now is what you will one day give. Great Taming
fields.gene_keys:
Pride Artfulness Invisibility Artfulness begins when you learn the difference between will and intention. Will is you forcing your idea onto life. Intention is a quiet aim that was in you before you chose anything, behind everything you do and say. You cannot force it out. You can only listen for it.

Then pride becomes a craft you enjoy. To sell a truth, you have to step into the light yourself, and you love the light. Freed from fear, your skill at winning people sells through love. Your ego becomes something you wear, like a costume before a show. In a crowded camp where most people waited, one group built a fire at the centre and cooked stew to share. Your cleverness can work the same way, for everyone. Ask yourself whether you are a giver or a taker. Pride starts from a belief that nothing comes to you unless you reach out and take it. Out of fear, you stop trusting the easy flow of life and pit your will against everything else. Will really can get you almost anything, and believing it is a step on the way. To climb by will alone you push others down, often without seeing it. Pride is clever enough to find the cheapest deal and pass off the blame. It even edits its own conscience. It forgets that what it takes from one place is taken from everyone.

Pride needs to be seen as strong, because underneath it fears being powerless. You can tell it in a person because they cannot relax, even for a moment. However much you gather, it never feels like enough inside. Under it all lies the oldest fear, of being no one. The more solidly you build yourself up, the harder that fear bites. Invisibility comes when the pride has been polished all the way, until it serves everything. To give up an ego, you first need one worth giving up. Your own will stops pushing and joins the rest of life. People find you hard to pin down. Wherever they look you are there, and when they try to hold you, you are gone. You turn the light onto someone who needs it and step out of it yourself. Only you know what you did, and that is enough. You take life less seriously than anyone, and your laughter rings on like a string of bells.
fields.human_design:
Integrity Gate 26 is the pull to tell a story so well that people take it in. It knows how to present a thing so it captivates, whether that is an idea, a product or yourself. What matters is what the selling serves. Out of lack, it sells to fill your own store. In integrity, it sells a real answer to a real problem. Integrity here means being whole, with no part of you split off from the rest.

The challenge of this gate is to believe you are worth your place in the world. If you learned you cannot afford that place, you trade your values for feeling safe. Then your worth hides under fear. Look after yourself so that you have something to give.
fields.tarot: This energy finds the quickest way to a thing, and it does not work alone. It belongs to a family of four, the Ring of Light, each a way you work with light. UL 5, The Space Between Time, is the patience that keeps time with everything around you. UL 9, Ease in This, is the step you keep taking. UL 11, Sol Star, is the dream of how things could be. This one finds the shortcut. Five of the tarot's major cards, its Arcana, gather here through the ring and the two trigrams.
fields.body:
Knowing what is yours is the reason this energy is given to the thymus gland. The thymus is where your body learned what belongs to it. Unfinished guard cells pass through it and are tested there. Any cell that would attack your own body is put down before it leaves. So the guard in you knows you and leaves you whole. When your will cannot rest, that guard wears down. When your will softens, your chest grows warm.

The gland did most of its work while you were a child. It shrinks after you stop growing, yet the cells it trained still stand guard in you. Lay a hand flat just below the notch at the top of your chest. Under your palm is the part of you that learned what is yours, without ever taking anything. The drive in you has a chemistry, and one substance in it is threonine. Your body cannot make it, so it comes to you in food, from fish or eggs. You share this substance with three other energies, and together they carry how your body takes in light and turns it into energy. Your part is the will, which bends that light to your own use.

The plainest proof of light at work in you is on your skin. Sunlight on it makes vitamin D, which your health depends on. Stand in the sun on any bright day and it is happening in you.

fields.essence: When a person close to you needs looking after, the care in you is already moving. You remember the birthday, and you look in on the friend who is sick. Near you, others lower their guard and let themselves be looked after, sometimes for the first time.
fields.glance:
When a person close to you needs looking after, the care in you is already moving. You remember the birthday, and you look in on the friend who is sick. Near you, others lower their guard and let themselves be looked after, sometimes for the first time.

At times you give more than you have, until it wears down your health. Resentment creeps in, or you hold people so close they cannot grow. Feed yourself first, with food, rest and time. Before you step in, notice who truly needs you.

Look after yourself as closely as you would anyone you love, and let others care for you in turn. Give to what is alive and able to grow, without keeping count. A day given freely moves slowly and feels full. Given this way, your care feeds you as it goes out, and you do not run dry.
fields.iching:
You have gathered something, and now it is time to eat from it and feed others with it. You stand at the mouth, where food goes in and words come out. What matters now is what you let in and what you let out. Feed the people who will go on to feed others, and what you give reaches everyone.

This time asks for care in two things: what you eat and drink, and what you say. Words are food too, so what you say to someone is something they have to eat. Keep to the kind who feed rather than take. Feed the ones below you before you go asking from the ones above.

Your jaw is the place to check. When you are reaching for more than you need, it hangs a little open, ready for the next thing. Close your lips, let the jaw go loose, and chew what you already have before you swallow it. Mountain over Thunder is the hexagram of how you are fed. Thunder is the movement in you that reaches for what you need. Mountain is the stillness in you that knows when you have had enough. The stillness sits above the movement because reaching on its own never stops. That is why this hexagram has long been read as a mouth. A mouth opens to take food in and closes when it is full. The same mouth speaks. So the care you take in eating is the care you take in what you say. You are fed by what you reach for and by when you stop. Nourishment
fields.gene_keys:
Selfishness Altruism Selflessness Care that wants nothing back is your nature, and nobody taught it to you. When one dolphin in a pod is in trouble, the whole pod turns to help at once. Your care moves the same way, toward whoever is in trouble, before you have decided anything. When your arm comes off the plate it goes to the middle of the table, and you are fuller for it.

This care knows, without being taught, what is worth giving to whom. It will not feed anyone's wish to stay helpless. It is the same pull that keeps a parent beside a child for the first seven years, the years that shape everything. A wound of your own from those years heals as you give what you did not get. What comes off you is trust, so people near you lower their guard, some for the first time in their lives. Purpose wells up out of this like water from a spring and spreads to whoever stands close. Selfishness is holding on to what you have, and it is the oldest move there is. Everything alive eats something else, and one thing's death is another's birth. You are in that chain, and holding on is what kept your blood line in it. So it is not a sin, whatever you were told. But it makes a small room, where life is tight and worry runs under everything. When you hurt inside you have no room to think of anyone else. At the table you eat with your arm around the plate.

You came into the world unselfish. A house or a school taught you to take, and what you learned you can unlearn. What is missing underneath is a purpose, a reason for your life bigger than yourself. People will do almost anything to avoid feeling that gap: once they went to war to fill it, now they go shopping. Stay in the small room long enough to ask what the larger reason would be. That question is what makes the room bigger. Nobody sits at the head of this table now. You still feed people, and there is no you doing it. What remains is a longing your body carries, for everything to be at peace with everything else. Food is only the visible part of it. This is different from doing good. The ones who help so they will be seen, or to cover a pain of their own, still have a self doing the helping. Here no self remains, so the people who live this go unnoticed, as ordinary as anyone in the street.

They give without end and never run dry, fed by the love around them. Where an ounce of life remains in anything, this care can reach it. Listen from there and everything eating and being eaten sounds like music. What you hear in it is love. You came into the world without a self and you will leave it without one. The self in between is something you dreamed up.
fields.human_design:
Caring Low in you sits the pressure to look after what is yours. Gate 27 is the name for it. It drives you to feed and protect the people you are responsible for, yourself among them, before anyone has asked. It is the pull that checks the door at night and counts the ones asleep. Nobody has to ask, and when it has nowhere to go you are restless without knowing why.

Left to itself, the same pull feeds people who did not need it and holds them so close they cannot grow. It picks up loads that were never yours, until you are tired, unthanked and sour. The question to ask is whose problem this is. Treat the other person as able, and let go with love so they can find their own strength.
fields.tarot: This care keeps one life going on another, and it belongs to a family of six, the Ring of Life and Death. Each of the six is a stage that something in your life passes through. UL 3 is the stage where it begins, and UL 20 the stage where you are fully in it. UL 23 is where it falls apart, UL 24 where it comes back and UL 42 where it grows on. Open the one that matches where you are. Five of the tarot's major cards come to this card through its family and its two trigrams. Each names one part of how you are fed.
fields.body:
The sacral plexus is where feeding ends in you, and that is why this energy is given to it. It is a weave of nerves on the inside of the flat bone at the base of your spine. The same low place holds the energy to carry and feed a child. What went in at your mouth this morning ends its road here. Nerves from this weave move the last of it along and say when to let go. Low in your back beside it, you keep the strength you were born with. You lived on that before you could eat, and every meal since has added to it.

You are doing it now. Something you ate is on the last of its road, and this weave is moving it without a thought from you. Put your hand on the small of your back, where the bone goes flat. Your hand is resting on the part of you that finishes what feeding began. The care in you has a substance, and its name is leucine. Your body cannot make it. It arrives in meat, eggs or beans, or not at all. After a meal your muscle notices it first, and between meals it is gone. Whether you hold on or give, you are running on the same chemistry.

Give for the sake of giving and you start healthy currents deep in your body. You share its chemistry with five other energies.

fields.essence: When something matters enough to give it everything, purpose wakes up in you. You feel it in your body: the day has an edge, and you are wide awake. You go toward the hard thing by choice, because a challenge you picked feels more alive than a comfort you were handed. You are building something you cannot see yet, and you give yourself to the mystery of where it leads.
fields.glance:
When something matters enough to give it everything, purpose wakes up in you. You feel it in your body: the day has an edge, and you are wide awake. You go toward the hard thing by choice, because a challenge you picked feels more alive than a comfort you were handed. You are building something you cannot see yet, and you give yourself to the mystery of where it leads.

Some days nothing seems to have a point, and a voice in you says it will all be too hard. That voice is fear, and your purpose lies inside the very fear you keep walking around. Look at it for as long as you can, and it loosens its grip.

Give the whole of yourself to what is in front of you. As your own fear quietens, your strength turns toward other people. Then you stop asking what your life is for, because you are living it.
fields.iching:
Something you have taken on has grown bigger than what holds it up. It might be a plan, a love or a cause. The middle is strong and the ends are weak, and the whole thing has started to bend. This is an unusual time, and there is nothing wrong in it. An unusual time asks for action out of the ordinary.

It is good to have somewhere to go. A weight like this cannot be held still for long, so either lighten the load or carry it somewhere. Adjust as you go, firmer where you are weak and softer where you are too hard. If most people are against you, you can stand alone without fear. If you have to leave a whole world behind, you can go without sorrow.

Open your mouth and say plainly what you are carrying, and people will be glad to help you with it. Stand like someone who chose the load. Lake over Wind is the hexagram of carrying more than you were built to hold. Wind is the quiet strength in you that holds things up. Lake is the part of you that draws people in and stirs them to act. The gathering sits above the holding because what you take on grows faster than what carries it. This hexagram has long been read as a lake risen over the trees. Water feeds a tree until there is too much of it. Too much of what you love can do the same to you. When what you care about grows bigger than your life can hold, you have to move. Great Preponderance
fields.gene_keys:
Purposelessness Totality Immortality Totality is living alongside fear instead of running from it. You stay open to every change and still keep your commitments. You take in the whole of life, the pleasure with the pain, and you stop letting your mind run your days. You trust life enough to follow the story without knowing how it ends.

Life becomes a play, and you have a part in it. Lover or fool, you play your part all the way. Under the giving you find a strange calm, which is the reward for holding nothing back. Each fear you accept leaves you lighter, and hard times get a lighter touch. The demons you face turn out to be angels in disguise. As your own worries settle, your energy turns toward other people. One fear sits under every fear you have, and it is the fear of dying. Where getting through life is no longer in doubt, it changes clothes. It becomes the fear that none of it means anything. Most lives are built so that this fear never has to be looked at. It comes in three layers, and the first is the fear of living. Then comes a panic about dying some time after forty. Last comes the fear that you will die without really living. That last one is the fear that finally moves you.

Avoiding it is a dance around an empty hole, and you can dance for years. A fixed set of beliefs numbs the fear, because the mind hates surprises. Your body knows two older answers: a loving hand on your belly, and a breath that goes deeper than the fear. The body is not afraid to die. Only the fear is. There are moments when time stops, and in them you have no fear of death at all. The mind pictures living forever as more and more time, which is the one thing it cannot be. The present is so full that you stop waiting for the next moment. Picture the end of a great play. The actors and the crowd have gone, the lights are out, and you are still in your seat before the empty stage. That is the part of you that was there before the play began and is there after it ends. It watches, listens and breathes. It wakes through a life lived wholly, even a life wholly miserable. Near someone who lives here, your own fears come up to be seen.
fields.human_design: Adventure and Challenge Gate 28 drives you to struggle for a life that means something. It goes toward the hard thing to find out what the struggle is for. It will change a whole life, the work or the country, to get nearer the answer. Its fear is that the road will be too hard and end in failure, so why begin. That fear can hold you still for years. A hard thing is not a failure. Lived through, it becomes a story worth telling, and other people find their own meaning in it.
fields.tarot: Purpose runs out when it waits for a later day. It belongs to the Ring of Illusion, two energies that share your fear of death. Its one sibling is UL 32, Art of Living, which carries the fear of dying before you have done what you came for. Open it when you notice you are saving your life for later. Five of the tarot's major cards, its Arcana, arrive through the ring and the two trigrams.
fields.body:
Fear is the reason this energy is given to your kidneys. They keep the store you have from birth, and a life spends it without making more. Each kidney holds about a million tiny filters, all there at birth, and no new ones are made after it. The fear that life has no point and the fear of running out are one fear, kept in one place. It stays quiet for as long as you spend the store on something that matters.

They lie high at your back, one on each side of the spine, under the last ribs. Put your hands on your waist behind you with the thumbs forward, and your fingers are over them. You will feel nothing through the muscle, though on a deep breath in they slide down a little. One kidney is enough for a whole life. You are resting your hands on the part of you that was full at birth and holds more than one life needs. Your sense of purpose has a chemistry, and one substance in it is asparaginic acid. Your body makes it for itself from what is left when food is burned, so you never have to eat it. It is part of every protein in your body. Its share of the fear is the fear of death itself. In your body it is there when you put your life off for a later year that you hope will mean more. It is there too when you give a moment everything and feel the calm underneath. One other energy in you shares this substance and the same fear of death.

keywords: A Hand Kept on the Door

fields.essence: Everything you have, given to one thing before you can see where it leads: that is this energy, the whole yes. In you it is the moment a decision stops being weighed and becomes a road you are already on. It rises low, below thinking, as a quiet warmth that moves through the whole of you without arguing. Once it has risen the giving is no longer an effort; it carries you. In a life this is the work or the person you have gone all the way into.
fields.glance:
Everything you have, given to one thing before you can see where it leads: that is this energy, the whole yes. In you it is the moment a decision stops being weighed and becomes a road you are already on. It rises low, below thinking, as a quiet warmth that moves through the whole of you without arguing. Once it has risen the giving is no longer an effort; it carries you. In a life this is the work or the person you have gone all the way into.

The whole yes is honesty first. You cannot know where a decision goes, nobody can, and the only thing that travels with you is how whole you were when you began. A thing begun whole makes its own luck; a thing begun with one hand on the door makes the other kind. The yes has a length of its own, a night or a life, and when it is over you feel that where you felt it begin. Your part is to stay through the hard middle, where it is tested, then to leave cleanly when it is done, rather than a little before or long after.

Hold nothing back. Keep one part of yourself out of the thing, for safety, and the yes is not a little smaller; it is gone. Most of what you keep back is fear that was never looked at. Look at it once, then give the rest.
fields.iching:
You are in danger, and it is not the kind that comes once. There is a drop below you, and under that drop another, so the comfort that hard times pass does not hold here. What holds is that the same danger comes back until you have learned it, the way a young bird falls until its wings carry. What it asks is the way of water. Water does not shrink from any fall. It goes down, fills the low place to the brim, and when the place is full it goes on, still water after every pit, having lost nothing of itself. Go all the way into the thing, and keep to what you are.

What carries you through is the firm line in the middle, the heart kept true while everything round it gives way. Held with a true heart, even this goes through, and what you do from it has worth. Danger is not only what you fall into; it is what keeps a city safe, the mountain no army crosses, the river at the wall, and there is a time when it is the thing to use. Keep to the ones who bring what they have plainly, and let the grand rescuers pass.

In the body this energy is the ear, the one part of you that cannot be shut: it hears in the dark and it hears in your sleep. Notice what you are listening for now. Sit low, as water sits, and listen for the way through rather than looking for it. Water over Water: a river through a gorge, and under it the gorge again, one drop below another. The water falls into the first pit, fills it to the brim, spills into the next, and none of the falling changes what it is. The traditional character shows earth opened into a hollow; the word set beside it, to repeat, shows a young bird beating its wings until they hold. The Abysmal Water
fields.gene_keys:
Half-Heartedness Commitment Devotion Commitment, when it is real, feels nothing like excitement. It is not nervous and it does not shout. A clear decision settles in you the way a river settles into its bed. From then on you do not have to think about the goal, because the decision has the goal inside it, and only time will show where the river goes. What matters is not arriving but following it to its end. Cycles run inside cycles, some five minutes long, some a lifetime, and a life is the shape of a million small ones, so the same wholeness goes into washing a dish as into a night of love. A commitment like this lasts as long as it lasts. When it is over, both of you feel it at the same time, and what began clean ends clean. The length has nothing to do with success.

Nobody can give you the yes, no teacher, no system; it comes up from the belly and does not argue. Held whole, it rides out any storm, because it was never about the other person. It was about leaping with your eyes open. Half-heartedness is a yes with something kept back, and from inside it feels like good sense. You go into the work or the person, and a part of you stays outside it, in case. That is not caution. It is a dishonesty practised on yourself, and a life that is being lied to withdraws. The days go dull or go frantic, and you stand at the side of your own life, watching. It hides in postponing. You have a picture of how things should go, life fails to match it, and you take yourself out of the present to run ahead in your head, missing the only moment you were ever in. It hides in quitting at the first hard weather, and in not knowing when to stop a thing that hurts. Both come from a fear you never went into. Break off a cycle before its end and life builds the same one again, from different people, until you finish it. Look back and you can see them, the same trouble wearing different faces, each one left before it was done. Devotion is commitment with no one left holding it. You were always devoted to something; everyone is, the mother to her child, even the sad to their sadness, and this is that same pouring with the object gone. First it fixes on one thing, a face or a cause, and worships it without caution; people call that blind. Then the love poured out begins pouring back, from everything, until the rocks and the trees seem to bleed it toward you. There is no worshipper left, only what was loved.

Whoever comes near this catches it. It is nearly impossible to say no to someone like this, and they care nothing for the rules, only for the heart, which knows none. To be devoted is to lie forever in the lap of what you love.
fields.human_design:
Perseverance The pull to say yes and stay is this energy's pressure in the body. Gate 29 is the door it comes through, the drive that gives the whole of you to a thing and keeps on when the first excitement is gone. It says yes easily. Every yes you give has weight, every no as well, because each one sets the shape of the years after it. When the yes was the body's, you are the one still there when the others have left, and people build on you.

The trouble built in is the same drive saying yes to too much, or to the wrong thing out of a fear of saying no, so that you are held to a promise you had no strength for, and devotion turns into obligation. From outside it looks like stubbornness, or like someone who cannot plan past tonight; what is going on is that the yes came before the seeing, and you trusted it. People who carry this all their lives learn that the yes they can keep is the one that came from below the neck, and that the way to keep it is to give fewer of them.
fields.tarot: Within the Ring of Union, this code is the power of the full yes. Its siblings, UL 4, 7, and 59, carry the rest of the family: the not-yet-knowing, the inner guidance, and the breaking of barriers between people. Bound by a single amino acid, they are the chemistry of how humans come together, the ring most alive right now in how we bond and relate. Two axes carry the Tarot into this water. The codon ring gives the Lovers, choice and union, the moment a person commits to another and to a path. Both trigrams are water, so the trigram axis speaks once, doubled: the High Priestess who waits and perceives, and the Hanged Man who hangs in suspension and sees the situation from below. The Lovers, the High Priestess and the Hanged Man point one way here: the full yes is made from a still, surrendered place rather than a thrashing one.
fields.body:
Your body's yes is kept in the sacral plexus, a weave of nerves on the inner face of the bone at the base of your spine, and the reason is that it answers before you do. The engine that does your work is seated here, and it does not decide. Something is put in front of you, a sound comes up before a thought, and that sound is the only yes your body keeps its word to. Say yes from the head to a thing this place had no yes for, and you pay for it here; it is your body that gives out, not your plan.

Stand up from your chair. The order to the great muscle at the back of your hip, and to the ones that kept you level as the weight moved, went out from this weave before you had finished deciding to rise. Try to catch the moment you chose. You cannot, and that is the part of you this energy is given to: the whole of you going, with the deciding left behind. The yes you give whole has a substance in you, and the substance is valine. Your body cannot make it; it arrives in meat or lentils, or not at all, and turned from the water, it is folded into the inside of every protein you build. The part of you kept back is made of the same substance. What you keep from someone you love is kept below words, in your chemistry, out of fear. Down there a yes that keeps back one part in a hundred is the same as one that keeps back all but one.

Three other things in you share this substance; it is the same in all four. In you it is the yes said to life itself, with no promise about where it goes, since the only promise your body can keep is to what it is being led to now.

fields.essence: Passion is alive in you as heat, and you feel it first in your stomach. When something catches you, your whole body leans toward it. A spark is enough to set you blazing. Your wants make your days bright. People are drawn to that warmth, and your passion wakes theirs.
fields.glance:
Passion is alive in you as heat, and you feel it first in your stomach. When something catches you, your whole body leans toward it. A spark is enough to set you blazing. Your wants make your days bright. People are drawn to that warmth, and your passion wakes theirs.

Some wants take hold, and your mind fans them the way wind fans a flame. Your body needs food and sleep, but most wants are for things you could live without. In the heat of it, a want feels like a need. Sometimes you follow one to the end and find it cost more than it gave. Forgive yourself, because you needed to learn it.

Feel every want all the way, and follow the few that matter most. A want is neither holy nor wicked, so there is nothing to feel guilty about. You can enjoy the pull of it and still know it will pass. Held like this, passion stops weighing on you, and you move through your days lighter.
fields.iching:
Something has lit you up, and the question is what you are holding on to. Everything that shines or grows holds to something, the sun to the sky and the grain to the ground. Your fire lasts only as long as what it burns. Hold to what is true, and your light goes a long way.

What it asks is gentleness with your own strength. The old counsel is to raise a cow, and like a cow you can be strong without pushing. Tend the light in you before you spend it. No fire burns without fuel, and yours comes from the people and the world around you. So stay close to them.

Your heart is where this fire is kept. Light it first, and let its warmth reach the people nearest you. From there it reaches the four corners of the world. Fire over Fire is the hexagram of what your light holds on to. Fire below is the warmth in you, the part that feels and wants. Fire above is the clarity in you, the part that sees what is worth wanting. The seeing sits above the wanting because a flame lasts only as long as what it burns. Fire has long been read as clinging, since a flame has no shape of its own. It takes the shape of the wood it is on. What you hold on to is what your light becomes. The Clinging Fire
fields.gene_keys:
Desire Lightness Rapture Lightness comes when you stop fighting and say to life: all right, do your worst. What gives way then is your distrust, the sense that life is against you. You see the joke, that things had to go the way they went, and you see your own place in the story. From then on there is a glint in your eye.

Wants still come and go. Each one is a guest you ask in for tea, and it either leaves in its own time or stays until it is followed. Either way, you know no want will bring you lasting peace, so it has lost its hold. You laugh at yourself first. Real lightness is never afraid of being swept away by a feeling. Desire is a hunger that has left the stomach and gone out into the world. It is a hunger for experience itself, for every taste there is, the bitter ones too. It is not for anything in particular. You are built to yearn, and what you reach for is never the point. The moment you are full, you are empty again, and the yearning starts over.

The suffering comes from what you do against it. Fight the wanting and it grows. Call it unholy and it grows faster. So most people neither give in nor let go, because both are too frightening, and they live half-heartedly in between. The fire itself is not the trouble. The war with it is. Rapture is the one longing left when all the others have burned down into it. Under the thousands of wants that pass through you each day, one grows stronger. It is the longing to be free of suffering and to go back to where you came from. Step into it willingly, and you give up everything, even the wish to be free. You become your longing, and in that you feel you belong in the world.

Then bliss burns you, over and over. It is so close to the surface that whoever comes near you is likely to catch it.
fields.human_design:
Passion Gate 30 sits in the belly and carries the wish to feel everything, together with the fear of feeling it. It is the most intense gate there is, and it turns up whatever else you carry. It drives you toward a dream you can feel, strong enough to live by. You can hold that dream a long time and bring it into form.

The risk is burnout, and it is often learned young, from leaping the moment the heat rises. So the drive asks you to know which dream is worth the fuel. Wait for the right time to share it. Fed by devotion, a passion lasts for years. Keep your own flame, and it stays lit for the long road.
fields.tarot: This fire burns off what it feeds on, and it cannot do the burning alone. It belongs to a family of two, the Ring of Purification, and the other is Universal Crest. There, the force of wanting meets the ability to listen to what the past has taught. Open it when your wanting keeps making the same mistake. Three of the tarot's major cards, its Arcana, come to this energy through its ring and its two fires.
fields.body:
Your body gives this energy to the solar plexus, and the reason is hunger. The solar plexus is a knot of nerves behind your stomach, the largest of its kind. Its fibres run out in every direction like the rays of a sun. In front of it is the soft hollow under your breastbone, the pit of the stomach. Miss a meal by an hour, and the pang arrives right there, whether you meant to eat or not. Your fear arrives in the same place. So your body feels a want before you have decided anything about it.

Lay a hand flat in that hollow and take a sharp breath in. It pushes out against your hand, then falls back as you let the breath go. About a hand's depth behind your palm is the part of you that wants first. When you give in to a strong want, it runs through you like a fire, and your body feels it first. That fire has a chemistry in you, and one substance in it is glutamine. Your body makes it for itself, in your muscles. Your body builds its proteins from twenty small pieces, and your blood carries more of this one than of any other. It carries what is left of a burnt protein safely out of the muscle to where it can be let go.

Follow every want and you often feel low afterwards, and part of that low is this chemistry. The same substance is in you when you listen as when you burn. Your fire burns to make you clean. As your longing grows stronger, your body begins to fill with light.

fields.essence: Sometimes everyone in a room feels the same thing, and nobody says it. You sense it before anyone speaks. When you say it, they recognise what they felt and could not put into words. You have no wish to lead, and that is why they trust you.
fields.glance:
Sometimes everyone in a room feels the same thing, and nobody says it. You sense it before anyone speaks. When you say it, they recognise what they felt and could not put into words. You have no wish to lead, and that is why they trust you.

Some days you speak to be seen, and the words go hollow. When you notice it, stop talking and listen again. Then ask what would help the people in front of you.

Listen before you speak. Let people see you make mistakes, because they follow the most human person in the room. Choose each word with care, because words go on working long after they are said. Said at the right moment, one plain sentence of yours can turn a whole room.
fields.iching:
You and someone else are drawn to each other, and neither of you has moved yet. The other side may be a person, or a piece of work that has caught hold of you. What this time asks is that you receive rather than reach. Chase someone and they back away. Stay open and still, and they come to you in their own time. Give more than you are given, and you end up with more.

Every attraction has a strain in it, and that strain carries the feeling across. Once you know the feeling is true, commit to it. What you put in is what you get back.

Your body feels it first, as a stir that climbs from your toes to your mouth. Stand still with your face open, and let what is coming come to you. Lake over Mountain is the hexagram of two people drawn to each other. Lake is the part of you that opens up, smiles and answers. Mountain is the part of you that stays still and does not reach. The openness rests on the stillness because only someone who is not grabbing can be moved. This hexagram has long been read as a lake on top of a mountain. A proud peak holds no water, but a hollow at the top holds a whole lake. It works the same way between you and a crowd. Let people move you, and you will move them. Influence
fields.gene_keys:
Arrogance Leadership Humility Being followed happens to people who are not looking for it. You have an ear for what people are about to feel, and you can say it in words they understand. What moves them is the feeling behind the words. A thing said at the right time reaches much further than what it says.

You use what you know about how people are led to lead them out of traps you were once caught in. To speak for what is new, you first learn the language of what came before. It asks for patience with your own mistakes. It asks for the quieter courage to stay with what you know is true while people misread you. You will fall where everyone can see, and you get up with your heart still open. That is what people follow. The need to be recognised grows out of feeling unsure of yourself. The less sure you are, the more you look to others to tell you who you are. One kind is loud: the one who knows best and makes sure you know it. The bully is always the least sure person in the room. Another kind is quiet and harder to spot, the calm certainty of having found the right way while others have not. Both hold on to the words and lose the feeling behind them.

The strange thing is that you cannot see it in yourself. Look for it and the part of you doing the looking is the part that hides it. It shows only when you fall in front of people. Sooner or later life arranges that fall for everyone. What anyone thinks of you stops mattering, and nothing about it is gentle. A soft voice and a lowered head are often pride in disguise. This comes when life has stripped you to the bone and you stopped minding. You would not even mind being thought proud. You leave the world as it is.

You say what has to be said, knowing the words came from everyone and go back to everyone. Where they land is not your concern. You fell where everyone could see, and this time you stayed down. It is quiet down here. From the ground you can look up and laugh.
fields.human_design:
Leading Gate 31 sits in the throat and presses you to speak for a group. It says what the group has felt and not yet said. It works only when you are called into it. Take it for yourself and the voice loses its power. The moment your own wanting steps in front of the group, people stop hearing you.

From outside this can look like ambition or like hiding. It fails in two ways: pushing forward to be approved of, or shrinking back for fear of not being heard. Called, it listens first, and people follow what you heard in them.
fields.tarot: This energy moves people with words, and it cannot take back what it says. It belongs to a family of two, the Ring of No Return, whose theme is words that cannot be unsaid. Its one kin is UL 62, Voice of Nature, which finds the exact word for you. This one gives you the word that turns a room. Five of the tarot's major cards, its Arcana, show this energy in faces you may already know.
fields.body:
This energy is given to your throat, and the reason is the air. Your voice is air taken from the room and sent back into it through two closed folds, with your shape on it. The shape is the only part that is yours. It is the one thing your body makes that reaches inside another person across a room. That is what influence is in the body: something taken in and given back. When your throat is easy, the words go out on the breath. When it is tight, you are pushing air, and people hear the push.

Say a long sentence out loud and notice where it stops. It stops where the breath ran out. You cannot say a word on the breath in. What you say is made from what you took in first. When you speak from the heart, the words come out in order before you have thought about what they mean. That has a substance in you, and the substance is tyrosine. It is one of the twenty your body is built from. Your body makes it from another one you must eat, and meat, eggs and beans carry it too. From it your body makes what wakes you up and gets you moving, and the colour of your skin, hair and eyes. The sentence that leaves you before you choose it is made from the same substance as the colour of your eyes.

The word that forms in your head when you look at a tree runs on this substance too. So do the words you follow and the words you lead with. Cut an apple and leave it on the table, and it turns brown. A close relative of what made your colour does the browning. It goes on working in the open air, as a word does once it has left you.

fields.essence: When the newness of something has worn off, the long middle begins. A feeling for what will last comes alive in you here. You can tell which plans and friendships have a future in them before you could say why. You know what to keep and what to let go.
fields.glance:
When the newness of something has worn off, the long middle begins. A feeling for what will last comes alive in you here. You can tell which plans and friendships have a future in them before you could say why. You know what to keep and what to let go.

Some days a quiet panic runs under everything. You rush from one task to the next toward a rest that never comes, and underneath it is the fear of failing. Slow down inside the rush, and it loosens its grip. An ending met with grace is never a failure.

This is the art of living: to take your time with things and enjoy more of your days. Let people in, even when it hurts, because being opened is what makes you rich. Ask what you want to leave behind, and give your days to that. Lived this way, an ordinary life becomes something worth handing on.
fields.iching:
You are in something for the long haul now. The start is behind you, and what matters is how you keep it going. You may be carrying more than was ever fairly yours. The way to bear it is to keep changing inside while you stand firm on the outside.

Bear the hard days with dignity, and the good ones with humility. Change yourself, and leave others to change in their own time, since forcing it on someone is oppressive. Look for allies who are least like you, because a bond between different people holds the longest. Keep a direction, since it helps to have somewhere to go.

Your legs do the work now: the feet that carry you forward and the thighs that bear the weight. Stand the way someone stands through a long day, with feet planted and knees soft. Thunder over Wind is the hexagram of lasting, of how a thing goes on once it has begun. Thunder is the part of you that stirs things up and acts where others can see. Wind is the part of you that works quietly underneath and never stops. The stirring sits on top because what lasts needs action on the outside and patience within. Thunder and wind have long been read as a couple married for years. One of the two makes the moves the world sees, while the other keeps the home going. Your life lasts the way the seasons do, by changing as it goes. What lasts in you is one bold part and one patient part working together. Duration
fields.gene_keys:
Failure Preservation Veneration Keeping things alive is what this energy becomes, and its whole art is choosing which things deserve to go on. You sense the long run of a situation. You can hold your energy or your money back from what tempts you but would not serve. You trust a feeling about someone that no reason supports, and it proves right. The balance is between holding back and taking a chance. The one who buries his coin for fear of losing it loses it.

The craft is grafting. You keep the old rootstock, the part that has proved strong, and set the young shoot onto it. Then one day you see that what you fought to preserve was never the real thing, and its shell cracks. You can plant a few trees every day around your home, lose most of them, and keep planting through wars and changes of government. In time you stand in a forest where the ground was bare, with villages living off it. Whether or not anyone learns your name, you will know. Failing, deep in the body, means being cut off. Long before you, the people you come from learned that to be pushed out of the group was to die. That lesson is still in you. Today the fear has moved into money. The bigger the number, the safer you feel. Yet it never settles, because fear always needs something to feed on. Take the money away and it would find the next thing. Close beside it is the fear that your family line will end, with no one to hand anything to.

The fear made people stingy in spirit, keeping to their own small circle, and it kept the species alive while it did. It lives deep in the body, and the mind feeds it by telling its story again. Let go into the way life moves, and you find the support was there all along. Reverence is what remains once the fear has burned away. You see your place in the long chain of living things, with lives behind you and lives still to come. You look at it with no self in the way, so all that is left is wonder. You stand on the shoulders of those who came before, and you offer your shoulders to whoever comes next. Even the smallest insect is holding you up. You feel tiny and huge in the same breath. Wisdom lives in one person for a while, then moves on to the next who can hold it. The one discipline it asks is to pause and listen inward.
fields.human_design:
Endurance Gate 32 is a sense of what will last, and it sits in the Spleen Center. It reads a plan, a job or a friendship for whether it has a future, and it usually knows before you could explain. Growth under it comes in cycles rather than leaps, because real change takes time. The drive is to prepare, to set the stage so you are ready when the moment comes, without dragging it closer.

The fear of failing presses from the same place. It can stop you from trying at all, or from preparing, so you are not ready when the time is right. It can also push you too hard, too fast, for too long. The line to find is between holding on and clinging.
fields.tarot: This energy keeps a life going, and under it lies an old fear of dying before that life has been lived. It belongs with one other card in the Ring of Illusion, whose theme is the fears that look solid until you face them. UL 28, Becoming the Mystery, carries the fear of death itself. This one carries the fear of failing to live well. Five of the tarot's major cards arrive through the ring and the two trigrams, each a turn your life can take.
fields.body:
Keeping is the reason this energy is given to the spleen. Your blood passes through it many times a day, and it sorts what it finds. It retires what is worn out and keeps what still serves. A red cell lives about four months, and most of them end here, taken apart. Their iron is kept and sent back to be built into new cells, so your body loses almost none of it. The red in your blood today was carried by cells long gone. In the old medicine the spleen holds the blood inside its vessels and moves the water through you. It also turns what you eat into what you live on.

It sits high under your left ribs, behind the stomach, about the size of a fist. Look at the pink under your fingernails. That colour is iron your spleen has kept for you, cell after cell, for years. Keeping what matters has a chemistry in you, and one substance in it is asparaginic acid. The letters your body is written in are partly built from it. Joined to one other piece, it is the sweetener printed on a can of diet drink. In a body that keeps and counts, the fear of death and the worry about money run together, older than any bank account.

What is yours in it is the fear of dying with your life unlived. The same chemistry holds the old root and the young shoot, what has lasted for generations with the new set onto it. You share this chemistry with one other energy, the one that fears the ending itself.

fields.essence: After anything big, you need time on your own to look back at it. Mindfulness is alive in you here: you go over it quietly until you can see what it was about. Even your mistakes have something to teach you once you see them from a distance.
fields.glance:
After anything big, you need time on your own to look back at it. Mindfulness is alive in you here: you go over it quietly until you can see what it was about. Even your mistakes have something to teach you once you see them from a distance.

The hard part is the pace of life, with the next thing always coming at you, so the days go by without a second look. The people near you may read your quiet as distance. Take the time anyway, let the bad hours go, and forgive yourself for them.

Give part of every day to what has just gone by, even if it is only a cup of tea drunk slowly. Ask what was best about yesterday and let yourself feel it again. Talk it over with a friend, and you will both feel closer. Wait to tell your story until it can lift the person who hears it. Then what you have lived becomes something you can give.
fields.iching:
Something smaller than you has been gaining ground for a while, and arguing will not stop it. Staying to fight spends your strength on ground that is already going. So leave while leaving is still your choice. This is not running away. You decide how far and how fast, and you go with what is yours.

Keep your distance from what is small, and do not hate it, because hating would tie you to it. Be firm, and carry no bitterness out the door. In small things, keep doing what is right. Knowing when to step back is the hardest call there is. A step back at the right hour often turns out to be the way forward.
