In the body this is the head and the hand. The hand below has put the work down, and the head above stays clear. Let the hand rest, keep your head up, and go. Heaven over Mountain is the hexagram of knowing when to step back. Heaven is the strength in you that keeps moving forward. Mountain is the part of you that knows where to stop. The stopping sits below the strength because a strength that never stops wears itself out. This hexagram has long been read as a mountain under a sky that is drawing away. A person who leaves in good time takes all of their strength with them. It is a time when something smaller has begun to gain ground, the way the days shorten after midsummer. You keep what matters by stepping back before you are pushed. Retreat
fields.gene_keys:
Forgetting Mindfulness Revelation Mindfulness starts the day you catch yourself in the middle of a heated argument and see that you have forgotten who you are. You still hide or react, and now you can watch yourself doing it. For a while that is harder than sleeping, because now you feel every repeat. The patterns seem to grow stronger the nearer you come to the end of them. They are not stronger; you are more awake. Nothing you do can hurry this, and the watching is all you can lean on.

Then the trees open into a clearing. There is light and a place to sit, and from there you can see the path you have been walking. Sit down in it for a while. From here you can make something out of what you feel, because you can see it without drowning in it. Your best work happens when you are out of its way. Forgetting is how a life goes when there is never a pause in it. Your eyes stay on what is coming, the next message or the next job. You rarely look at where you have just been. So you walk through the forest head down and cross each clearing without stopping. You miss what was waiting there, a sunrise or a stranger. The same argument comes round again, and each time it feels new. Life starts to feel hard in a way you cannot name.

The memories you carry keep you in the pattern, and every wish you have seems to add another. One wish loosens it: the wish to remember who you are. The people you cannot get free of help you most, the ones you feel you have known from somewhere, loved and fought with in turns. Stay with them, and they wake you up. Everyone forgets in this way, even though forgetting leaves each person feeling separate and alone. Revelation comes to you as silence, the way autumn comes to a forest. Your life turns brighter as it lets go, the way leaves do before they fall, and your attention turns inward. All that you were is forgotten, and all that you could be is remembered. The past no longer stands between you and this moment. Here you have no more to tell, and if you speak at all, it is to say that.

Your story is coming to its end. Part of you does not want it to end, and the greater part is ready to let go. Fall in love with your own story and follow it without holding anything back. It will reach its end, and no one else's will be like it.
fields.human_design: Retelling Gate 33 sits in the throat and pushes you to step back from the world after something has happened. You go off alone to go over it and gather your thoughts, and this is not hiding. Then you come back and share what you found, with a depth you could not have had before. The people near you may take the distance for coldness, so say plainly that you need the time. Its risk is going over the past too long, alone, until it turns to worry. When it runs well, your story lifts whoever hears it. When it runs badly, you tell a story of pain that keeps you and your listener stuck where you were.
fields.tarot: This energy looks back, and looking back is where waking up begins. It belongs to a family of three, the Ring of Trials, whose theme is the tests on the way to knowing who you are. UL 56, Infinite Journey, carries the test of being pulled away by your senses. UL 12, Petals of Freedom, carries the last test of meeting who you really are. This one carries the first: seeing that you have forgotten. Four of the tarot's major cards, its Arcana, arrive through the ring and the two trigrams.
fields.body:
This energy is given to your throat because you hear your own voice from inside. Everyone else hears your voice through the air. You hear it by a second road as well, through the bones of your own head, which carry the low notes best. So the voice you have heard all your life is the one from within. A recording of it sounds thin and high, like a stranger's. Your life is the same: only you have heard it from inside. A gland below your voice stores two to three months of what it makes, so what runs you today was made a while ago.

Block both ears with your fingers and say a few words. Your voice sounds louder and deeper, because the road through the air is shut and only the one through the bone is left. What you hear then is the part of your voice that nobody else has ever heard. No substance in you answers to this energy. It is a mark in the code you are written in, one of three that name nothing. Where your body's reading reaches it, the reading stops. The written message runs on past it, and only the reading ends there. When these marks come alive in you, they begin to unplug you from the world your senses show. Past every stop in you, another beginning is written further on. Something starts where you come to an end.

This energy is the first of three such stops in you. Only the strength of your own dissatisfaction can shake you out of sleep, and it begins at this first stop.

fields.essence: You feel strong, and something real in front of you is asking for all of it. That is when strength moves through your whole body. You can work hard all day with nothing in you pulling against the work. The work flows out of you, and you become one with it.
fields.glance:
You feel strong, and something real in front of you is asking for all of it. That is when strength moves through your whole body. You can work hard all day with nothing in you pulling against the work. The work flows out of you, and you become one with it.

Some days there is nothing real to meet, and the strength goes looking for something to push. You lean on things that will not move and want them to go your way. Listen for the word try in your own voice, because it comes just as the pushing starts. Once you hear it, stop, and the strain goes out of your body.

Let the strength rest until something real calls it. You will know the call, because the strength rises on its own, with no talking yourself into it. Take the way that feels easy, since the easy way is the right one. Then all of you goes in, and the whole of life is behind you.
fields.iching:
Your strength has grown to its full height. The time of holding back is over, and you are ready to act on what is worth it. There is more power in you now than in anything around you. This is also where the danger lies. People with this much strength grow too sure of themselves and start to run wild. Great power draws envy from those who have less.

Use only as much strength as the moment needs. Never strike before you can strike at full strength, and never out of pride. Be fair with what you have, because only the weak are merciless. Strength spent on a cause nobody else supports is wasted. Put it behind what is right, and good people will stand with you.

Thunder belongs to the foot, the first part of you to move. Stand with your weight even over both feet. Let the strength settle there before you take a step. Thunder over Heaven is the hexagram of strength at its full height. Heaven is the steady strength inside you. Thunder is the urge in you to move, and to move now. The urge sits on top because once your strength is full, it wants to be used. This hexagram has long been read as thunder high in the sky. When your strength is this full, people feel it the way they feel thunder overhead. The same reading asks you to walk no road that is not right. You are strongest when your strength goes only where it should. Great Power
fields.gene_keys:
Force Strength Majesty Strength has always wanted to be seen. A flower opens its colour to bring the bee, and there is no pride in it. Your strength shows in the same way, and people notice it without being told. Someone who moves and speaks from their centre has a strength you can feel across a room.

You may do a brave thing without deciding to, then feel uneasy when people praise you for it. It seems to have happened through you. Your movement is at its finest once you stop watching yourself. Often this strength means not moving at all. The easiest fight is the one you never start. Real strength is not aware of itself. Force is the oldest power in you. It is older than any animal, and it has one aim, to keep one life going. It does not even know that anyone else is there. Caught in it, you keep going the way you set out, and help from outside falls on deaf ears. Other people cannot see how you could be so blind. Their anger takes you by surprise, because you had no idea what you were doing.

Your spine feels it first. Each time you push your life where it does not want to go, your back tightens somewhere and you begin to stoop. Go to the ache and stay with it, instead of fixing it from outside. It is there because of something you are doing or not doing. The longer you listen, the plainer it says where your life wants to go. Majesty is life moving through a body with no one in there taking charge. On a crowded train, an old man calms a raging drunk by asking about his garden, while a trained fighter sits ready to strike. At this height you settle a fight the way that old man did, without lifting a hand.

Majesty is hidden and humble, and it always finds the easiest way. A god living in a human body would not know it is one. Then the whole of life moves through you, and you are joy in a body.
fields.human_design: Power Gate 34 is the pressure to put your great store of energy to use. It can keep you busier than anyone around you. It gives you the stamina to keep going long after others stop. It is built to answer, not to start. When something real comes to you and your yes rises, the energy brings the right people together around one idea, and what you start lasts. When nothing has come, you stay busy to feel in control. All that work leaves you feeling powerless. The pressure asks you to carry the power rather than wield it.
fields.tarot: This strength is the power of the body, and it has already done its greatest work by standing the human spine upright. It belongs to a family of two, the Ring of Destiny, which shapes where a life goes. UL 43, Cipher of Knowledge, carries the sudden knowing that breaks through your mind. This one carries the strength of the body. Together they are two halves of one destiny. Your strength shows up in five of the tarot's major cards, its Arcana.
fields.body:
This strength is given to the sacral plexus, and the reason is that nothing in you is watched less. The plexus is a weave of nerves against the inside of the flat bone at the base of your spine. It sits low, below and around the level of your navel. Strength comes from here, from the belly, while pushing starts in the head. Its power is real because no thought sits on it.

Stand up from a chair. The big muscle of your buttock straightened your hip on an order from this weave, before you had finished deciding to stand. The muscles that kept your hips level took their orders from it too. You felt none of it, and that is how this strength works. The strength in you has a chemistry, and one substance in it is asparagine. Your body makes it for itself from what it already has, so it asks nothing of your plate. The proteins on the outside of every cell you have wear their coats of sugar on it.

When the strength takes you over and you can hear no one, this chemistry is part of what is moving. Left alone, your life runs smoothly and costs you little. Each push against the way it wants to go uses more of your energy than the flow would have. You share this chemistry with one other energy.

fields.essence: Life is opening up, and you want more of it. That wanting is your sense of adventure, the pull toward whatever you have not tried yet. You do not have to travel far for it. The streets around your own door hold enough to fill a lifetime, once you meet them as new each time. The same walk is never the same walk twice.
fields.glance:
Life is opening up, and you want more of it. That wanting is your sense of adventure, the pull toward whatever you have not tried yet. You do not have to travel far for it. The streets around your own door hold enough to fill a lifetime, once you meet them as new each time. The same walk is never the same walk twice.

Some days you want everything now, and the wanting gets ahead of you. Impatience and appetite feed each other until nothing you reach for is tasted. Stop just before the edge, the way a glass of wine is best a sip short of too much. When you overshoot, be as kind to yourself as to anyone driven by hunger.

Do the things you already do in a new way. Learn the name of the person who serves you in the shop. When someone starts talking to you in the middle of your work, stop and give them your whole attention. Life comes closer when you pause for it, and every ordinary day holds an adventure.
fields.iching:
Things are going well. What you started is growing on its own, like young plants in full sun, and other people can see it. People want you around, ask you back and trust you with more. The old picture is a lord at ease, given many horses by his king and received three times in one day. None of it was seized.

What it asks is that you rise the way he rose. Serve the people above you with loyalty and the people below you with generosity. Advance quietly, like a mouse, and take your seat when it is offered. Be willing to change before you ask anything around you to change. A good run is the easiest time to overreach, so save some of what comes and stay kind to the people who helped you. Every time of rising passes.

This time shows in your eyes: you look up, and you take in more than you did an hour ago. Hold yourself the way the sun comes up, without hurry, lighting each thing it reaches. Fire over Earth is the hexagram of rising in the world with ease. Fire is the clarity in you that lets people see what you are good at. Earth is the willingness in you to serve and to follow. The clarity sits above the willingness because you rise when the good you do quietly becomes plain to others. This hexagram has long been read as the sun coming up over the earth. A morning shows each thing more clearly by the minute, and nobody has to push it. You rise most easily when you let the good in you be seen and serve the people around you. Progress
fields.gene_keys:
Hunger Adventure Boundlessness Adventure is the hunger with love in it. Love here is not one person filling you for a while. It is the feeling of being joined to everything, and it is the only thing that ends the hunger. The reach turns inward, and what changes now is you. There is still some fear in you, but you stand high enough to outwit it.

Most of us keep our lives in sealed rooms: the job that never touches the marriage, the belief that lets no new idea in. Open one door between two of them and new people walk through. The easiest way to change your life is to give without asking anything back, in as many places as you dare. People stop short when you do it, and something opens in you. A hunger runs through every person, and nothing out in the world ends it. You do not know what you want, only that you want it now. While it has hold of you, you cannot think about the cost. So you reach out for food or a new person, and soon after you are full the emptiness comes back. Then comes the mistake. Either you cling to what filled you, or you blame it for failing and move on.

Whatever you reach for outside leaves you hungrier than before. Starving the hunger does not end it, and neither does stuffing it. What loosens its grip is to feel, with all of you, how completely it drives you. Once you see that, the reach stops pouring out into the world and turns back inside. Boundlessness is the state in which you no longer feel separate from anything. There is nowhere left to reach, because you are part of everything you once reached for. The fear that gave the adventure its edge falls away too. The mind cannot hold this, but the heart can, and the heart treats love and awareness as the same thing. A child already lives this way, and to a child anything is possible. Near a love like this, what seemed impossible happens.
fields.human_design:
Experience Gate 35 sits in the throat and presses you to live things, then pass on what they taught you. It wants the new place, the new feeling and the thing you have never done. You go through them to see what they are like, not to reach an end. You are not here to master one thing; you learn by living many.

Its first danger is the rush: one experience straight into the next, with nothing taken in. Its second comes later. After you have seen a great deal, you can grow bored and sure that nothing is new. Then you settle into a life that asks nothing of you. The drive stays healthy when you choose the experiences worth your time and share what they taught you.
fields.tarot: This energy reaches out to meet everyone, and one reason is that it stands alone. It is the only member of its family, the Ring of Miracles, whose theme is the impossible made possible. With no kin to lean on, it goes out to connect. This one carries the miracle that love makes possible. Its ring and its two trigrams bring five of the tarot's major cards, its Arcana, to this one.
fields.body:
This energy is given to the thyroid, and the reason is pace. The thyroid sits low in the front of your neck, across the windpipe, and what it makes sets how fast your body runs. It is the slowest dial in you. Its hormone lasts about a week in your blood, and a change in it shows only over weeks. Whatever the day's hunger wants, your body's pace was set a while ago. The same hormone turns a tadpole into a frog, and nobody sees the moment it happens.

Put two fingers on the inside of your wrist and find the beat. Fear can raise it in a second. The beat you find at rest was set by this gland, and no amount of wanting hurries it. The hunger you were born with runs on a substance, and the substance is tryptophan. Your body cannot make it, so it comes in with meat, eggs or beans. You carry less of it than of any other piece you are built from. From it your body makes serotonin, the chemistry of having had enough, and most of that is made in the wall of your gut. So your hunger and your feeling of enough share one chemistry, made inside you from what you eat.

Serotonin is one link in a chain your body makes for itself. Giving with nothing wanted back sets it running, and what follows is happiness and a trust that your life is in order. A meal of bread or rice lets more tryptophan into your brain than a meal of meat does.

fields.essence: An open heart is alive in you, and it shows when life shakes you. The ground goes out from under you, and your stomach drops before your mind catches up. Your heart takes in the whole of what is happening, because it can hold any amount. Life keeps drawing you toward feelings you have not had yet, and you learn from each one.
fields.glance:
An open heart is alive in you, and it shows when life shakes you. The ground goes out from under you, and your stomach drops before your mind catches up. Your heart takes in the whole of what is happening, because it can hold any amount. Life keeps drawing you toward feelings you have not had yet, and you learn from each one.

Some days your heart pulls back for a moment, and that is human. Look straight at what is happening, and let it in all the way.

Each time you come through, what you feel grows clearer. The pain you let in joins you to other people instead of setting you apart. You understand what people feel, because you have felt it. So they come to you in their worst hour, and near you they open too.
fields.iching:
The light has gone under. Someone in power is doing harm, and what is clear in you is at risk for being clear. One order is ending and the next has not come. The push for change is in the air, and its time has not arrived.

So keep your head down and your light lit. Do the day's work, even the drudgery. Live among the others and look like one of them. Underneath, stay firm about what is right. Do not force the change. A light shown too early gets put out, and one kept low lasts.

Your eyes do the work now, under a soft belly. Let the belly stay soft, keep your eyes open, and wait for the morning. Earth over Fire is the hexagram of a light that has to go under for a while. Fire is the clear sight in you, the part that sees what is going on. Earth is the part of you that gives way and carries on. Here the giving way sits on top, because in some seasons what you see is not safe to show. This hexagram has long been read as the sun gone down into the earth. All night the sun is still burning, out of sight. So you can live among others, keep your light low, and still shine. What you know stays lit in you until the morning. Darkening of the Light
fields.gene_keys:
Turbulence Humanity Compassion Humanity is what grows in you once you stop running from pain. You meet the storm with an honest, open heart, and you graduate as a human being. Your suffering stops setting you apart and becomes what you share with everyone. Pleasure comes with pain, and you stop waiting for a life with only one of them. Once you let go of the idea that fate is against you, you speak cleanly with people.

You earn this over time, and you still close sometimes, because that is human too. Then you forgive yourself and the other person. You coax your heart back to life, again and again. Living from the heart, you have an answer to fear. In time nothing can wound you, because nothing wounds a healed heart. Disaster could strike at any hour, and everyone knows it. The news says so all day, until a low hum of fear runs under your days like weather. This storm in you is turbulence, and no life is free of it. What overwhelms you is less the suffering than the fear of it. The heart closes, the body braces, and a life gets written as one upset after the next. It shows most in love, where you want the most.

No feeling in you is wrong. You are innocent of your own chemistry and the way it makes you feel. The trouble starts when you push a feeling down or throw it at someone out of fear. Then this energy pulls crisis toward you like a magnet. It keeps bringing you the same lesson until you learn it. Compassion is the fragrance left when the storm is over. It is earned, on a road through the worst a person can feel, so it speaks in a human voice. The walls between you and everyone else fall away. You feel their pleasure, their pain and their longing as your own.

You go where the light is darkest, into wars or among the poor, without flinching. You have been so low once that nothing can feel that strong again, so fear has nowhere left to live. The look in your eyes or the softness of your voice can open the hardest heart. The seed of this was in the storm all along.
fields.human_design: Crisis Gate 36 sits in the centre of feeling, low in the body, and drives you toward what you have not yet felt. It carries a desire for new experience and a fear of not being equal to it. You learn by going in, through the highs and the lows. Because you have felt so much, you understand what other people feel. The drive runs in cycles, and when boredom comes it tempts you to leap into chaos. Its work is to stay with a thing long enough to become good at it.
fields.tarot: This energy lets suffering in, and suffering is how its family works. It belongs to four energies, the Ring of Divinity, and each of them can wake the highest thing in you. UL 22 is Treasure of the Way, the grace of having your feelings heard. UL 37 is Journey Home, the tenderness that holds your family together. UL 63 is Adornments of Time, the doubt that sets you searching. This one carries the heart that stays open through the dark. Five of the tarot's major cards show faces of this energy, from the weight that holds a light down to the sun that returns.
fields.body:
The lurch is the reason this energy is given to the solar plexus. When a lift starts down or a plane drops, your stomach seems to rise before you can think. The loose organs of your belly hang on their folds, so they lag a fraction of a second behind you. The knot of nerves behind your stomach reports that lag. It reaches every organ in your belly, and the pit of the stomach in front of it is where trouble shows first. So when the ground goes out from under your life, you feel it in the same place, before you know it anywhere else. A feeling you fight instead of feel spreads from here through your whole body as a nervous hum.

Rest a hand in the soft hollow just under your breastbone. The knot lies about a hand's depth behind it, against your spine, and it is where a drop is felt first. What churns in you when life lurches is chemistry before it is a thought, and one substance in it is proline. Your body makes it for itself, though meat and cheese are full of it too. Collagen is what holds your skin, bones and every healed cut together. About a quarter of it is proline.

This chemistry is shared with a family of energies in you. Together they bring the strongest feelings you will have, and a dark stretch full of doubt that you come out of cleaner. Suffering is built into you to crack you open. Freezing when it comes is something you learned.

fields.essence: At the end of the day you sit down to eat with the people who are yours. You feel affection for them in your body, as the warmth that spreads through you after a meal eaten together. You need no shared blood for this, since any few people drawn together can become a family. In you it is the wish to belong, and to see that everyone near you is fed.
fields.glance:
At the end of the day you sit down to eat with the people who are yours. You feel affection for them in your body, as the warmth that spreads through you after a meal eaten together. You need no shared blood for this, since any few people drawn together can become a family. In you it is the wish to belong, and to see that everyone near you is fed.

Some days your giving carries a quiet hope of something back. Giving that comes from your head always does. Look after yourself first, and ask your own heart what it needs. The giving that follows asks for nothing.

Let people lean on you, and lean on them without shame. What you give from the heart comes back to you, often from somewhere you were not looking. Then your affection reaches past your own table, to people you have never met.
fields.iching:
Something out in the world has hurt you or worn you down, and you have turned back toward home. That is the right way to turn. When a birth, an illness or a death changes a life, people go home to their own. The strength here is inside the house, and what is set right there sets right what lies beyond it. So the one who keeps the house matters most. That person sees to the food, leaves no chore undone and does not follow every whim out the door.

This time asks two things of you. Let your words have something behind them, so that what you say at home can be trusted. Let the way you live stay the same from day to day, long enough to be relied on. Give each person their own place, the older as the older and the younger as the younger.

This time lives in your legs and your eyes. Your legs bring you home, and your eyes see each person there as they are. Come in and sit down among your own before you do anything else. Wind over Fire is the hexagram of the people you live with. Fire is the warmth in you that draws your people close. Wind is the gentle way that warmth reaches every one of them. The warmth sits underneath because a home is made from the inside out. This hexagram has long been read as wind coming out of a fire. Your warmth at home spreads the same way, like the heat of a stove moving into every room of a cold house. So what you say at home needs something behind it, and the way you live needs to stay the same from day to day. When your own home is right, the good in it goes out into the world. The Family
fields.gene_keys:
Weakness Equality Tenderness Equality begins inside you, between the two sides of you. You have a sharp mind and a soft heart, a will that pushes and a willingness to give way. When one side rules and the other gives in, you are split and weak. Let the two meet as equals, and the balance you find goes with you into every room.

The one a group worries about is often the one who holds it together. In a family or a team you go to that weak place and help it mend, without taking it over. You hold a young tree up until it can stand, then let go. The ones you set free are the ones who stay loyal. You are never too proud to ask for help. People know you by your friendliness. Weakness here is a belief that you are powerless, and it feels like plain fact. You look at the part of your life that struggles most, money or health or one bond, and decide it is a dead end. So you bow your head to it and call that being realistic. Most people would rather stay beaten than find out otherwise. Giving in wears you down with a tiredness that has nothing good behind it. It is not the tiredness you feel after work you were glad to do.

You have been leaning on crutches you never needed. You need them only as long as you believe you are weak without them. Put them down, and you find your legs were strong all along. The part of your life that struggles most is where the whole of it can be lifted from, once you stop hiding it. Tenderness is the way a mother holds a child, and no single person owns it. You can feel it only with other people. It passes between people and grows among a few who have been drawn together. On a bright morning in a busy market you can see it pass from one pair of eyes to the next. It has no tension in it, so nothing can push against it. It is nearer the surface than anyone thinks, and in the right conditions it comes up by itself. What frightened you most is what changes you, once you trust it. Soft as it is, nothing can beat it.
fields.human_design: Friendship Gate 37 sits in the centre of feeling, in your belly, and presses you to belong. It is the wish to have a few people who are yours and to see them looked after. Its fear is that your own needs will go unmet while you meet everyone else's. When it runs well, your loyalty holds a group together and people know they can rely on you. When it runs badly, you give until nothing is left and keep the peace by leaving the hard thing unsaid. The peace worth keeping is the one where it gets said. Its nervousness is about tradition, the way things have always been done, kept long after it has stopped serving anyone.
fields.tarot: This energy gathers a few people into a family. It belongs to a family of four, the Ring of Divinity, whose theme is suffering that opens you. UL 22, Treasure of the Way, carries grace. UL 36, Crystal Creation, carries the dark stretch that tests you. UL 63, Adornments of Time, carries the questions that come once a thing is finished. This one carries the tenderness that can only be felt among people. Four of the tarot's major cards, its Arcana, come to this one through the ring and the two trigrams.
fields.body:
A shared meal is the reason this energy is given to your solar plexus. This knot of nerves sits behind your stomach and reaches everything a meal touches, from the stomach down to the gut. After you eat, blood goes to your belly along a nerve that runs through it, and your whole body slows and warms. It runs the part of you that is fed. It knows whether you have been fed long before you have a word for it.

Sit down to eat with people you belong to. Half an hour later the hollow under your breastbone is warm and your whole body has settled. Rest a hand there and you are resting it on the part of you that knows it has been fed. The warmth that passes between your people has a substance in you, and it is proline. Your body makes its own from another of the twenty pieces your proteins are built from, so it never has to come from food. Milk, cheese and bread are full of it all the same. Boil bones for a stock and let it go cold: it sets to a jelly, and the setting is proline's doing.

This energy is never carried by one person alone. It is the heart of a family, whatever the blood. You will not feel it being made. You feel the warmth when you are among your people.

fields.essence: Perseverance is alive in you once you have found something worth staying for. You know in your heart when a thing is right. Your body wants to be in the thick of it, and the effort feeds you instead of wearing you out.
fields.glance:
Perseverance is alive in you once you have found something worth staying for. You know in your heart when a thing is right. Your body wants to be in the thick of it, and the effort feeds you instead of wearing you out.

Some days the fight has nothing real to aim at, so it lands on the people closest to you. When that happens, stop and take one breath. The pattern breaks, and in the pause you can see what deserves your strength.

Be honest about where you are unhappy, in your work or in your closest bond. Then picture the thing your heart wants most, and put all that daily effort into it. Stay with it until it grows into what you hoped for. People who live this way have a light about them, and they smile easily.
fields.iching:
Two people who belong together have turned to look different ways. Neither of you is wrong, and neither of you is an enemy. You feel misunderstood, and still the difference between you matters to what you are doing. The large question between you cannot be settled now.

So settle the small things within your reach, one at a time, and let the large one heal from the edges in. What you have lost comes back on its own if you do not chase it. Keep company with everyone, and keep your own ground while you do. Look for what you share on the things that matter most, and let the small differences stand.

Your eyes and your mouth carry this. The eyes see the difference, and the mouth wants to smooth it over. Keep the eyes clear and the mouth kind, and give it time. Fire over Lake is the hexagram of two close people who have turned different ways. Fire is the clear sight in you that sees where you and another differ. Lake is the part of you that enjoys company. The clear sight sits above because once you see a difference, friendliness no longer closes it. This hexagram has long been read as a flame rising off a lake as the water sinks. Your clear sight rises the same way, while the ease between you sinks. What each of you wants from a life stays the same. You can differ from the people you love and still share one aim. Opposition
fields.gene_keys:
Struggle Perseverance Honour Perseverance is the same force with a fight worth having in front of it. The only thing that changes is which fight you are in. Resistance is pushing against the way things are moving, and it wears you out. An obstacle is part of the work, a test that sharpens your skill. You enjoy the odds against you, and you make hard things look easy while giving them everything. Your stubbornness can wear down a stronger opponent. Your deafness shuts out the voices that say it cannot be done.

This strength also knows when to hold back. Animals stop for no reason at all, and a fly lands on your arm and simply rests. Let life call you to these pauses. A day with pauses in it is a day you were awake for. Struggle is a fight with no purpose. It turns on whatever is in reach, even your own life or the people at your table. Once you bite down on something, you do not let go until it gives way. Struggle can free you, and it traps you the moment it becomes a habit. The day begins with a list of things to do and is over before you have looked up. There is a great sadness in this, because the fight you are having is never your real one. Most of it lands on the people closest to you, and the love between you wears thin.

Under it sits an old fear. As long as you are fighting, you feel in charge of your corner of the world. With nothing to fight, you fear you might cease to be. When the fighting stops, the whole of you is still there. Honour is what the fight becomes when nobody needs to win it. It comes from living your own truth, and at its height it joins you to everyone else. To honour someone is to hold them at their best, whatever they are doing now. People can lie to you or use you, and you still do not sink to their level. The test of an act is whether it brings people together or pulls them apart.

What you do from honour is remembered and told again. Each telling reminds people what they can be. Honour is quiet, and it lights a fire in everyone who meets it.
fields.human_design: The Fighter Gate 38 is the Fighter, and it presses you to find out what is worth fighting for. The finding matters more than the fight. You question and probe, and you do not look away from a hard truth. Other people's opinions move you very little, so you stand up for what you believe in even when it is unpopular. From outside you can look stubborn, as if every disagreement has to become a fight. Pick your fights, because a fight chosen only to let off pressure leaves you drained. Near you, people find a loyal friend and a steady ally.
fields.tarot: This energy fights for what matters, as every human life does. It belongs to a family of six, the Ring of Humanity, whose theme is your own human story. UL 25, The Mysteries Play, carries the wound you start with. UL 17, Pearl of Christos, carries going past the limits of your mind. UL 21, Beyond Binary, carries letting go of control. UL 10, Internal Treasure, carries finding your true self. UL 51, Unshakable Arrival, carries your waking up. This one carries the battle with your own shadows. The ring and the two trigrams bring five of the tarot's major cards, its Arcana, to this one.
fields.body:
The fight is the reason this energy is given to the adrenals. They are two small glands, one on top of each kidney, under the last ribs at your back. When something startles you, they arm you in the same second: your heart beats harder and your airways open. They do this before you have decided anything. They arm you the same way for the wrong fight and the right one, because they cannot tell the two apart. If nothing follows, it all settles within a couple of minutes.

Put a hand on your chest a second after a door slams. The heart under it is already going harder, and you chose nothing. Keep the hand there a minute and feel it settle. Perseverance has a chemistry in you, and one substance in it is arginine. Your body makes it for itself and builds it into every protein in you. It also comes in meat, eggs and nuts. With two others it makes the charge your muscles keep ready for the first seconds of hard effort.

This substance is in every person, and so is the struggle it carries here, to rise above your own lower nature. It is often through defeat that a person learns to be stronger.

fields.essence: You still carry a small child's energy, and it always wants to move. It rises in your body before you have thought, ready to act. When something stands in your way, this energy gathers there, so a block shows you where to look. It starts things and keeps them moving.
fields.glance:
You still carry a small child's energy, and it always wants to move. It rises in your body before you have thought, ready to act. When something stands in your way, this energy gathers there, so a block shows you where to look. It starts things and keeps them moving.

Some days a person gets under your skin, and you react before you can stop. Forcing a block open only makes you tighter. Holding the energy down leaves your breath shallow. Let in what bothers you, and ask which habit of yours it is pointing at.

Put the energy into what you love, and the more you make, the more of it there is. Breathe all the way down into your belly, the way a child does. Near you, people breathe more deeply and feel able to do more. This is the spark in you that wakes everyone up.
fields.iching:
You set out, the way is blocked, and the next way is blocked too. It is not your fault; the trouble is in the lay of the land. Pushing on only takes you deeper into it. What this time asks is that you see the danger and stop. Stopping here is knowing, and it is different from giving up. Go where the ground is easy, away from the hard country. Look for someone who has already come through this, and follow what they value. Hold to what is right through it, and it ends well.

While the road is closed, the work turns back on you. Look at your own conduct and mend what you find, instead of blaming anyone. Held back from outside, you grow from within.

The body here is the feet. Notice them now, cold or warm, ready to go or planted. Let them stand where they are until the way opens. Water over Mountain is the hexagram of the road that closes in front of you. Water is the part of you that wants to keep moving, even toward danger. Mountain is the part of you that knows when to stop. The danger sits above the stopping because it lies ahead, and only the one who stops in time sees it. This hexagram has long been read as water on a mountain, with no way down. Water held still on a height settles and clears, and your mind does the same when you stop. The texts also say to find someone who has crossed this way before. When the road closes, you get clear by stopping. Obstruction
fields.gene_keys:
Provocation Dynamism Liberation Dynamism is the energy you see in a small child, which never runs out and comes back as soon as it is spent. Most of it was set into habit by the age of seven, and none of that is final. When it comes back in a grown person, it comes as creativity. The quickest way to call it back is to do what you love. Your breath drops back into your belly, the way a child breathes.

Other people catch it. Near someone living this, people breathe more fully and feel able to do more. This energy does not wait. It starts things and keeps them going, and it will risk hurting someone's feelings to shake them awake. Its joy comes after long, steady work, and it shows in a laugh that shakes the whole body. Someone close says a small thing in a certain tone, and something in you goes off before you can think. It is almost never the words. The tone finds the exact place where you already feel guilty or sore. Under the anger sits an older fear, of being trapped and losing your freedom to act. Anything that feels cornered will strike. You are caught the moment you react. Most people push buttons on some days and have theirs pushed on others.

Held in, the same energy keeps your breath high and short. Leaving the job or moving house does not help, because the trapped feeling moves with you. What changes it is how you meet the next tone. Liberation is the state where nothing can provoke you. A word enters your ear, your mind turns it into meaning, and your breath does not catch. You hear the sound without following it. To get here you give up the thing that seemed to drive you, your own separate freedom. It feels like a physical death, every plan and piece of work let go at once, and it passes through agony into joy.

People who live here are hard to be near. They aim their love at your weakest spot to test how far you have let go. If anything still lands as personal, there is further to go. A dragonfly larva hunts well under the water, then one day climbs up toward the light. The same push can rise in you, out of nowhere, and take you past a life that was working.
fields.human_design: Provocation Gate 39 sits in the Root, low in your body, and it presses you to stir up what has gone still. It drives you to provoke people, sometimes by playful teasing and sometimes more fiercely, until something in them moves. What you push them toward is trust that life will give them what they need. Everything depends on timing. With the right person at the right moment, it is a spark that wakes up the whole room. If you do it only to ease your own pressure, nobody enjoys it. This gate is hard to talk out of anything. It treats every moment of feeling that there is not enough as a place to push off from.
fields.tarot: This energy is the push that starts every search. It belongs to a family of six, the Ring of Seeking, and each member makes a different pressure in you. UL 52, Timeless Blossom, keeps the pressure in check. UL 53, Creation Oscillation, carries the urge to begin. UL 54, Everlasting Bounty, carries the drive to rise. UL 58, Rhythm of Life, carries joy. UL 15, Ordinary Valiance, is where the seeking comes to rest. This one wakes first. The ring and the two trigrams bring four of the tarot's major cards here, and one of them twice.
fields.body:
The rush is the reason this energy is given to the adrenals. Two small glands sit on top of your kidneys, and they fire before you have decided anything. Within a second the rush is through you. Your blood leaves your skin for your muscles, your hands go cold and a little damp, and you are ready to move. The rush is real, and it is gone in a couple of minutes, because your body clears it that fast. A body that keeps calling for it is under a pressure with nowhere to go. You feel that as a tiredness rest does not touch.

Think of the last time something startled you. Your hands went cold a moment later, because the blood had gone where it was needed. When the rush had passed, a deep breath came on its own. That breath is what lasts. The pressure in you has a chemistry, and one substance in it is serine. You feel it low in your body, where the rush starts. It is gutsy and all about action, and it never waits for your head. You share this chemistry with five other energies, and each makes a different pressure in you.

Yours is enormous, in you and in the room around you, and it is what makes things. It drives a person past what they were. When you cut yourself, serine is part of what makes your blood clot and close the wound.

fields.essence: When a long push is over and you can finally set things down, your will starts to fill again. With it you can carry what is yours all the way to its end. It rises from deep inside you the way a spring does, and nothing in it has to be forced. Work that fits you does not drain you, so you can work harder than most and still have strength left.
fields.glance:
When a long push is over and you can finally set things down, your will starts to fill again. With it you can carry what is yours all the way to its end. It rises from deep inside you the way a spring does, and nothing in it has to be forced. Work that fits you does not drain you, so you can work harder than most and still have strength left.

Some weeks you give to everyone who asks, and the tiredness goes deeper than sleep can reach. That tiredness comes from pushing your life in a direction that is not its own. Slowly put down one thing that is not yours, and your body breathes out.

There is a thing you are here to do, and it is probably in front of you already. Give yourself to it, and say no to everything else without a fight. Stop when it is time to stop, and keep some of every day for yourself. The strength you spend on what is yours comes back as fast as you give it.
fields.iching:
The hard time is over. What held you for so long has let go, the way the air clears after a storm. Now the time can go one of two ways. If there is nothing more to do, go back to your ordinary days and keep the old ways. If something is still to do, do it early at first light, before the trouble settles in again. Do not stay in the relief longer than it lasts. Others have come through this before you, and they were back at work the next morning.

Then forgive. Let the mistakes go, your own with everyone else's, because while you hold on to who was to blame you are still tied. Go gently, and rest the way the ground rests after rain. In the body this starts in the feet. After a long time sitting, your feet want to move before you have decided to walk. Let them take the first step, and keep the rest of you easy. Thunder over Water is the hexagram of the moment a hard time lets go of you. Water is the danger you have been living inside, where each step feels like a risk. Thunder is the part of you that moves, the jolt that gets you up after a long time held still. The movement sits above the danger because you get out of trouble by moving, and here you have moved. This hexagram has long been read as a thunderstorm breaking. The air is heavy for days, then the rain comes, and afterwards you can breathe again. The same rain splits the seeds open, so what was shut tight begins to grow. What held you is coming loose, and your part now is to let it. Deliverance
fields.gene_keys:
Exhaustion Resolve Divine Will Resolve starts with an open hand that holds one thing. Take hold of what is truly yours, and the rest falls from your fingers. The favours you did not want to do fall away, and so do the promises made only to please. What stays feeds you. You can work hard and not wear out, because the will is built into the work from the start. You say no without a fight, since whoever you turn away belongs somewhere else. When someone you love calls you away in the middle, you put the work down, and taking that break is part of the strength.

Most of it is knowing how to relax. Rest is everywhere once you stop giving in to too much. It is a walk with nowhere to get to, or the work you love with people you love. None of this is going without. You take what life offers, with measure, and sometimes more than you need. Someone worn out who meets you goes away changed. Tired is where this begins, a tiredness that sleep no longer reaches. Picture a hand so full it cannot open. In it are the job, the people who lean on you and the things you agreed to without wanting them. You were taught that a strong person does more and holds on harder, and both drain you. The cost shows up as thirst. You want something you cannot name, and mostly you do not notice how thirsty you are. Underneath it there is usually a feeling you have refused to feel.

It shows up as too much: too much work and no time for home, or all of you going to other people. You become many things to many people and no one to yourself. Cut off from what feeds you, you run down, the way anything does that is drawn on and never filled. The hand does not need to be forced open. Noticing it is where the tiredness starts to end. Both hands are empty now, and nothing is missing. You no longer feel like the one making the choices. You are free to do exactly as you please, and none of what you do is in your hands. Every part of your body is at ease, and people near you can see it as a kind of light. Nobody can pretend their way here. Some who are tired of searching take up the idea of surrender to get off the hook, and that only makes them quiet. This comes at the end of the search, when every hope has been dropped, and it comes to you alone.
fields.human_design: Restoration Gate 40 sits in the Will Center and pulls you away to gather yourself. After work or after people, it wants you on your own for a while to restock what you gave. It asks you to value yourself enough to step away, even from the people you love. A partner can read this as rejection, so tell them what it is. When it runs badly, you stay instead: you give to everyone who asks and prove your worth by doing more. Then you blame others for a tiredness you never named. The loneliness that comes with this gate is a signal to turn inward. You come back from the time away with more to give than you left with.
fields.tarot: This energy saves your strength by not wasting it. It belongs to a family of four, the Ring of Alchemy, whose theme is turning something rough into something fine. UL 6, Harmonious Mirage, carries the walls coming down between two people. UL 47, Garden of Alchemy, carries the change of old ways. UL 64, Communion, carries the fresh possibilities that follow. This one carries the new openness into a community. Its family and its two trigrams bring five of the tarot's major cards, its Arcana, to this one.
fields.body:
Rest is the reason this energy is given to your stomach. The stomach is where what you eat becomes what you run on, and it does that only while you are at rest. It loosens to make room for a meal before the meal arrives, then works on it for hours without being asked. When you are afraid or angry or straining, it stops and the blood goes to your muscles instead. A full stomach leaves the will in you content, and an empty one sends it out to find food. What you force costs you what you had. What you take in at rest is what you have to give.

Your stomach lies high on your left, under the ribs, a little below the tip of the breastbone. After a meal, rest a hand there and you can feel the fullness. On an empty morning, the growl under your hand is its wall working on nothing. Your hand is on the part of you that works only when you leave it alone. The will in you has a substance, and it is glycine. It is the smallest of the twenty pieces your proteins are built from. Your body makes most of what it needs, and the rest comes from the skin and bones of meat or fish. A third of the frame that holds you up, your skin and bone, is made of it. In your spinal cord it is the signal that tells a nerve to stop firing.

Three other energies in you run on this same substance, and between them they waste no strength. Together they release everything your body still holds against itself. Carried all the way, that release leaves every part of you at rest.

fields.essence: When one part of your life ends and the next has not begun, a longing for more rises in you. You feel it low in your body, as a pull toward a life you can already picture. You sense what is on its way before it arrives, and you want to feel it for yourself. The picture shows you which way to walk.
fields.glance:
When one part of your life ends and the next has not begun, a longing for more rises in you. You feel it low in your body, as a pull toward a life you can already picture. You sense what is on its way before it arrives, and you want to feel it for yourself. The picture shows you which way to walk.

Some days the picture feels so good that its hope is enough, and you stay where you are. Then life takes that picture away, and it can feel like a loss. What you wanted stays with you, and a new picture rises in its place.

Hold each picture the way you hold a plan for a trip, ready for the road to change it. Keep your plans small, and take the first real step toward what you see. Each ending then clears the way for a new start. Step by step, the picture becomes a life you are living.
fields.iching:
Something in your life is ending, and you have less to hold on to than before. The loss comes either way. What you can choose is whether you give it up freely. Given up on purpose, what you lose becomes an offering. It need not be much. Two small bowls are enough when what is in them is sincere.

Start with what you have too much of. Hold back your anger, and let a craving pass without feeding it. This is heavy at the start and light afterward, so do not take the weight as a sign that you are wrong. Keep away from what could harm you while you have less. Do not dwell on what has already ended. Setting out goes well now, and where having less ends, having more begins.

In the body this time asks for less. Eat until you have had enough, then stop, and notice how much lighter you feel. A few days by a lake or in the mountains can give back what the everyday wore away. Mountain over Lake is the hexagram of giving up what you do not need. Lake is the joy in you that gives freely. Mountain is the part of you that knows when to stop. The stopping sits above the joy because a pleasure you can stop is one that does not run your life. This hexagram has long been read as a lake at the foot of a mountain. The lake gives its water up as mist, and the mist falls as rain on the heights. What you let go of below comes back to lift you. What you give up on purpose makes room for what raises you. Decrease
fields.gene_keys:
Fantasy Anticipation Emanation Anticipation is the same picture once you have seen what it was asking for. Under every fantasy there is one ache: to be loved and to belong to something whole. Once you know that, the picture can be used. You stop mistaking a wish for a sign, and you begin to feel what is really taking shape. A musician can hear a whole piece before one note is written, then write it down. Someone who only pictures a thing and someone who brings it into the world may see the same thing, and only one of them starts.

The light down the road is something you walk toward now. Having found the root of your own pictures, you can see where someone else's is heading. You can sense when a habit that has held them is ready to break. Of all you make, the children you raise and the stories you tell are what last. You know how a story goes, and you can wait for its ending. A picture of a better life sits in you, and most days you live in the picture instead of the life. The pressure behind it is the pressure to grow. Through a tired mind it comes out as the pressure to feel happy, and the mind paints the right person or the money. You hold the key to your dream and never turn it in the lock. The hope it brings feels so good that you never take a step. When you feel empty, you picture being full. When you feel full, the past weighs on you and you want to be rid of it.

The picture was a light thrown down the road to show you the way, and you stand still looking at the light. Life will take each of these pictures from you, one at a time. That is good news, though it never feels like it. The emptiness a picture leaves can be filled, though never by the next picture, and never by what you achieve. Emanation is the end of the road turning out to be where it began. You thought you were travelling forward, and you were travelling back to where you came from. Each picture that rises in you is a small light thrown ahead from that source, looking for the way home. Followed all the way, the lights lead back to where they were thrown from. Nothing you do brings this on. It simply arrives, and then there is no one there for it to happen to.

There is no more hunger here, and no more pressure to become anything. People hear an agenda in whatever you say. If you keep quiet, they hear one in that too. None of it matters to you now. It was all a dream, and you had to be asleep to hear it.
fields.human_design: Imagination Gate 41 sits at the base of the body and presses you to picture more than is here. It imagines a fuller life or a better world, then makes you want to feel it for yourself. It gives the first push whenever something new begins in your life. What it starts it does not always finish, because starting is its work. From outside this can look like restlessness, someone never content with what they have. People may call your ideas unrealistic, or say you ask too much. Then you may keep your pictures to yourself until they turn into the worst that could happen. Share a picture when the time is right, and enjoy imagining it for its own sake.
fields.tarot: This energy begins, and every other energy needs a beginning. It belongs to the Ring of Origin, a family of one, whose theme is the push to seek out new ground and new experience. Whatever else moves in you starts with the first step this one takes. Five major cards of the tarot gather here, and each names something this longing asks of you.
fields.body:
This energy belongs to the adrenals because of the morning. These two small glands sit one on top of each kidney, high at the back under the last ribs. Each night they begin your day before you wake. Their tide is lowest around midnight and rises through the last hours of sleep. It is highest in the hour after you wake, so your day has already begun when you open your eyes. They ready you whether the day will be good or not.

You cannot feel them, even with a hand flat on your back below the ribs. What you can notice is waking just before the alarm. When you know the hour you must be up, their tide rises earlier to meet it. Most people have done this without knowing why, and this tide is part of the reason. The longing for more has a chemistry in you, and one substance in it is methionine. Every protein your body makes begins with this one piece, because the code that spells it also says begin. Your body cannot make it. It comes in from eggs, fish or meat, and beans are short of it. Once the building is under way, that first piece is most often trimmed off.

Every story your body tells opens on the same first word. Beans are short of this piece, and rice is short of another. Eaten together they are short of nothing, which is why kitchens all over the world pair them.

fields.essence: Growth is alive in you as a steady pull to see things through. It carries a piece of work, or a bond with someone, from the first stir to its ripe end. You feel it low in your belly as a clear yes when a thing is done. When more comes to you than you planned, you pass some of it on, and more keeps coming.
fields.glance:
Growth is alive in you as a steady pull to see things through. It carries a piece of work, or a bond with someone, from the first stir to its ripe end. You feel it low in your belly as a clear yes when a thing is done. When more comes to you than you planned, you pass some of it on, and more keeps coming.

Some days you set your heart on how a thing must turn out, and by when. Whatever arrives then falls short, and you catch yourself waiting for your real life to start. Keep your hope and let the picture go. Your life is already under way.

Finish what is ready, even when it was good, because each ending clears the way for the next. You are writing your life and reading it at the same time. You feel every part of it, even the letdowns. Your life moves toward perfection one finished thing at a time.
fields.iching:
This is a time of gain. Opportunities come knocking, and more reaches you than you worked for. It comes from above you, from people or a life with more than enough, letting some of it go. The time is good for something large, even a crossing you would not risk in a leaner year. It will not stay open for long.

What it asks is that the gain keep moving. What you receive, give on, because giving is the only way the increase lasts. A full cup has to be poured before it can be filled again. Move toward the good in others as quickly as wind moves. Mend your own faults with the nerve of thunder. Kept for yourself alone, the gain turns against you.

Your feet and legs do the work now. The feet take the first step, and the thighs bring the rest of your body after them. Stand while the water is high, and cross. Wind over Thunder is the hexagram of a time when your life is gaining. Thunder is the stir in you that wakes something new and sets it moving. Wind is the part of you that carries what has woken out to the people around you. The carrying sits above the stirring because a gain kept inside you stops growing. This hexagram has long been read as wind and thunder, each making the other stronger. A good idea goes further when someone passes it on, and passing it on brings you the next one. The same two ask you to move toward the good you see in others, and to mend the faults you find in yourself. What stirs in you is meant to reach past you. Increase
fields.gene_keys:
Expectation Detachment Celebration Detachment means feeling more, not less. No fixed outcome squeezes what happens, so you feel all of it. You can even enjoy being disappointed. It cannot be forced. Hold a feeling down by will, and the grip only tightens. It comes when you give way to every feeling fully, without always acting on it.

From there your life reads like a book. You write it as you go and read it too, absorbed but never swept away by the words. You let go of each plan as soon as life changes it, and you can see where you still want to steer. You keep your hope and drop your demands. An obstacle starts to look like a chance to grow. You find this by giving in to being ordinary and human, breathing deeply and not flinching from what hurts. Almost everyone is waiting for the day their life comes right. The money will be sorted, love will be in place, and there will be room to live at last. First there are a few things to clear up. So the living is put off, year after year, until you are old. It is never too late to be here now. It takes seeing through what you were waiting for, once and completely.

The trouble starts when the mind takes hold of hope and gives it a date and a shape. Whatever arrives is measured against that shape, and it falls short. Hopeful or gloomy, a fixed outcome narrows your eyes until you miss the good in front of you. Under every other ending sits the one nobody escapes. Your body is made to die, and your unease about time running out comes from there. Many disappointments turn out, later, to be blessings. Celebration comes when the story ends in a laugh. In detachment you still watched your life from a little way off. Now the one watching and what is watched are the same, so there is only one thing happening. Every cell in you starts dying the moment it is born. You are less a fixed thing than a passage life moves through. Somewhere deep in you, something gets the joke. The whole serious search was the set-up, and you laugh because you let yourself be tricked.

Sit by a river and follow its currents with your eyes. Then stop following and simply gaze. The river loses its direction and seems to flow at you and out of you from everywhere. No practice brings this on. Whoever it happens to wants only to share the laugh.
fields.human_design:
Growth Gate 42 is the drive to finish what has been started. It wants to see a cycle through its beginning, its middle and its end. It can stay with a piece of work or a person until it has ripened, and it knows real growth takes time. From outside, that can look like patience or stubbornness. Its gift is knowing how to wrap a thing up so there is room for what comes next.

Its trouble runs two ways. It can hold on to something long after it is over, because finishing was the whole point. Or it feels it should start everything itself, and a pile of half-done things grows too heavy to look at. Then it rushes to close them early, just to be rid of the pressure. It works best when it is led to what is ready to finish.
fields.tarot: This energy closes things, and every close leaves room for a start. It belongs to a family of six, the Ring of Life and Death, which holds one whole life. When you are starting over, open UL 3, Messengers of the Infinite. When you need to be here now, open UL 20, Emerging as the Code. For clarity, open UL 23, Beneath the Surface. To go back to where a thing began, open UL 24, Frequency Flutter. To look after someone, open UL 27, Inner Majesty. Four of the tarot's major cards, its Arcana, gather around this energy. Death comes twice, because letting go runs all through your growth.
fields.body:
Finishing is the reason this energy is given to the sacral plexus. It is a weave of nerves low in your pelvis, part of the engine that keeps a body going without being watched. The low back around it has long been held as the body's store, where you keep what you carry until its season ends. In you this weave is where a movement is carried to its close.

Stand up from your chair. Your legs begin it. The last of the rise, straightening at the hip, is done by the largest muscle you have. That muscle takes its order from this weave. You have finished that movement thousands of times without knowing where the finish was made. The growth in you has a substance, and it is leucine. Your body cannot make it, so it comes in with fish, milk or lentils. The muscle you move with breaks it down, where most of what you eat is handled by the liver.

This energy shares that substance with five others in its family. Together they hold the whole run of every living cell, from its first innocence to what it has learned by the end. This energy is where that run closes. What was alive in the cell steps out of the shape it wore, the way you let go of someone who has died.

fields.essence: Insight comes to you all at once, often just after you have stopped trying to work a thing out. You hear it more than you see it, a knowing that runs through your whole body before your mind has caught up. It comes whole, like a message in code, clear to you and hard to put into words.
fields.glance:
Insight comes to you all at once, often just after you have stopped trying to work a thing out. You hear it more than you see it, a knowing that runs through your whole body before your mind has caught up. It comes whole, like a message in code, clear to you and hard to put into words.

Some stretches bring nothing, and it is tempting to fill the quiet with plans and worry. Chasing an answer only pushes it further off, the way a song will not come when you force it. Leave a gap in the day with no purpose in it, and let yourself not know for a while.

Walk through your days a little slower. The flash tends to come from where you were not looking. One clear insight can change the course of a life. You take the new path it shows you without needing to know where it leads.
fields.iching:
A tension that has been building for a long time is about to break. More has piled up than can be held, and now it has to go somewhere. Only one thin thing stands in the way at the top, and everything beneath it is strength. Do not meet it with force. Say it openly where it counts, and tell the truth, knowing there is some risk in it. Tell your own people first, so they are ready for what comes. Then set out, and expect the way to differ from the one you first had in mind.

When it has broken through, give what comes of it to the people around you. Do not rest on it as if it made you better than they are.

Your mouth does the work now. Say the thing plainly, once, to the people who need to hear it. Lake over Heaven is the hexagram of a breakthrough after a long build-up. Heaven is the drive in you that keeps building and never tires. Lake is the part of you that wants to say it out loud. The lake sits on top because what has built up for so long now has to come out. This hexagram has long been read as a lake risen into the sky. Water that high cannot stay there, and it comes down as rain. What has been building in you is ready to be said. Breakthrough
fields.gene_keys:
Deafness Insight Epiphany Insight begins when the old deafness turns into a friend. You stop listening to what everyone expects of you. You go deaf to the things that used to matter and do not any more. You still hear what others say, and it simply stops moving you. What you trust now is the voice inside you, whatever it costs.

This makes you a rebel, and the rebellion is against your own mind, never against other people. You cut a new path and do not worry where it goes. There is delight in it, a glitter in the eyes, spirit without a fight. Every person is born to fill a space in the world that nobody else can fill. This is you filling yours. Deafness here is noise: a day so full of things to do that the question with no answer never gets a hearing. You wake not knowing what the day is for, and rather than sit with that, you fill it. The day is gone before you get there. By evening you are too tired to see that it was beautiful. Your hearing is fine. You are too busy worrying to hear, or too sure of what you are doing to listen.

Underneath is fear, and it fastens onto the way your body feels. So you look for the happiness that would end it, in the right partner or in enough money. Happiness is part of your natural chemistry, there on some days and gone on others. Nothing outside you can buy it. You want change more than anything, and the wanting is what keeps it away. Epiphany is the silence coming back, and it is loud. Sit an hour alone in the dark of a cave, listening, and the silence fills every part of you. What you learn there is that you cannot know anything. In knowing nothing, you rest in everything. You may search for years, until you are too tired to go on. When you give up, you find an ordinary person looking for what they already were.

From here you are ordinary again, and there is nothing to rebel against. You say what you like and laugh often, because nothing can be added to you or taken away. All that you know gives way to what you do not. What is left is friendliness toward everyone.
fields.human_design: Insight Gate 43 sits in the part of the mind behind your forehead and brings sudden clarity. A problem you have been stuck on makes sense all at once, often on a walk, in the shower or just before sleep. It cuts through the confusion and shows a way forward. It comes after its own quiet time and cannot be hurried. It can overturn your plans and what you believed yesterday. It is also hard to put into words. So you may say it before anyone can take it in, or keep it and feel alone with it. Some people with this gate come to doubt their own sanity, because they see what others miss. Its work is to trust what you know without second-guessing it.
fields.tarot: This energy drops down into your life as a knowing. It belongs to a family of two, the Ring of Destiny, whose theme is timing. UL 34, Sublime Power, carries the strength that pushes up to become more. This one carries the insight that comes down to meet it. A life is steered by the two together. Its family and its two trigrams bring five of the tarot's major cards, its Arcana, to this one.
fields.body:
You hear yourself from the inside, and that is why this energy is given to the inner ear. Everyone else hears your voice through the air. You hear it mostly through the bone of your own skull. That is why a recording of your voice sounds like a stranger. The inner ear sits sealed inside the hardest bone in your head, with no opening to the outside. In the same place, three small curved tubes of fluid keep you upright without ever telling you.

Block both ears with your fingertips and hum. The hum gets louder, because it reaches the inner ear through your skull and needs no air. That is the voice only you can hear, and the part of you that hears it is working now. The timing of this energy has a substance in you, and its name is asparagine. It was the first of the twenty pieces your proteins are built from that anyone ever found. It was drawn out of asparagus juice two hundred years ago and named after the plant.

This energy shares that substance with one kin, and together they carry the secret of timing. The secret is that chance and love dance together in your life. The more you let love in, the more chance seems to work in your favour. In the end what looked random turns out to have a pattern, and your timing comes right.

fields.essence: When you meet someone new, you know within seconds whether they belong in your life. You feel it in your body, well before you could give a reason. Some strangers seem familiar the moment you meet them, and those are the people you have work to do with.
fields.glance:
When you meet someone new, you know within seconds whether they belong in your life. You feel it in your body, well before you could give a reason. Some strangers seem familiar the moment you meet them, and those are the people you have work to do with.

Sometimes an old hurt clouds what you feel, and you let the wrong people close or keep the right ones away. A lesson you leave unlearned comes back through someone new, even after you walk away. Stay with the fear until it passes, and your instinct comes back clear.

Trust what your body tells you, and follow each person you recognise to the next. Over time a group gathers around you that you did not set out to build. It is like finding your section in an orchestra: each of you plays your own part, and the music comes from all of you. Working together stops being work and turns into play.
fields.iching:
Someone or something has come into your life that you did not plan for, and the pull toward it is strong. For now it is small, one soft thing under everything firm you have built. It arrives at a high point, the way the light starts to shorten on the longest day of the year. Every living thing comes from two things meeting, so the meeting itself is not wrong. What it asks is that you see it clearly while it is still small.

Meet it, and do not marry it. What comes in this softly keeps coming. One thing let in without a look can push one good thing after another out of its place. Hold it the way a firm hand holds a rope, neither crushing it nor letting it run. A middle course works better than giving in or fighting.

Your head and your thighs carry this time. The head sees far, and the thighs carry you toward whoever is coming. Stand with your head clear and your step unhurried, and look at what comes before you let it in. Heaven over Wind is the hexagram of meeting what you did not plan to meet. Wind is the part of you that lets a new person in before you have decided to. Heaven is the strength in you that keeps to its own course. The letting in sits below the strength because every meeting starts small, underneath everything you have already built. This hexagram has long been read as the wind blowing under the sky, reaching every living thing. In the same way, one person you allow in reaches every part of your life. Who you let in, you carry into the whole of your life. Coming to Meet
fields.gene_keys:
Interference Teamwork Synarchy Teamwork begins when fear no longer muddles how you read people. You can size someone up with a single handshake, but only up close, because you have to be near a person to read them truly. Once you trust that reading, you start to find your own people. The sure sign that you have found them is devotion.

A team like this gives each person their freedom. Nobody stands over anyone, and the lead passes sideways to whoever the music needs. There is more life in you, because the energy you spent defending yourself is free. Without organising anyone, you become the one they come together around. Interference sounds like a room where everyone plays their own tune and nobody hears anyone else. It is a family that loves each other and cannot stop hurting each other, or good people at work who make only friction. Fear plays out in two ways in a room like that. Some people go along with anything to keep the peace. Others turn the fear outward as irritation, anger and the need to control every small movement, and most of us have been both. What builds up is resentment, and resentment ends in a break. Between people it is a break-up, and inside one person it is a breakdown.

It is easy to decide the other person is the problem. It is never about the others. The noise starts inside you, as a way of seeing the world through fear, and it goes out from you into everyone you meet. Everyone around you becomes part of one music, and the conductor is inside every player.
