You see the whole weave of who meets whom, back through the generations, and instead of standing outside it you dissolve into it. You hear it only in silence, the way a still mind can hear a whole hive moving. Everybody leads together, each one different and each a perfect fit.

Nothing here needs fixing. You see everything as it is and leave it where it is. Every life finds its own way, even the ones still caught in the noise. The harmony was there from the beginning, only hidden. By the time it arrives, the separate person who went looking for it is gone.
fields.human_design:
Alertness Gate 44 keeps hold of what happened last time. It looks at a new situation and sees the pattern in it: what worked before, and what caused pain. Its fear fits in one sentence: last time I did this, it did not work. The pressure is there so the past does not repeat itself unchanged. It keeps what served and lets go of what did not. It also has a sense of timing, of when one round of things is closing and the next is about to start.

Pushed too far, the memory turns into suspicion. It can also become a belief that the old patterns can never change, so you stop moving at all. Used well, it turns an old pain into a purpose.
fields.tarot: This energy gathers people, and every group that works starts with two. It belongs to a family of two, the Ring of the Illuminati, which is about you and your people living in harmony. UL 50, Melt Into Perfection, carries the values that keep your group in balance once it has formed. This one carries the meeting that starts it. The ring and the two trigrams bring five of the tarot's major cards, each a picture of how you meet people.
fields.body:
Smell is the reason this energy is given to your immune system. The immune system is not in one place. It stands along every surface where the outside touches you: your skin, your gut and the lining of your breath. It meets whatever comes in before anything else does. It knows what it meets by the fit of a shape, the way your nose knows a smell. Once it has met a thing, it keeps cells that know that one thing, for years or for life.

That is why a childhood fever comes once and never again. Where there is a round scar high on your arm, a memory was put in on purpose. Scratch your skin, and within minutes the place turns warm and pink. That warmth is the part of you that meets everything, arriving where it is needed. Fear sends chemical signals through you, and they go one of two ways. Some hold you down, and some fire you up. Either way, the trouble between you and other people begins in your cells, and so does the peace. The substance of this energy in you is glutamic acid. It is one of the twenty pieces every protein in you is built from, and your body makes its own. It is also the savoury taste, what hard cheese and a ripe tomato have in common on your tongue.

You share this chemistry with one other energy. A queen holds a hive of bees together, keeping every bee on course by what she gives off. Without her, the hive falls apart. Your cells are a team in the same way. They learn to work together, and you are their captain.

fields.essence: When people gather around something they all need, goodwill is what lets it go round. You feel it as a wish to see everyone at the table fed, yourself included. You would rather share what you have than sell it, since it goes further that way. People relax near you, since nobody has to fight for a place.
fields.glance:
When people gather around something they all need, goodwill is what lets it go round. You feel it as a wish to see everyone at the table fed, yourself included. You would rather share what you have than sell it, since it goes further that way. People relax near you, since nobody has to fight for a place.

Some days the old fear of not having enough comes back. You feel yourself tighten the moment you step out of the door. Stop and feel the fear where it sits in your body. Given your attention, it melts, and under it is the feeling that everything is fine.

Gather the people you trust and give them the freedom to do things their own way. Let each of them add their own thread. Woven together like this, a crowd becomes one people.
fields.iching:
People are coming together, far more of them than a family or a street, around something they all need. A crowd this size can do what no small group could. It can also come apart in confusion, with people pushing for the better place.

What holds it is something larger than any of you. The king in this hexagram goes first to the temple of his ancestors, to remember where his people came from. Remember your own roots before you lead. Go to someone who sees further than you. Bring your best, never what you can spare. Know where you are going together, because people with nowhere to go drift apart. While all is well, get ready for trouble nobody expects, since friction comes wherever many people meet.

Your mouth does the work here, in the words that bring people together and the food they share. Stand like someone who has made room at the table for one more. Lake over Earth is the hexagram of a crowd coming together. Earth is the part of you that makes room and provides for everyone. Lake is the part of you that makes people glad to be near you. The gladness sits above the making room, because when you go along with people, they are happy to stay. This hexagram has long been read as water gathered on the ground. Water collects where the land lies low, and people collect around whoever makes room for them. Here the gathering is large, a whole people rather than a few neighbours. You bring people together by making room for them, and your welcome keeps them. Gathering Together
fields.gene_keys:
Dominance Synergy Communion Synergy is what a group feels when nobody needs to be on top. It comes from trust settled in your body, the sense that the whole is holding you up. Then a group finds its own order, the way iron filings on a sheet of paper line up over a hidden magnet. Given time and space, it arrives at something better than anyone could have planned. On the way, one person often carries the whole group's fear, and the group works through it together.

The hard part falls on whoever holds the power. Handing someone complete authority looks like a loss, and it is pure alchemy. The goodwill it sets free spreads outward by word of mouth and comes back many times over. Dominance starts with food. Everyone has to eat, so whoever controls the food holds the power, and money is the same thing in newer clothes. Out of the old fear of not having enough grew rank. To feel safe, you push someone down so you can rise, and the ladder feeds you for staying on it. Nobody is to blame for it, you included. The fear is older than any of them.

In you it began early, the first time the world seemed unsafe and your whole body drew in. Since then you hold on to things, a patch of ground or a person, as if you could take them with you. Most people loosen their grip only near the end. The fear is worth feeling, because it leads you toward your own heart. Communion is a meal with no host. You feed each other without keeping count, so money has no work to do. It feels like an early Sunday morning outside, before anyone is up. The world seems newly born, and you have nowhere you need to be. Nobody asks why they are here or what they have to do. Being here is enough.

Dying after a life like that would be no different from living. You drift in and you drift out, with no need even to miss each other. The order you found was there all along, hidden inside the old ladder, waiting.
fields.human_design:
Distribution Gate 45 sits in the throat and is the drive to gather people and share out what there is. It has been called the king or queen of the tribe, and when it speaks, people listen. It holds the resources for the whole group, whether money, knowledge or care. Its favourite way to share is to teach, so that the people around it learn to provide for themselves.

Its fear is that there will not be enough. Then it holds back what it should share, or grows loud and showy to prove it deserves its seat. It also needs to be heard, and when it is not, it either goes quiet or gets louder. Its power comes from being present, never from putting on a show. It knows when to step forward and when to step back.
fields.tarot: This energy unites what people have, and on its own it can draw everything from a single well. It belongs to a family of two, the Ring of Prosperity, whose theme is abundance that is shared. UL 16, Grand Rising, carries the skill of drawing on many sources when one runs dry. This one carries the gathering that brings them together. The ring and the two trigrams give this energy five of the tarot's major cards, its Arcana.
fields.body:
This energy is given to the thyroid, and the reason is the sea. The thyroid sits low in the front of your neck, across your windpipe, and it is the one organ in you that needs iodine. Iodine comes from the sea and the soil. You get it from fish and seaweed, from milk and eggs, and from the salt on most kitchen tables. Your thyroid pulls it out of your blood and holds it many times stronger than the blood around it. From it, the gland makes what every part of you runs on. So one thing, gathered out of what everyone eats, is kept in one place and given out to your whole body.

Look at the salt in your kitchen. Somewhere on the packet it says iodised, or iodine added, and that was put there for this gland alone. Rest a hand at the base of your throat, and you are resting it on the part of you that is fed by the sea. The gathering in you has a chemistry, and one substance in it is cysteine. It is one of the twenty pieces every protein in you is built from, and one of only two that carry sulfur. Where two of them meet across a folded protein, they clasp sulfur to sulfur and hold its shape. The insulin in you holds together at three such clasps. A perm works by breaking those clasps in your hair and letting them join again.

You share this chemistry with one other energy. In your body, separate pieces fuse into a working that is more than any of them.

fields.essence: Some days things work out without any pushing, and you turn up in the right place at the right time. Delight lives in those days, the plain gladness of being alive in a body. Food tastes of something, and the air feels good on your skin. You love life more than any plan you have for it.
fields.glance:
Some days things work out without any pushing, and you turn up in the right place at the right time. Delight lives in those days, the plain gladness of being alive in a body. Food tastes of something, and the air feels good on your skin. You love life more than any plan you have for it.

At times you brace against how things will turn out, and worry takes the place of the gladness. The mind can be told that all is well, but it is the body that has to feel safe. Worry holds you the way a parent holds a struggling child, tighter while you fight and loose once you go still.

Hold your plans loosely enough to drop them when something better comes along. Stay open to surprises, and let life take you where it was already going. Make room for play, for good food and for the people you love. Good fortune finds you there, and you are glad to be alive when it does.
fields.iching:
The way ahead is open, and what you have worked at slowly begins to rise. Little stands in its way now. Do not worry about how it will go. Keep adding one small gain to the next, and do not overlook them, because they are what lifts you. Go and see someone who has already been where you are heading, and listen to them. Move toward what is warm and bright.

Honour where you came from as you rise, because your roots decide how long you stay up. Stay humble while you climb. People who climb fast and stop looking down miss the first signs of trouble. Calm, steady progress keeps you where you have climbed to.

Your thighs carry this time, the strongest muscles you have, the ones that lift you up a stair. Let the lift come from low down, and keep your shoulders loose. Earth over Wind is the hexagram of steady growth, the kind that rises a little every day. Wind, which here is also wood, is the part of you that grows into whatever room it finds. Earth is the part of you that gives way and lets that growth come through. The yielding sits above the growing because nothing rises far unless something makes room for it. This hexagram has long been read as a tree growing inside the ground. Your own progress grows the same way, out of sight a little each day, until one morning it shows. Small gains add up the same way, until something tall stands there. You rise the way anything living rises, a little at a time. Pushing Upward
fields.gene_keys:
Seriousness Delight Ecstasy Delight is the freedom of enjoying how rich it is to be alive. It begins with owning what is yours. Once you have seen something about yourself and let it go, you have more energy for being glad. Nothing really matters except life and love, and you feel this in your body.

A dry village sends for a rainmaker, and after a few days it rains, though he has no power over the weather. He has found what he is for, so he turns up where he likes, and it happens to rain. Find what you are for, and you need only turn up. Luck is what happens when you stop interfering with life. It tells you that you are in step with everything around you. People like this let the past go and ride the present, soft and at ease in their bodies, whatever they look like. Others are drawn to them without knowing why. Seriousness is the most common ailment there is. It is worrying, expecting, wishing life were other than it is right now. Your attention sits on what is coming or on what is gone, and the day in front of you goes by. It feels like being responsible. Mostly it is a grip, and it takes you out of life and love into control. Out of step with life, you find it rains whenever you least want it to.

It is handed down. Parents who are serious about life pass it into the air a child grows up in, however much they want the child to be happy. They have forgotten how to play. Even people on a spiritual path take it too seriously, and it shows in their faces. Ecstasy lives in the heart. It is your natural state whenever your mind is fully at rest. When the mind is needed it comes forward, and when the task is done the ecstasy returns. It lives in the shopping, at the family table, in the ordinary world. Others can feel it from across a room.

There is no work on earth more important than play. The heart knows only that it is alive and beating right now, and that knowing floods you. If you have felt this once, you can find it again. It begins with a slow, easy breath.
fields.human_design:
Embodiment Gate 46 is the love of the body, the joy of being in one and meeting life through its senses. It is the determination of a child in the womb, pushing its way out into the world. It draws you toward touch and movement, and toward caring for your body tenderly. Your body is not just something you live in. It carries your whole life, and it wants to hold as much life as it can.

Turned against, the same pressure leaves you at odds with your body. You may neglect it, hide it, or try to make it into something else so that you cannot be fully seen. Some are drawn to yoga or sport, and others fall out of step with their body altogether.
fields.tarot: This energy lives in the body, where every life first learns whether it is safe. It belongs to a family of four, the Ring of Matter, which shapes how you settle into a body up to the age of twenty-one. UL 57, Flight of the Tao, carries the months you spent in the womb. UL 48, Doorways of the Unknown, carries your second seven years. UL 18, Liberation of the Greater, carries your third. This one carries the first seven years. The tarot's major cards, its Arcana, bring five pictures to this one through its family and its two trigrams.
fields.body:
Warmth is the reason this energy is given to the blood. Your blood is made from what you eat, and it comes out red. It goes to your palms so they can hold, and to your feet so they can walk. The warmth in your skin is the blood arriving. When you are at ease in your body, it rises to the surface. Your hands are warm, and there is colour in your face. When you brace, it draws inward and your hands go cold. Your body decides this before you do.

Lay a cold hand flat on the warm skin of your belly. The heat you feel was made deep inside you and carried out to the skin by your blood. Your marrow makes two or three million new red cells every second, so you are in new blood three times a year. The gladness of being in a body has a chemistry, and one substance in it is alanine. It is one of the twenty pieces every protein in you is built from. Your body makes its own, though nearly every food with protein in it carries some too.

It took you seven years to arrive fully in your body. What you learned then is written in your posture, your breathing and the way you touch things. Hours into a walk with no food, your muscles send alanine through your blood to your liver. Your liver sends it back as sugar. A body is there to be filled completely by the life in it, and delight is what that feels like.

fields.essence: Hope is alive in you, and it grows strongest when life hems you in. You feel it as a pressure inside to become more than you have been. It keeps you true to what lit you up, even when nothing around you changes.
fields.glance:
Hope is alive in you, and it grows strongest when life hems you in. You feel it as a pressure inside to become more than you have been. It keeps you true to what lit you up, even when nothing around you changes.

Some stretches wear you out, and the same fear keeps coming back. Much of it was handed down to you before you were born. You cannot fix it or hand it to anyone, but it is yours to own. When you cannot see the next step, trust that the way will show itself in its own time.

Turn toward the fear you most want to avoid, and stay with it. What you look at steadily begins to change, though it takes years and cannot be hurried. You grow in the very place that hemmed you in, and your hope grows with you.
fields.iching:
Your reserves have run dry, and you are hemmed in on every side. From outside you may look fine, because the surface keeps its shape after what was under it has gone. Your strength is not lost. It is covered over for a while.

What you say in this time is not believed, however true it is. The more you explain yourself, the more it wears you out. So let what you do speak for you, and keep what you can do out of sight until its hour comes. Keep to what matters most to you, and do not let hardship talk you out of it. Climbing without a pause is what drained you, so the pause is part of the climb.

In the body this time lives in the mouth. Close it, and notice how much of you was leaving through your words. Accept what has fallen to you and live it out. Keep an easy face and hold your purpose firm within. A time this hard carries the start of a new growth. Lake over Water is the hexagram of being hemmed in and worn out. Water is the part of you that goes into danger and keeps moving. Lake is the part of you that stays open and glad and talks with people. The gladness sits above the danger because your ease shows on the outside while the hard part goes on within. This hexagram has long been read as a lake with no water in it, the water drained away beneath. You can look fine to everyone while your reserves run dry. Your strength is covered over for a while, not gone. Being worn out does not mean you have lost what you are here to do. Oppression
fields.gene_keys:
Oppression Transmutation Transfiguration Transmutation begins when you take the lid off and look at a fear. Held in your attention long enough, the fear changes, the way a thing changes in the heat of a fire. It does not simply lift. It becomes something else, and the heat of the change lifts you a little. Then the next fear shows itself, and you meet that one too.

Most of the change is small, one day after another. Now and then enough of it adds up to a leap, and your life stands somewhere new. The only thing in danger is the idea that anything about you is fixed. You let go of each thing you were sure you were. In time you greet the next fear almost gladly, because you know there is more light inside it. This change happens in your belly, the place where you feel things most. A weight sits on you that did not start in your own life. It is old fear, carried down the line of everyone you come from. It feels personal, though most of it is not. Few people look at it, because the deeper they look, the deeper it seems to go. So they keep a lid on it and escape into work and distraction, or they blame the people around them.

What is kept down does not stay down. It comes out in the shape of your life, and the pattern goes on repeating. No amount of thinking will solve it. The thing that frightens you most is the road that leads you out. Transfiguration is the change reaching all the way into your body. It works first through the mind, then through the feelings, and at last it reaches what you are made of. The elements in your body were made inside stars, and here you shine like one. Nobody reaches this by effort alone, and it comes as grace.

Life grows softer and quieter while the change goes on. The gaps between your thoughts widen until the thoughts are the interruption. What shows at the end is you as you really are, lit from within, like the sun after a storm.
fields.human_design:
Realization Gate 47 is the drive to make sense of what has happened to you. It turns raw experience into understanding, and the question it keeps asking is how. How do you make real the idea that lit you up? The way there is never straight. Confusion comes first, then frustration, then a stretch where nothing seems to move. Then the fog lifts and the whole thing comes clear at once.

From outside this can look like brooding, and people may take it for a bad mood. The drive needs a hopeful mind. If you have decided that nothing will come, you miss it when it does.
fields.tarot: This energy works on what was handed down to you, and it changes you from the inside first. It belongs to a family of four, the Ring of Alchemy, whose theme is turning something rough into something fine. UL 6, Harmonious Mirage, carries the walls coming down between you and someone close. UL 40, Eternal Wellspring, carries your new openness out into a community. UL 64, Communion, carries the fresh possibilities that open for you next. This one carries the change in your old ways. Its family and its two trigrams bring five of the tarot's major cards, its Arcana, to this one.
fields.body:
The past is the reason this energy is given to the neocortex, the thin outer layer of your brain. It is wired after birth, year by year, out of what happens to you. So your whole life so far is written into it, and it cannot put down what it has learned. When this energy stirs, this layer is turning your old experience over and looking for the pattern in it.

The layer has no feeling of its own. A surgeon can work on it while the person is awake and talking, because the part of you that takes everything in cannot feel itself. So you feel the weight of the past lower in your body, and the understanding catches up later. The change in you has a chemistry, and one substance in it is glycine. The red of your blood begins with it, because glycine is the first step in making the part of each red cell that carries iron. Your body makes glycine for itself and takes in more from food, most of all from the skin and bones of meat and fish.

This energy shares that substance with three others in you, one family whose work is turning something rough into something fine. Its own part of the work is letting your old ways change. That change happens in your body before it shows anywhere else, and to be in it is to be fully alive.

fields.essence: Resourcefulness wakes in you when someone needs more than you know how to give. You meet them open, without a plan, and the answer rises from somewhere below what you have learned. It is rarely what you expected, and it is just what the moment needs. What you do not know turns out to be a doorway.
fields.glance:
Resourcefulness wakes in you when someone needs more than you know how to give. You meet them open, without a plan, and the answer rises from somewhere below what you have learned. It is rarely what you expected, and it is just what the moment needs. What you do not know turns out to be a doorway.

Some days a quiet fear says you are not enough for what is coming, and you want to learn one more thing first. Sit with not knowing instead, and the fear has less to hold on to.

Give what comes up to the people who ask for it, and there will be more of it. You need only a little more than enough, and it arrives when it is needed. Again and again, you find you can do far more than you thought.
fields.iching:
You have been worn out, and now you come to the source. Everything around you may change, the work and the people, and the source does not. It gives neither more nor less than before. People come, draw from it and leave, and it is there for the next one. What you are facing goes deeper than it looks from the top.

Go all the way down. Water at the bottom helps nobody until it is brought up. The drawing fails in two ways only: the rope stops short of the water, or the jar breaks on the way up. So reach the whole way, and carry what you find in something whole. Then share it, and help the people beside you with their work.

The body's part is the ear and the thigh. The ear listens down into the dark, and the legs walk to the source and back. Stand still for a moment and listen before you reach. Water over Wind is the hexagram of the source you draw from. Wind, read here as wood, is the part of you that goes down gently into what you cannot see. Water is the depth in you that holds what you need. Water sits above because what you find down there is lifted up into your day. This hexagram has long been read as a well. A town can move, but the well stays, and whoever comes can draw from it. It also asks you to keep people at their work, helping one another. What you need is under you already, and it is there for everyone who comes. The Well
fields.gene_keys:
Inadequacy Resourcefulness Wisdom Resourcefulness begins when you stop hiding from the fear and sit with it. You let a bucket down into the dark and pull it up to see what is there. What comes up surprises you, and so much of it comes out of the dark. It comes when you arrive open and unready, without the answer. Each time it comes up full, you trust it a little more, and the fear slowly loses its hold. The body takes about seven years to unlearn the old pattern.

It is meant for other people. They come and let the bucket down, and there is more each time. Used only for yourself, it dries up. Serving everyone is the surest way to serve yourself. It will not do the same thing twice, so keep moving. It needs the sky and the woods, and it fades behind a screen. The fear of not being enough sits low in the body, and it does not come and go. It has no reason. It was laid down between seven and fourteen, while your feelings were forming and the world sent them mixed messages. It says someone else knows what you do not. So you reach for more knowledge, or a system detailed enough to feel like solid ground. None of it reaches the fear, because nothing outside you can. Underneath, the fear is of the dark itself. It is like standing at night at the edge of deep, cold water with no bottom in sight.

That water is not empty. It is warm underneath, and full of light. Tension is something you learned, and as a child you were gentle. Go gently into the dark, and it is gentle with you. Wisdom comes from not knowing, and it was in you before anything you learned. Knowing takes effort to gather, while not knowing is already there. Wisdom wells up gently from underneath, and if you grab it, it hardens into knowledge. It is like water, empty and full at once, taking the shape of whatever holds it. You are wise because you do not know you are wise.

It looks completely ordinary. Nothing inside you has changed, and seeing that is the whole change. Every feeling is allowed to rise and pass, the fear of not being enough among them. The body feels each one, and nothing in you is wiser than the body.
fields.human_design: Depth Gate 48 is the pressure to go below the surface of a thing until you reach its heart. It does not work things out step by step. It gathers what it knows from experience, time spent and close watching, until the pattern underneath shows. Its fear is not knowing enough. The more you know, the more you see how much you do not, though you often know more than anyone in the room. Held too tightly, it waits for certainty before it acts, and the waiting can take over. It works best when you put what you found to use.
fields.tarot: This energy brings people what they need in the world of things. It belongs to a family of four, the Ring of Matter. UL 18, Liberation of the Greater, carries the instinct for what has gone wrong. UL 46, Fountain of Light, carries the ease of a body that has stopped fighting. UL 57, Flight of the Tao, carries the hunch that knows the way. This one carries the answer that comes when you are asked. Together the four shaped you from the womb to twenty-one, in body, feeling and mind. Five major cards of the tarot, its Arcana, stand around this energy.
fields.body:
Return is the reason this energy is given to the lymph. The lymph is water that has already been your blood. The finest vessels let water out into the spaces between your cells. Most of it is drawn straight back, and a second set of vessels gathers the rest, two or three litres a day. They carry it up to the blood at the base of your neck. There is no pump to move it. It rises from your feet with every step and every breath, so it moves when you move and pools when you sit. Beside it, the spleen under your left ribs holds a store of blood back until the body calls for it.

Sit for a few hours and your ankles grow fuller. Walk for a few minutes and they empty, because the water down there was waiting for a muscle to lift it. What went down comes back. The depth in you has a chemistry, and alanine is part of it. Your body makes it for itself, and you also take it in from almost any food with protein, meat or beans. About one in twelve of the pieces your body is built from is alanine.

This chemistry sends you out into the world of things to get away from the fear, into work and money. Nothing you buy reaches the fear, because it lives in your body itself. What this energy in you is for is bringing people what they need. Whatever you own will wear out one day, as all matter does. Small, ordinary things can teach you more than the cleverest thinker.

fields.essence: The urge for change is alive in you when the way you live stops fitting. It starts in you and in your closest bonds, before it reaches the wider world. You feel it first in your belly, as a warmth that shows you plainly what has to go. At its best you understand how things work, so you know what to keep and how long the change will take.
fields.glance:
The urge for change is alive in you when the way you live stops fitting. It starts in you and in your closest bonds, before it reaches the wider world. You feel it first in your belly, as a warmth that shows you plainly what has to go. At its best you understand how things work, so you know what to keep and how long the change will take.

For a while the people closest to you may seem harder to live with. They are not harder; you are seeing old hurts more clearly, and each one you let go shows a smaller one underneath. Forgive yourself for what you did before you could see.

Whenever something sets you off, look under the feeling for the need behind it. Once you see the need, it loses its hold on you, even if it stays. Act from goodwill toward everyone the change will touch. Some people will step back, and others will ask how you did it. Out of the ashes of the old way comes a closer union with the people you love.
fields.iching:
A habit, an arrangement or a bond you live inside has stopped fitting. Now it has to change as a whole. People trust a change like this only once it is done. Before then they doubt it and dislike it, and you may doubt it too. So you do not make it in a hurry. It has its day, and when that day comes you will know it.

Until then, change the one thing you can: yourself. A change that asks everyone but you to change is the old way in new clothes. Make sure the new way is better, and not only different.

Let the change come the way one season follows another, each one clear when it arrives. It starts in your heart, and your mouth speaks only after your heart has changed. Lake over Fire is the hexagram of changing the way you live. Fire is the part of you that sees what is still alive and what has died. Lake is the part of you that says so out loud and brings others with you. They sit this way round because what you see and what you say are at odds until one of them gives way. This hexagram has long been read as a skin that is shed. An animal that has grown sheds its old skin whole, and you leave an old way of living the same way. You do not go back to a life you have outgrown. Revolution
fields.gene_keys:
Reaction Revolution Rebirth Watched instead of obeyed, the heat becomes a way of sorting. A need rises in your body and you watch it rise. You see whether it is met, and you judge neither. Then you ask whether it was needed at all. Often the body was not hungry, and you ate anyway. Once the loud needs quiet down, you hear the quiet ones, for beauty or for a kind word to yourself. Some needs stay and some go. The sorting is uncomfortable, and it is doing you good.

Your cut grows sharper the longer you use it. You can show someone what they do not need and what they do, and it can turn their life around. Your own life gets simpler, more beautiful and harder to sell things to. You can still have the cake, because it is the right afternoon and the right cake to share. No need drove you to it. This is the revolution: to live simply, and to live well. Someone close to you does a small thing, and the heat is up in you before you have thought. A cup left out or a question not answered, and you are already braced for a fight. You cannot react on your own. It takes another person, and it runs hottest with the one you share a bed with. Under each flare is the fear of being left. The more finely you feel, the closer to the surface that fear lies.

Most of what sets you off is a need you did not know you had, like a coffee at the same hour each morning. Miss it once and the whole day goes wrong. You set these needs yourself, then let other people trip over them. A need makes an expectation, and an expectation makes a disappointment that feels like something they did to you. As long as you are the good one and they are the wrong one, the heat has you. Born a second time, you carry nothing of the pattern you start life with. That pattern is wiped clean, not improved. A butterfly keeps nothing of the caterpillar, though it comes from nowhere else. Change goes round and round, the same fight over and over, until one leap takes you clear of the circle. That leap comes because it must, and still you have to make it.

After it you cannot be a loner. Two people who love each other are never only two, because the love between them is a third. You are more yourself than ever, and you can no longer hide.
fields.human_design:
The Catalyst Gate 49 is the pressure in you to live by a principle, and to act the moment it is broken. It does not change things for the sake of change. It reads the agreement underneath a bond, between two people or in a whole country. It feels the day the values that held that agreement together have gone. Then it presses you to end it and make a new one on something truer. From inside it feels like loyalty: you keep your word, and you expect others to keep theirs.

The work is knowing when to hold on and when to let go. This pressure can quit too soon, backing away from real closeness. It can also stay far too long in a dead arrangement, afraid of the upheaval, until giving way has turned into giving yourself up. When you do leave, leave with your integrity whole.
fields.tarot: This energy carries change outward, into a home or a whole society. It belongs to a family of two, the Ring of the Whirlwind, which shares one chemistry in the body. UL 55, Untouched Perfection, carries the same change inward. There it is the quiet freedom of a life no longer ruled by its needs. This one carries it out into the world. The ring and the two trigrams bring five of the tarot's major cards, its Arcana.
fields.body:
The solar plexus holds this energy because it is the place in you that gets set off. The solar plexus is a knot of nerves on the front of your spine, behind the stomach. It sits a hand's depth behind the soft hollow under your breastbone. Nerves run out from it to everything in your belly. One reaches the gland that readies you to run or fight. A fright travels this road, and the charge is in your blood within seconds. Each need you have forgotten is a wire across your middle. A touch on it sets off that charge before you know what was said. You lose your centre there because it is your centre. Each need you see through takes one wire out, and your breath sinks a little lower.

Feel it when a door slams behind you: the jolt is under your ribs before you have turned. That is the part of you that fires first. The change this energy makes begins in your body, and it needs heat. The hotter it runs, the faster it goes. What it builds in you is built from what was already there, out of the ashes of the old. It has a substance in you, shared with one other energy, and the substance is histidine. It goes into every protein your body makes. You cannot make it, so your body takes it in from meat, eggs or beans. What your body makes from it lies behind the warmth and redness where something has got in, a sting or a bite.

Draw a fingernail firmly once across your inner forearm. Within a minute the line reddens, a flush spreads around it, and the line itself may rise pale as you watch. What reddens along the stroke is heat your body made on purpose, from a substance it could not make at all.

fields.essence: A household or a team has fallen out of balance, and you can feel what is missing. Balance lives in you as a feel for what the people near you need, and for what has gone off. You sense it low in your body before you can put it into words. You add a little here and take a little away there, the way a cook tastes a pot and adjusts it. People settle around you without knowing why.
fields.glance:
A household or a team has fallen out of balance, and you can feel what is missing. Balance lives in you as a feel for what the people near you need, and for what has gone off. You sense it low in your body before you can put it into words. You add a little here and take a little away there, the way a cook tastes a pot and adjusts it. People settle around you without knowing why.

There are days when everyone near you is out of tune at once, and you feel it in your own body. Do not force them back into line, and do not walk away. Stay in the middle yourself, and let them find their own way back to it.

Start with your own balance, since a group finds its balance one person at a time. Change one habit at a time, slowly. Say out loud what is hidden, so nothing sits unspoken between you. In time the balance stops being work, and you melt into it.
fields.iching:
An old way of doing things has ended, and something new has to be set up in its place. Setting it up is harder than pulling the old one down. What you have been handed is raw, and it has to be cooked before it can feed anyone. Feed what is best in the people around you first, since the new grows out of them.

Clean the pot before you cook, because whatever has gone stale from before will spoil what is new. Take your right place and stand in it, and your life sets firm the way bronze sets in a mould. Go gently, and your ears grow clear and your eyes sharp. Watch the heat to the end, since one slip near the finish can lose the whole meal.

Your ears and eyes do the work now. The ears hear what the people at your table need, and the eyes see when the food is ready. Stand the way the pot stands over the fire, steady on three legs while the heat does its work. Fire over Wind is the hexagram of turning what you were given into what feeds people. Wind, which here is also wood, is the patience in you that keeps feeding a task a little at a time. Fire is the clear sight in you that knows when a thing is ready. The seeing sits above the feeding because you can only judge what has been given time to cook. This hexagram has long been read as a bronze pot on three legs over a fire. Whatever raw thing you put in, you take out as food for a whole house. It is also read as the new order set up once an old one has fallen, which is harder than pulling the old one down. Whatever you inherit feeds people only once you have cooked it through. The Cauldron
fields.gene_keys:
Corruption Equilibrium Harmony Tuned by ear, the same string in you holds its note. You find the middle by being thrown off it. Pour yourself in too hard and you tense up. Hold back and only watch, and you give up. Each extreme hurts, and the hurt sends you back to the centre.

Then you can walk into a room where everything has gone to pieces and feel what is missing. You put the parts back together, and harmony is possible again. A parent's unlived life shapes a child more than anything else, and what parents hide from each other comes out in their children. So balance cannot be imposed on anyone. Each person has to be trusted with their own. Something in you was miscopied before you were born, and it sounds like a string that rasps instead of holding its note. It is not your fault, and it is yours anyway. You meet it first in the world, in crooked dealing and in people who answer to nobody. It shows up out there because it is wound around the inside of you. Nobody clears it from the world without first clearing it in themselves.

The fault stays alive because you give up on it. No one else bothers, you tell yourself, so why should you. You have tried and prayed, and it is still there. Or you go the other way: one bad day and you tighten up and try too hard, which only makes it worse. You are like a child learning an instrument, and the sound is painful at first. Then, one small tune at a time, your notes start to hold. Your note joins a music that was already playing. Balance can be lost, and this harmony cannot. Nobody makes it, and all you can do is enter it. First every sense of being separate falls away. Then your body becomes a chamber that rings, and in the end the chamber itself dissolves.

Every life is a note in one piece of music, and the music grows sweeter. It plays under your days whether you hear it or not. When one person arrives here, what was hidden comes to light around them, and the whole group shifts. You are the instrument, and the music plays through you.
fields.human_design:
Values Gate 50 presses you to look after your people. You feel responsible for whether they are well, fed in body and in spirit, and for the values that hold them together. It is a mother's drive, whoever carries it. Under it runs a fear of not caring enough, of letting them down. The fear makes you take on more than is yours, until you are carrying people who could walk.

From the outside this can look like meddling, or like rules so strict that no one may make their own mistakes. Care driven by guilt empties the one who gives it. Look after yourself first, since that is the only way there is anything left to give. Trusting the people you love to look after themselves is its own kind of care.
fields.tarot: This energy brings a group into balance. It belongs to a family of two, the Ring of the Illuminati. Its theme is people working together as equals, with no one ruling over them. UL 44, Sophia's Orchestra, carries teamwork and the sense of who belongs together. This one carries the balance that lets them work as one. Five of the tarot's major cards, its Arcana, each show one side of the balance you keep.
fields.body:
The spleen holds this energy, and the reason is cooking. It has long been pictured as a pot on a stove, warmed from below, that turns what you eat into blood and strength. Nothing you eat is yours until it has been cooked there. From there the strength goes out to your arms and legs.

The organ itself sits under your left ribs, behind the stomach, and it does not cook. It skims the pot. All of your blood passes through it many times a day, and it takes out the worn cells and anything that should not be there. What goes round stays fit to feed you. For some months before you were born, it was one of the places your blood was made. Inside every cell of you, a messenger copies the instructions for life. It can misread them, the way fear misreads what people say in a room. This energy has a substance in you, and the substance is glutamic acid. Your body makes it itself. Nearly every other amino acid your body takes apart hands its nitrogen to this one. In your brain it is the messenger that says go, and the one that says stop is made from it in a single step.

Balance starts down at this level, in your cells. A real sense of belonging somewhere can bring it all the way there. The same substance runs through one other energy, the sense of who belongs together, and it ties that sense to your balance. The liquid in each of your cells tunes itself to whatever you line up with. If you live among chaos, chaos is what your body feels like.

fields.essence: Initiative is alive in you as the nerve to go first, onto a path nobody has walked. When something you did not see coming shakes your day, you are the one who moves. You feel it as a jolt of charge, and your body is ready before your mind has caught up.
fields.glance:
Initiative is alive in you as the nerve to go first, onto a path nobody has walked. When something you did not see coming shakes your day, you are the one who moves. You feel it as a jolt of charge, and your body is ready before your mind has caught up.

At times that charge turns to nerves, and you brace for the next blow. Bracing only makes the blow land harder. Let the fright come, give it room, and it passes through you.

Take the step that is yours, without waiting for it to feel safe. The more you believe in yourself and act on it, the more life comes to meet you. Each shock you take this way leaves you steadier on your feet. Others see it and find the nerve to go their own way.
fields.iching:
Something you did not see coming has happened, and it has shaken the ground you stood on. At first there is fear, then laughter once you see you are still here. Everyone near you felt it too. Most people jump and then forget it. They go back to talking as before and learn nothing.

This time asks you to use the fright. You cannot choose what strikes, and you can choose how you answer it. Let the shaking make you look at your life, then set in order what it shows you. The care that fear puts in you is where the good fortune comes from. Keep to the calm at the centre of the storm, and go on with the work that is yours. Whatever you lose now comes back to you in time.

Your feet do the work now. Put your weight down through both of them and feel the ground still there. Thunder over Thunder is the hexagram of a shock that shakes you, and what you do with it. Thunder is the jolt in you that makes you start at a sudden crash. Here it comes a second time, before the first has died away. You can shrug off one jolt, and the second reaches all the way down. This hexagram has long been read as a person in a temple who spills no wine from the ladle when the thunder breaks. Your hand stays on the work in front of you while the noise goes past. Fear comes first, then laughter, once you see you are still standing. You can be frightened and still keep hold of what is yours to carry. The Arousing Thunder
fields.gene_keys:
Agitation Initiative Awakening Initiative starts when you stop copying anyone and follow your own lead. There is no net under it. The crowd keeps to what is safe, so it admires this path and fears it at once. Teachers can inspire you, and none of them can tell you where your feet go. Whatever you fear most, you meet on this path, and you get past it.

A shock met with harshness makes you hold on tighter, the way a cold wind makes a man pull his coat close. You lean into it and give it room instead, the way the sun gets the coat off. The charge that rattled you becomes the push to make something new. Life rewards you for it, and sometimes it shocks you with good fortune. Life is not in your control, and some part of you never forgets it. Something could happen to you at any moment. You see it happen to others, one house hit while the next is spared, and your body waits for its turn. Trust in life is not a thought or a mood. It is felt in your body, or it is not. Without it you stay jumpy and on edge, waiting for the next crack of thunder.

That restless charge wants a way out. It pushes you to do something, anything, just to feel it go. You may shy away from life, or rush at it. You may need to come first, not to grow but to stand above the others. Underneath all of it is the one shock nobody escapes, your own death. Pushing that thought away is what takes the life out of your days. Awakening comes once, without warning, and it stays. There are only two states, awake and asleep, and anyone who draws a ladder between them is still asleep. No practice brings it, and it has come to kind people and cruel ones alike. It comes to someone so fully themselves that it has no choice. You do not take the leap. The leap takes you.

After it, nothing in you is separate enough for a shock to strike. You become a vessel that only gives, with nothing in the way of life flowing through. That giving is love, though not always the warm kind. The thunder you once feared is now the sound of your own giving.
fields.human_design: Initiation Gate 51 sits in the Will Center, near your heart, and it is the gate of shock. It presses you to meet a sudden turn and come out of it stronger. It gives you a taste for the unknown and a pull away from what is comfortable, and people feel a charge around you. When it runs well, a shock becomes the start of something, and your sense of purpose holds through the turn. When it runs badly, you chase upheaval for its own sake and jolt people just to jolt them. Or you try to control every outcome, and that drains you.
fields.tarot: This energy steps off the known path, a step every human life has to take. It belongs to a family of six, the Ring of Humanity, whose theme is the whole human story. UL 25, The Mysteries Play, carries the wound you start from. UL 38, Inner Light Symphony, carries your fight with your own shadows. UL 17, Pearl of Christos, carries the limits of your mind. UL 21, Beyond Binary, carries your letting go of control. UL 10, Internal Treasure, carries finding your true self. This one carries your waking up. Its family and its doubled trigram bring three of the tarot's major cards, its Arcana, to this one.
fields.body:
Decision is the reason this energy is given to your gallbladder. It is a small bag tucked under the right side of your liver, and it makes nothing of its own. Between meals it holds what your liver makes and draws the water out, until the store is five to ten times as strong. When a meal reaches your gut, it gets one signal. It squeezes, empties within the hour, and goes still again. You know this from inside: the long hours of holding before a leap, then the moment you go. When you find the gall to do a bold thing, you are naming this organ.

Find the place under your right ribs where the flat muscle of your belly meets them. The tip of your gallbladder lies just beneath, too soft to feel. Rest your hand there, on the part of you that waits and then goes all at once. At some point in your life you leave the crowd and head off alone into the wild country of your own heart. That step off the known path has a substance in you, and it is arginine. Your body builds it into every protein you have. Your body makes it for itself, and more comes in with eggs, beans or a handful of seeds. The substance in you was first found in seedlings, as a salt of silver, and is named for silver.

You share this substance with five other energies, and all six are about being human. What wakes you also wakes the people close to you, one family after another, until everyone has heard it.

fields.essence: At the end of a cycle, stillness settles in you. Your breath drops low into your belly, and your weight rests on whatever holds you. Nothing in you is in a hurry. You see your life in seasons rather than days, and the people near you slow down without being asked.
fields.glance:
At the end of a cycle, stillness settles in you. Your breath drops low into your belly, and your weight rests on whatever holds you. Nothing in you is in a hurry. You see your life in seasons rather than days, and the people near you slow down without being asked.

Some days the pause feels like being stuck, and on others you cannot sit still at all. Both come when your breath has risen high into your chest. Let it fall back down to the floor of your body, and the pause becomes rest again.

Once you are calm, the way forward is plain. While you rest, the next thing is already forming out of sight, the way buds form on a branch before a single blossom shows. It opens in its own time, and you are ready when it does.
fields.iching:
Whatever you are asking about has gone as far as it can go for now. A cycle has closed, and before the next one opens there is time to stop and see where you stand. Your eyes reach for what they see and your hands for what they can hold. Your back reaches for nothing; it stands straight and carries you. Rest your attention there, and the reaching lets go of you. You can be among people and still be alone, doing what is right whether anyone is watching or not.

Stop at the point where it is right to stop. Stop when it is time to stop, move when it is time to move, and nothing is missed. When you are lost, do not wander. Stay where you are, and a path clears. Once you have stopped, you can see what is coming, which you cannot see while you are still moving. Watch for a stop held with a clenched jaw, in anger or in pride. That is stubbornness, and it only looks like stillness.

Sit straight and let your weight go down. Keep your thoughts on where you are and on what is yours to do. Mountain over Mountain is the hexagram of knowing when to stop. Mountain is the part of you that can stop and stay stopped. Here it stands a second time, so you are still on the inside as well as the outside. It sits on itself because a thing that has gone as far as it can go has nowhere left to go but rest. This hexagram has long been read as a back kept still. Your eyes, hands and mouth all reach for something, and your back only holds you straight. You stop when it is time to stop, and move when it is time to move. Keeping Still Mountain
fields.gene_keys:
Stress Restraint Stillness Everything alive has its own speed, and you know this in your body. A yew seed and a sunflower seed are about the same size. The sunflower is full grown within a few months. The yew may take ten years to reach that height, then live for thousands. The bigger the thing you are growing, the slower it starts, and hurrying it disturbs the ground it was sown in.

What you begin from fear carries the fear into everything that grows from it. What you begin with a clear wish to be of use already holds all it will need. It even draws the right people at the right time. Your part is to leave it alone while it grows. Someone who lives like this steadies everyone around them, the way an anchor lets a boat rest and find where it is. One question sets your pace: how can I be of the greatest use? The pressure you live under is not only yours. Everyone alive puts it into the air, and in a city you cannot get away from it, even alone at home. The first thing it does is lift your breath. Somewhere in growing up your breath left your belly for the top of your chest, and the day runs short from there. Time changes with it. It goes too fast or too slow, and you are always behind.

You hand the trouble to your mind, and your mind sets out to fix it. The thinking is the pressure, so every plan to end it feeds it. Nobody enjoys the rush, but most of us get used to it, and then we need it. Your body sounds an alarm when your rhythm falls out of step with the world around you. Most people hear it so often that it sounds like silence. The alarm is on your side. It asks you to stop, breathe low and come back to the base of yourself. Slow yourself down far enough and everything in you stops. Speed up far enough and it all runs together, which is also a stop. Stillness waits at both ends, and it is full of life. Your body is rebuilt every hour you are alive, and underneath all that building nothing moves.

Gaps open between your thoughts. A feeling rises so slowly you could turn it over in your hands before it breaks the surface. It spreads through you like a coin dropped in a pond, then settles back into the quiet. You watch the drama of your life from a little way off. Near you, other people's thoughts go quiet and time seems to slow. Whatever moves in you now moves only to meet the same stillness in someone else.
fields.human_design: Stillness Gate 52 is a pressure low in your body to find the one thing worth your focus. It is a charge held at the base of your trunk, strong enough to drive a whole life, waiting to be aimed. Think of a bow drawn back with no target yet. While you wait, you can see the whole of what needs to happen and the order it needs to happen in. So much at once can freeze you, or send the charge into whatever is nearest. When you find the thing, you can work at it for hours and forget the room around you. The hard part then is stopping. From outside, the waiting can look slow and the focus can look like not caring. You are holding still until you know where to aim, then giving that one thing all you have.
fields.tarot: This energy holds pressure steady, and it belongs to the Ring of Seeking, a family of six that each press you to look for more. Ordinary Valiance (UL 15) draws people to you. Nobel Spark (UL 39) stirs you to act. Creation Oscillation (UL 53) makes you grow, Everlasting Bounty (UL 54) makes you rise, and Rhythm of Life (UL 58) makes you feel alive. This one keeps all of that in check, so your search lasts long enough to find something. The Hermit comes to you three times here, through the ring and both trigrams, as the seeker who stops to see.
fields.body:
This energy lives at the floor of your body, in the perineum, and the reason is the breath. The perineum is the small floor of muscle between your legs. Each breath you take rises from it and returns to it, and nothing in you is lower. At the other end of your spine is the soft spot on the crown of your head, and the two hold the spine between them. When your breath reaches the floor, you are at rest, and everything above it settles. When it stops short, high in your chest, you are already hurrying.

Sit down and let your weight settle. It rests on two bones, one under each side, with the perineum between them. You sit on either side of it, never on it. Breathe in and it gives a little, with your belly. Breathe out and it lifts. It has moved with every breath since your first. Let your breath go all the way down to it, and you are resting on the part of you that stops. There is more life in you than you can use at once, and it presses to get out. That pressure has a chemistry in you, and serine is part of it. It is one of the twenty small pieces every protein in you is built from. Your cells hold a protein still or let it go by pinning a small charge onto it. Four times in five, that charge goes onto a serine. You share this chemistry with five other energies.

Under fear your body releases adrenaline, the rush that keeps you moving. You can get so used to the rush that you go looking for it. In deep stillness your body releases other chemicals, ones that quiet your thoughts, so the stillness is in your body before it reaches your mind.

fields.essence: At the start of something new, the urge to begin rises low in your body. You feel more alive in that first push than at any other time. This urge comes and goes in pulses, and each time it returns a new start is ready in you.
fields.glance:
At the start of something new, the urge to begin rises low in your body. You feel more alive in that first push than at any other time. This urge comes and goes in pulses, and each time it returns a new start is ready in you.

Some days the urge is gone, and you cannot make yourself start. Nothing is wrong with you, since the pulse has only gone quiet. The harm comes from starting early out of fear of being late.

So ask what a new start is really made of, because it goes on the way it began. Start only when every part of you says yes, then slow down and let the thing grow. Someone else may carry it to the end, and it is still yours. Year by year your life outgrows its old shape, and each start reaches wider than the last.
fields.iching:
Something has begun that will take years, and the years are part of it. What comes quickly leaves the same way, and what grows by degrees stays. Others will seem to move faster. Let them, because your success will come in time and it will last longer than theirs.

Be firm and be slow. Take one small, honest step and then the next, the way a good marriage is made. Play to the nature you have rather than the one you wish you had. When people are coarse with you, answer with dignity, because how you carry yourself is part of what you are building.

The thighs do this work in the body, the long muscles that carry you uphill one step at a time. They keep a pace the head does not. If you are already at the top in your mind, come back to the step you are on. Wind over Mountain is the hexagram of growth that takes years. Wind is the part of you that goes on, a little further every day, without force. Mountain is the stillness in you that stays put and keeps what it has. The going on sits above the stillness because only what is rooted can keep growing. This hexagram has long been read as a tree on a mountain. A tree up there grows slowly, and its roots matter more than its height. Its six lines follow a wild goose that lands by stages, the way you arrive in anything new. What you build slowly is what lasts. Development
fields.gene_keys:
Immaturity Expansion Superabundance Maturing feels like slowing down. A mature river is wider and slower than the stream it was. When your breath drops deeper, life seems to move in slow motion while your seeing grows sharper. The restless drive that chased the next thing turns round to face what it was running from. It uses your hardest times as fuel.

What grows then is your whole life at once. Your work keeps outgrowing its shape, the way life outgrows every shape it takes. Awareness, love and making grow together, since your life is one thing and not a set of rooms. This growth comes without effort. It brings calm instead of excitement, and perspective instead of ambition. The way in is to give way, to let life carry you and drop your ideas of who you are. Life turns out simpler than you thought. Looking outside for the answer to a problem that can only be solved inside is where this energy starts. The cause seems to lie with the boss or the town. So you try to fix it out there, where the fix never holds. Under it runs a restlessness that says the next thing will be the one. A life can be spent on the next thing, always one step short. Nothing outside has ever given anyone the fulfilment it promised. Most people keep looking until a book, a teacher or a loss turns them round.

Flowers open at different times of year. Snowdrops come up through the snow, while others wait for autumn and are just as beautiful. People ripen at different times too, and nobody is behind. Under all of it lies a fear of not existing, rooted in you like a weed. The grace here is seeing how much of what you do grows from that fear. Once you see it, your heart begins to trust life as it is. Beyond plenty there is a place where nothing is counted. It is neither plenty nor lack, but the source both come from. The seeking of a whole life ends here, when you find that nothing is missing. Life is endless beginnings with no endings, and you watch it with no stake in how it turns out. The excitement is gone, and so is the weight.

From here the rush of the world is a game in time. Run in it and you feel it slow around you. The fruit that was ripening drops from the branch on its own. All that remains to learn is the art of letting go.
fields.human_design:
Beginnings Gate 53 is the pressure to start something new, felt low in the body. It gives a new thing its first push, before anyone has agreed it should exist. You feel more alive at that point than at any other. Your part is to strike the match, and someone else may tend the fire. You do not have to carry every fire to its end.

Under pressure, the urge rushes to start out of fear of being late. It then burns out when the thing does not come as hoped. After enough of that, you may hesitate before starting anything at all. It works best when you start only once every part of you agrees, then let go of how it turns out. Value what you started, even when someone else finishes it.
fields.tarot: This energy pushes outward, and every push is part of a search. It belongs to a family of six, the Ring of Seeking, and each member is a pressure that sends you looking. UL 15, Ordinary Valiance, is the pull you have on people. UL 39, Nobel Spark, is the push that stirs people awake. UL 52, Timeless Blossom, is your power to hold still. UL 54, Everlasting Bounty, is your wish to rise. UL 58, Rhythm of Life, is your joy in being alive. This one is your life outgrowing its shape. Four of the tarot's major cards, its Arcana, show how this energy moves in you.
fields.body:
Growing up is the reason this energy is given to the adrenals. These two small glands grow up in stages, to a clock nobody sets. You were born with them far too big, each a third the size of the kidney it sits on. In your first weeks they lost a third of themselves, as the part built for life in the womb died away. By two they were back to their birth weight, and they reached full size around your puberty.

You can check this by memory rather than by touch. At about seven the glands began a new work, and the first sign was that your sweat changed. Most people remember the year. Growing up had started, before you knew it. The glands sit high at the back under your lowest ribs, each the size of the top joint of your thumb. They cannot be felt. The pressure in you to begin has a chemistry, and one substance in it is serine. Every protein in you is built from twenty pieces, and serine is one of them. It sits in the outer skin of every cell you have and in the sheath around each nerve. At its lowest, this pressure comes out as stress and a wish to be rich. What you build then is a stockpile, held out of fear.

The same pressure shows you what your wanting, your greed and your fear are made of. In time it teaches you that what you were seeking is already in you. Slowed down, with your breath deeper, it becomes a flow that widens and narrows with its seasons. You share this chemistry with five other energies.

fields.essence: Ambition lives in you as the wish to rise. You feel it most when you start low, in a place where others got there first. Carried with trust, it settles a room before you speak, and people want to work with you.
fields.glance:
Ambition lives in you as the wish to rise. You feel it most when you start low, in a place where others got there first. Carried with trust, it settles a room before you speak, and people want to work with you.

Some days you measure yourself against everyone above you. Then the wish to rise starts to grab, and people feel it and pull back. Notice the grab without fighting it, and the trust comes back.

Know what you are worth, and win your own approval first, so you have no one to convince. Take no shortcuts, because rushing ahead before you are ready costs more than the long way. Keep what you gain moving between people, and the bounty keeps coming back. You rise, and you bring others up with you.
fields.iching:
You have come into a place below the one you hoped for, and someone else already holds the first seat. A change came that was not in your hands, and you are inside it now. Pushing forward from here goes wrong. Nothing you force will help you.

Know what you are worth, and stand in it without show. When you are sure of your worth you have no need to convince anyone. Do not take the first offer, because waiting can work for you. Rise only by ways you would be glad to be seen using. Whatever happens, keep your composure where others can see it. You begin with no power, and by the end you may be the one holding it. Before you start, decide what you are willing to pay, and pay no more.

Thunder is read as the feet, so this time shows in how you walk into a room. Set each foot down fully, and walk in as someone who came to stay. Thunder over Lake is the hexagram of coming into a place below the one you want. Lake is the delight in you that draws you toward what is above you. Thunder is the part of you that jumps to act. The delight sits underneath because a liking moves you before you have thought it through. This hexagram has long been read as a young woman who marries in as a second wife, below the first. A newcomer in a house already arranged finds a place by how she carries herself. The same holds wherever you work under someone else's rule. Your worth, carried quietly, raises you further than any push. The Marrying Maiden
fields.gene_keys:
Greed Aspiration Ascension Aspiration is the same wanting with its trust kept, pointed at something higher. The word shares a root with breathing: you breathe in the raw fuel of the want and refine it. Ambition aims at one goal. Aspiration is wider, a reach toward something higher that you sense before you can name it. It starts with honesty about the wish to rise in you.

Then one question cuts through it: how can I be of use? What you gather goes down to the people below you, the way fruit falls and feeds the roots of its own tree. Your reach turns into hope you carry into rooms where people feel stuck in lives of compromise. When it runs too hot, life brings you back down to earth, and that is part of the gift. Greed is the wish to rise with the trust taken out. It wants to be at the top and to look it, with the new car and the bigger house. It is greediest in love. You taste love and chase more of it, then blame the other person when it slips away. Fear sits at its root, the old fear of not surviving if you do not climb. So it trades its own honesty in a moment for what it wants, and that is its downfall. It cannot trust its allies either, since they want the same things.

None of this is wrong in itself. It is raw fuel, and a child who says I want that is only being honest. Seen for what it is, greed shows you the empty place it comes from, and that seeing is where it starts to turn. Ascension is the climb that goes on past every ladder. The pressure that once wanted the top now rises through the body itself. It has long been pictured as a serpent coiled at the base of your spine, waking each part of you as it climbs. No step can be skipped. The one person who always makes trouble for you cannot be walked around; it has to pass through your heart. The wanting is never cut out. It is worn smooth, the way wind wears rocks.

The road up takes a warrior's will, and near the top you find you have become all yielding. At the end your body itself changes, in a heat like liquid fire, and then you go still. Keep reaching, and sooner or later you rise.
fields.human_design: Ambition Gate 54 sits at the base of your body and presses you to move up in life. It gives you a feel for how the ladder is built. The ladder may be work or rank, or how deep your understanding goes. It does not tell you what is fair in the climbing, so that part is yours to bring. Nothing you have now ever feels quite enough, and other people's places get measured against yours. Left to run, it overworks, treats people as steps and burns out. Lived well, it holds an idea until it is ripe instead of forcing it into shape. It wants what answers something in you, and it can be content and ambitious at once.
fields.tarot: This energy is one of six ways people look for something higher. It belongs to the Ring of Seeking. Creation Oscillation (UL 53) climbs beside it. When climbing wears you out, the others show you another way to seek. Timeless Blossom (UL 52) and Rhythm of Life (UL 58) sit still and let the energy move. Ordinary Valiance (UL 15) seeks by serving, and Nobel Spark (UL 39) cuts straight through. Three of the tarot's major cards, its Arcana, arrive through the ring and the two trigrams.
fields.body:
The tailbone is where your body keeps this energy, and the reason is the base. It is the last bone of your spine, the bottom of the column, curving forward under you. It is what is left of a tail. Five or six weeks after you were conceived you had one, and your body soon took it back. The floor of your body is anchored to it. The two chains of nerves that run down either side of your spine meet in front of it and become one. Every climb up your back starts here.

Sit upright on a hard chair, and your weight rests on the two bones either side of it, with the tailbone hanging free. Slump and lean back, and it takes the weight. It is the bottom of you, and it carries you the moment you stop holding yourself up. The wish to rise in you has a chemistry, and one substance in it is serine. Every protein in you is built from twenty pieces, and serine is one. One of its carbons goes into the letters of your DNA. It belongs to a pressure you share with five other energies. Pointed outward, that pressure is the urge to gather more. Turned inward, the same pressure becomes the urge for meaning.

That pressure seeks in six ways, and yours is the way of effort. You yoke yourself to a practice or a teacher and climb by degrees, a little finer at each step.

fields.essence: Freedom is a fullness you feel from the inside. On a good day your whole life seems to be at its height, and your feelings run as high as they go. You know the lift does not come from the money or the person who walks in, so you have nothing to chase. There is a perfection in you that nothing happening around you can touch. What you make from there comes out of plenty.
fields.glance:
Freedom is a fullness you feel from the inside. On a good day your whole life seems to be at its height, and your feelings run as high as they go. You know the lift does not come from the money or the person who walks in, so you have nothing to chase. There is a perfection in you that nothing happening around you can touch. What you make from there comes out of plenty.

Some days the feeling drops, and you want to blame something outside you for it. Let the low be yours as much as the high was. A low you do not pin on anyone passes on its own and leaves you clear.

You cannot chase freedom head on. It comes sideways, while you live an ordinary life with everything in it. When a time is at its fullest, spend it and share it rather than guard it against the end. Let yourself be as you are, and if that changes, let it. Each time you do, you grow lighter and freer.
fields.iching:
Everything in your life has come to its height at the same time. The work is done, the people are near and there is plenty. A time this full cannot last, and the counsel here is plain: do not grieve. The sun at noon begins to set, and the full moon begins to wane. Spend the bright hours giving your light to everyone around you, the way the sun shines on all. Know when you have enough, and stop there.

The danger is a screen. Pride or doubt draws a curtain around the fullness until the stars show at noon. When someone doubts you, say plainly what you mean, and the shade lifts. Meet your equals as partners, and draw able people in. Whoever shuts the door on a full house ends up alone in it.

Your eyes and your feet do the work now. Your eyes take in the whole of what you have in one look, and your feet move while the light lasts. Stand the way someone stands at the top of a good day, with open hands and the doors open. Thunder over Fire is the hexagram of a full life at its height. Fire is the clarity in you that sees the whole of what you have. Thunder is the drive in you that acts on it. The action rests on the clarity because what you do well grows out of what you see clearly. This hexagram has long been read as thunder and lightning arriving together. In one flash you see everything you have, and the thunder moves you to act on it. A storm like that is over fast, and so is a time this full. It is also read as the sun at noon, which has only one way left to go. Your fullest times are real, and they are yours to live while they last. Abundance
fields.gene_keys:
Victimisation Freedom Freedom Freedom begins with understanding, never with a method. It dawns in the whole of you that your own beliefs have held you. To leave a prison, you first have to know you are in one. Then you start to take the suffering back inside, yours first and then other people's. The drama outside runs out of fuel. You stop pushing your life where you wanted it to go, and you drift, watch and let it be. The search that was desperate becomes almost funny.

A dragonfly lives for years underwater before it climbs into the air. The water from its old life is pumped into its new wings to spread them. Your feelings are that water. When you feel them to the end, they are what lifts you. Every mood seems to come from outside you, and you can always name the cause. The high was the money, the good weather or the right person arriving. The low was the food, your partner or the news. Looking outside for the reason you feel the way you do is the commonest habit on earth. It is so common that it looks like plain noticing.

What holds you there is longing. When you are low, you long to be high. When you are high, you long to hold on to it. The hunger is for the search and never for the finding, because what you love is the hope. So you rise and fall on every swell, in love and then out of it. Your breath goes thin at the bottom and fills your chest at the top, and you call the swell freedom. At its height freedom keeps the same name and stops being yours. You stop feeling shut inside your own body, and what you feel moves freely between you and other people. The idea that a feeling belongs to someone starts to seem absurd.
